** )pquit
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdpquit

#+INDEX: pquit


\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item=)pquit=
\end{list}

\par\noindent*Command Description:*

This command is used to terminate Axiom  and return to the
operating system.
Other than by redoing all your computations or by
using the =)history )restore=
command to try to restore your working environment,
you cannot return to Axiom in the same state.

=)pquit= differs from the =)quit= in that it always asks for
confirmation that you want to terminate Axiom (the ``p'' is for
``protected'').
#+INDEX: quit
When you enter the =)pquit= command, Axiom responds
%
\begin{center}
Please enter *y* or *yes* if you really want to 
leave the interactive \\
environment and return to the operating system:
\end{center}
%
If you respond with =y= or =yes=, you will see the message
%
\begin{center}
You are now leaving the Axiom interactive environment. \\
Issue the command *axiom* to the operating system to start a new session.
\end{center}
%
and Axiom will terminate and return you to the operating
system (or the environment from which you invoked the system).
If you responded with something other than =y= or =yes=, then
the message
%
\begin{center}
You have chosen to remain in the Axiom interactive environment.
\end{center}
%
will be displayed and, indeed, Axiom would still be running.

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)fin= ,
=)history= ,
=)close= ,
=)quit= , and
=)system= .


%Original Page 585

** )quit
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdquit

#+INDEX: quit


\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item=)quit=
\item{\tt )set quit protected \vertline{} unprotected}
\end{list}

\par\noindent*Command Description:*

This command is used to terminate Axiom  and return to the
operating system.
Other than by redoing all your computations or by
using the =)history )restore=
command to try to restore your working environment,
you cannot return to Axiom in the same state.

=)quit= differs from the =)pquit= in that it asks for
#+INDEX: pquit
confirmation only if the command
#+begin_example
)set quit protected
#+end_example
has been issued.
#+INDEX: set quit protected
Otherwise, =)quit= will make Axiom terminate and return you
to the operating system (or the environment from which you invoked the
system).

The default setting is =)set quit protected= so that =)quit=
and =)pquit= behave in the same way.
If you do issue
#+begin_example
)set quit unprotected
#+end_example
we
#+INDEX: set quit unprotected
suggest that you do not (somehow) assign =)quit= to be
executed when you press, say, a function key.

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)fin= ,
=)history= ,
=)close= ,
=)pquit= , and
=)system= .


** )read
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdread

#+INDEX: read

\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item =)read= {\it \lanb{}fileName\ranb{}}
\item =)read= {\it \lanb{}fileName\ranb{}} \lanb{}
=)quiet=\ranb{} \lanb{}=)ifthere=\ranb{}
\end{list}
\par\noindent*Command Description:*

This command is used to read *.input* files into Axiom.
#+INDEX: file!input
The command
#+begin_example
)read matrix.input
#+end_example
will read the contents of the file *matrix.input* into
Axiom.
The ``.input'' file extension is optional.
See \sectionref{ugInOutIn} for more information about *.input* files.

This command remembers the previous file you edited, read or compiled.
If you do not specify a file name, the previous file will be read.

The =)ifthere= option checks to see whether the *.input* file
exists.
If it does not, the  =)read= command does nothing.
If you do not use this option and the file does not exist,
you are asked to give the name of an existing *.input* file.

The =)quiet= option suppresses output while the file is being read.

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)compile= ,
=)edit= , and
=)history= .


%Original Page 586

** )regress
#+INDEX: regress
\par\noindent*User Level Required:* development
\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item =)regress= /filename/
\item =)regress= /filename.output/
\item =)regress= //path/filename/
\item =)regress= //pathfilename.output/
\end{list}

\par\noindent*Command Description:*

#+begin_example
The regress command will run the regress function that was compiled
as part of the lisp image build process. This function expects an
input filename, possibly containing a path prefix. 

If the filename contains a period then we consider it a fully formed
filename, otherwise we append ``.output'', which is the default file
extension.

  )regress matrix
  )regress matrix.output
  )regress /path/to/file/matrix
  )regress /path/to/file/matrix.output
 
will test the contents of the file matrix.output.

The idea behind regression testing is to check that the results
we currently get match the results we used to get. In order to
do that we create input files with a special comment format that
contains the prior results. These are easy to create as all you
need to do is run the Axiom function, capture the results, and
turn them input specially formed comments using the -- comment.

A regression file caches the result of an Axiom function so we
can automate the testing process. It is a file of many tests,
each with their own output.

The regression file format uses the Axiom -- comment syntax to keep
a copy of the expected output from an Axiom command. This expected
output is compared character by character against the actual output.

The regression file is broken into numbered blocks, delimited by
a --S for the beginning and a --E for the end. The total number of
blocks is also given so missing or failed tests also raise an error.

There are 4 special kinds of -- comments in regression files:

  --S n of M        this is test n of M tests in this file
  --E n             this marks the end of test n
  --R any output    this marks the actual expected output line
  --I any output    this line is compared but ignored

A regression test file looks like:

  )set break resume
  )spool foo.output
  )set message type off
  )clear all

  --S 1 of 3
  2+3
  --R                     this is the exact Axiom output
  --R   (1)  5
  --E 1

  --S 2 of 3
  2+3
  --R                     this should fail to match
  --R   (2)  7
  --E 2

  --S 3 of 3
  2+3
  --R                     this fails to match but we
  --I   (3)  7            use --I to ignore this line
  --E 3

We can now run this file with

  )read foo.input

Note that when this file is run it will create a spool file called
"foo.output" because of the lines:
  
  )spool foo.output
  )spool

The "foo.output" file contains the console image of the result. 
It will look like:

  Starts dribbling to foo.output (2012/2/28, 12:25:7).
  )set message type off
  )clear all

  --S 1 of 3
  2+3
  
     (1)  5
  --R
  --R   (1)  5
  --E 1
  
  --S 2 of 3
  2+3
  
     (2)  5
  --R
  --R   (2)  7
  --E 2

  --S 3 of 3
  2+3
  
     (3)  5
  --R
  --I   (3)  7
  --E 3

  )spool

This "foo.output" file can now be checked using the )regress command.
 
When we run the )regress foo.output we see;

  testing foo
  passed foo  1 of 3
  MISMATCH
  expected:"   (2)  7"
       got:"   (2)  5"
  FAILED foo  2 of 2
  passed foo  3 of 3
  regression result FAILED 1 of 3 stanzas file foo

Tests either pass or fail. A passing test generates the message:

    passed foo  1 of 3

A failing test will give a reversed printout of the expected vs
actual output as well as a FAILED message, as in:

  MISMATCH
  expected:"   (2)  7"
       got:"   (2)  5"
  FAILED foo  2 of 3

The last line of output is a summary:

  regression result FAILED 1 of 3 stanzas file foo

#+end_example

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)tangle= 

** )savesystem
#+INDEX: savesystem

\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item=)savesystem /filename/=
\end{list}
\par\noindent*Command Description:*

This command will save the current Axiom session including
currently set variables into an executable file under the given
filename. For instance,

#+begin_example
   axiom
   (1) -> t1:=4
   (1) -> )savesystem foo
#+end_example
and Axiom exits. Then do
#+begin_example
   ./foo
   (1) -> t1
   4
#+end_example

** )set
# label: ugSysCmdset
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdset

#+INDEX: set


\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item =)set=
\item =)set= {\it label1 \lanb{}... labelN\ranb{}}
\item =)set= {\it label1 \lanb{}... labelN\ranb{} newValue}
\end{list}
\par\noindent*Command Description:*

The =)set= command is used to view or set system variables that
control what messages are displayed, the type of output desired, the
status of the history facility, the way Axiom user functions are
cached, and so on.
Since this collection is very large, we will not discuss them here.
Rather, we will show how the facility is used.
We urge you to explore the =)set= options to familiarize yourself
with how you can modify your Axiom working environment.
There is a HyperDoc version of this same facility available from the
main HyperDoc menu.


The =)set= command is command-driven with a menu display.
It is tree-structured.
To see all top-level nodes, issue =)set= by itself.
#+begin_example
)set
#+end_example
Variables with values have them displayed near the right margin.
Subtrees of selections have ``=...=''
displayed in the value field.
For example, there are many kinds of messages, so issue
=)set message= to see the choices.
#+begin_example
)set message
#+end_example
The current setting  for the variable that displays
#+INDEX: computation timings!displaying
whether computation times
#+INDEX: timings!displaying
are displayed is visible in the menu displayed by the last command.
To see more information, issue
#+begin_example
)set message time
#+end_example
This shows that time printing is on now.
To turn it off, issue
#+begin_example
)set message time off
#+end_example
#+INDEX: set message time

As noted above, not all settings have so many qualifiers.
For example, to change the =)quit= command to being unprotected
(that is, you will not be prompted for verification), you need only issue
#+begin_example
)set quit unprotected
#+end_example
#+INDEX: set quit unprotected

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)quit= .


** )show
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdshow

#+INDEX: show


\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item =)show /nameOrAbbrev/=
\item =)show /nameOrAbbrev/ )operations=
\item =)show /nameOrAbbrev/ )attributes=
\end{list}

\par\noindent*Command Description:*
This command displays information about Axiom
domain, package and category /constructors/.
If no options are given, the =)operations= option is assumed.

%Original Page 587

For example,
#+begin_example
)show POLY
)show POLY )operations
)show Polynomial
)show Polynomial )operations
#+end_example
each display basic information about the
=Polynomial= domain constructor and then provide a
listing of operations.
Since =Polynomial= requires a =Ring= (for example,
=Integer=) as argument, the above commands all refer
to a unspecified ring =R=.
In the list of operations, =\$= means
=Polynomial(R)=.

The basic information displayed includes the /signature/
of the constructor (the name and arguments), the constructor
/abbreviation/, the /exposure status/ of the constructor, and the
name of the /library source file/ for the constructor.

If operation information about a specific domain is wanted,
the full or abbreviated domain name may be used.
For example,
#+begin_example
)show POLY INT
)show POLY INT )operations
)show Polynomial Integer
)show Polynomial Integer )operations
#+end_example
are among  the combinations that will display the operations\\ 
exported  by the domain =Polynomial(Integer)= (as opposed\\ 
to the general /domain constructor/ =Polynomial=).\\
Attributes may be listed by using the =)attributes= option.

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)display= ,
=)set= , and
=)what= .


** )spool
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdspool

#+INDEX: spool


\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item=)spool= \lanb{}/fileName/\ranb{}
\item=)spool=
\end{list}

\par\noindent*Command Description:*

This command is used to save /(spool)/ all Axiom input and output
#+INDEX: file!spool
into a file, called a /spool file./
You can only have one spool file active at a time.
To start spool, issue this command with a filename. For example,
#+begin_example
)spool integrate.out
#+end_example
To stop spooling, issue =)spool= with no filename.

If the filename is qualified with a directory, then the output will
be placed in that directory.
If no directory information is given, the spool file will be placed in the
#+INDEX: directory!for spool files
/current directory./
The current directory is the directory from which you started
Axiom or is the directory you specified using the
=)cd= command.
#+INDEX: cd

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)cd= .


** )summary
#+INDEX: summary

\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item=)summary=
\end{list}
\par\noindent*Command Description:*

#+begin_example
 )credits      : list the people who have contributed to Axiom

 )help <command> gives more information
 )quit         : exit AXIOM 

 )abbreviation : query, set and remove abbreviations for constructors
 )browse       : start an Axiom http server on 127.0.0.1 port 8085
 )cd           : set working directory
 )clear        : remove declarations, definitions or values
 )close        : throw away an interpreter client and workspace
 )compile      : invoke constructor compiler
 )copyright    : show copyright and trademark information
 )describe     : show database information for a category, domain, or package 
 )display      : display Library operations and objects in your workspace
 )edit         : edit a file
 )fin          : drop into lisp, use (restart) to return to the session
 )frame        : manage interpreter workspaces
 )history      : manage aspects of interactive session
 )include      : insert a file into a .input file
 )library      : introduce new constructors 
 )lisp         : evaluate a LISP expression
 )ltrace       : trace functions
 )pquit        : ask if you really want to exit Axiom
 )quit         : exit Axiom
 )read         : execute AXIOM commands from a file
 )regress      : regression test an output spool file
 )savesystem   : save LISP image to a file
 )set          : view and set system variables
 )show         : show constructor information
 )spool        : log input and output to a file
 )synonym      : define an abbreviation for system commands
 )system       : issue shell commands
 )tangle       : extract chunks from a literate program to an input file
 )trace        : trace execution of functions
 )undo         : restore workspace to earlier state
 )what         : search for various things by name
#+end_example

** )synonym
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdsynonym

#+INDEX: synonym


\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item=)synonym=
\item=)synonym= /synonym fullCommand/
\item=)what synonyms=
\end{list}

%Original Page 588

\par\noindent*Command Description:*

This command is used to create short synonyms for system command expressions.
For example, the following synonyms  might simplify commands you often
use.
#+begin_example
)synonym save         history )save
)synonym restore      history )restore
)synonym mail         system mail
)synonym ls           system ls
)synonym fortran      set output fortran
#+end_example
Once defined, synonyms can be
used in place of the longer  command expressions.
Thus
#+begin_example
)fortran on
#+end_example
is the same as the longer
#+begin_example
)set fortran output on
#+end_example
To list all defined synonyms, issue either of
#+begin_example
)synonyms
)what synonyms
#+end_example
To list, say, all synonyms that contain the substring
``=ap='', issue
#+begin_example
)what synonyms ap
#+end_example

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)set=  and
=)what= .


** )system
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdsystem

#+INDEX: system

\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item=)system= /cmdExpression/
\end{list}

\par\noindent*Command Description:*

This command may be used to issue commands to the operating system while
remaining in Axiom.
The /cmdExpression/ is passed to the operating system for
execution.

To get an operating system shell, issue, for example,
=)system sh=.
When you enter the key combination,
\fbox*Ctrl*--\fbox*D*
(pressing and holding the
\fbox*Ctrl* key and then pressing the
\fbox*D* key)
the shell will terminate and you will return to Axiom.
We do not recommend this way of creating a shell because
Common Lisp may field some interrupts instead of the shell.
If possible, use a shell running in another window.

If you execute programs that misbehave you may not be able to return to
Axiom.
If this happens, you may have no other choice than to restart
Axiom and restore the environment via =)history )restore=, if
possible.

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)boot= ,
=)fin= ,
=)lisp= ,
=)pquit= , and
=)quit= .

** )trace
# label: ugSysCmdtrace
# label: ugSysCmdltrace
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdltrace

#+INDEX: ltrace


\par\noindent*User Level Required:* development

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*

This command has the same arguments as options as the
=)trace= command.

\par\noindent*Command Description:*

This command is used by Axiom system developers to trace

BOOT functions.
It is not supported for general use.

\par\noindent*Also See:*

** )trace
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdtrace

#+INDEX: trace


\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item=)trace=
\item=)trace )off=

\item=)trace= {\it function \lanb{}options\ranb{}}
\item=)trace= {\it constructor \lanb{}options\ranb{}}
\item=)trace= {\it domainOrPackage \lanb{}options\ranb{}}
\end{list}
%
where options can be one or more of
%
\begin{list}{}
\item=)after= /S-expression/
\item=)before= /S-expression/
\item=)break after=
\item=)break before=
\item=)cond= /S-expression/
\item=)count=
\item=)count= /n/
\item=)depth= /n/
\item=)local= {\it op1 \lanb{}... opN\ranb{}}
\item=)nonquietly=
\item=)nt=
\item=)off=
\item=)only= /listOfDataToDisplay/
\item=)ops=
\item=)ops= {\it op1 \lanb{}... opN \ranb{}}
\item=)restore=
\item=)stats=
\item=)stats reset=
\item=)timer=
\item=)varbreak=
\item=)varbreak= {\it var1 \lanb{}... varN \ranb{}}
\item=)vars=
\item=)vars= {\it var1 \lanb{}... varN \ranb{}}
\item=)within= /executingFunction/
\end{list}

\par\noindent*Command Description:*

This command is used to trace the execution of functions that make
up the Axiom system, functions defined by users,
and functions from the system library.
Almost all options are available for each type of function but
exceptions will be noted below.

To list all functions, constructors, domains and packages that are
traced, simply issue
#+begin_example
)trace
#+end_example
To untrace everything that is traced, issue
#+begin_example
)trace )off
#+end_example
When a function is traced, the default system action is to display
the arguments to the function and the return value when the
function is exited.
Note that if a function is left via an action such as a =THROW=, no
return value will be displayed.
Also, optimization of tail recursion may decrease the number of
times a function is actually invoked and so may cause less trace
information to be displayed.

%Original Page 590

Other information can be displayed or collected when a function is
traced and this is controlled by the various options.
Most options will be of interest only to Axiom system
developers.
If a domain or package is traced, the default action is to trace
all functions exported.

Individual interpreter, lisp or boot
functions can be traced by listing their names after
=)trace=.
Any options that are present must follow the functions to be
traced.
#+begin_example
)trace f
#+end_example
traces the function =f=.
To untrace =f=, issue
#+begin_example
)trace f )off
#+end_example
Note that if a function name contains a special character, it will
be necessary to escape the character with an underscore
%
#+begin_example
)trace _/D_,1
#+end_example
%
To trace all domains or packages that are or will be created from a particular
constructor, give the constructor name or abbreviation after
=)trace=.
%
#+begin_example
)trace MATRIX
)trace List Integer
#+end_example
%
The first command traces all domains currently instantiated with
=Matrix=.
If additional domains are instantiated with this constructor
(for example, if you have used =Matrix(Integer)= and
=Matrix(Float)=), they will be automatically traced.
The second command traces =List(Integer)=.
It is possible to trace individual functions in a domain or
package.
See the =)ops= option below.

The following are the general options for the =)trace=
command.

%!! system command parser doesn't treat general s-expressions correctly,
%!! I recommand not documenting )after )before and )cond
\begin{description}
%\item[=)after= /S-expression/]
%causes the given Common Lisp /S-expression/ to be
%executed after exiting the traced function.

%\item[=)before= /S-expression/]
%causes the given Common Lisp /S-expression/ to be
%executed before entering the traced function.

\item[=)break after=]
causes a Common Lisp break loop to be entered after
exiting the traced function.

\item[=)break before=]
causes a Common Lisp break loop to be entered before
entering the traced function.

\item[=)break=]
is the same as =)break before=.

%\item[=)cond= /S-expression/]
%causes trace information to be shown only if the given
%Common Lisp /S-expression/ evaluates to non-NIL.  For
%example, the following command causes the system function
%=resolveTT= to be traced but to have the information
%displayed only if the value of the variable
%=\$reportBottomUpFlag= is non-NIL.
%\begin{verbatim}
%)trace resolveTT )cond \_\$reportBottomUpFlag}
%\end{verbatim}

\item[=)count=]
causes the system to keep a count of the number of times the
traced function is entered.  The total can be displayed with
=)trace )stats= and cleared with =)trace )stats reset=.

\item[=)count= /n/]
causes information about the traced function to be displayed for
the first /n/ executions.  After the /n-th/ execution, the
function is untraced.

\item[=)depth= /n/]
causes trace information to be shown for only /n/ levels of
recursion of the traced function.  The command
#+begin_example
)trace fib )depth 10
#+end_example
will cause the display of only 10 levels of trace information for
the recursive execution of a user function *fib*.

\item[=)math=]
causes the function arguments and return value to be displayed\\ 
in the Axiom monospace two-dimensional math format.

\item[=)nonquietly=]
causes the display of additional messages when a function is
traced.

\item[=)nt=]
This suppresses all normal trace information.  This option is
useful if the =)count= or =)timer= options are used and
you are interested in the statistics but not the function calling
information.

%Original Page 591

\item[=)off=]
causes untracing of all or specific functions.  Without an
argument, all functions, constructors, domains and packages are
untraced.  Otherwise, the given functions and other objects
are untraced.  To
immediately retrace the untraced functions, issue {\tt )trace
)restore}.

\item[=)only= /listOfDataToDisplay/]
causes only specific trace information to be shown.  The items are
listed by using the following abbreviations:
\begin{description}
\item[a]        display all arguments
\item[v]        display return value
\item[1]        display first argument
\item[2]        display second argument
\item[15]       display the 15th argument, and so on
\end{description}
\end{description}
\begin{description}

\item[=)restore=]
causes the last untraced functions to be retraced.  If additional
options are present, they are added to those previously in effect.

\item[=)stats=]
causes the display of statistics collected by the use of the
=)count= and =)timer= options.

\item[=)stats reset=]
resets to 0 the statistics collected by the use of the
=)count= and =)timer= options.

\item[=)timer=]
causes the system to keep a count of execution times for the
traced function.  The total can be displayed with {\tt )trace
)stats} and cleared with =)trace )stats reset=.

%!! only for lisp, boot, may not work in any case, recommend removing
%\item[=)varbreak=]
%causes a Common Lisp break loop to be entered after
%the assignment to any variable in the traced function.

\item[=)varbreak= {\it var1 \lanb{}... varN\ranb{}}]
causes a Common Lisp break loop to be entered after
the assignment to any of the listed variables in the traced
function.

\item[=)vars=] causes the display of the value of any variable
after it is assigned in the traced function.  Note that library code
must have been compiled (see \sectionref{ugSysCmdcompile} using the
=)vartrace= option in order to support this option.

\item[=)vars= {\it var1 \lanb{}... varN\ranb{}}] causes the
display of the value of any of the specified variables after they are
assigned in the traced function.  Note that library code must have
been compiled (see \sectionref{ugSysCmdcompile} using the {\tt
)vartrace} option in order to support this option.

\item[=)within= /executingFunction/]
causes the display of trace information only if the traced
function is called when the given /executingFunction/ is running.
\end{description}

The following are the options for tracing constructors, domains
and packages.

\begin{description}
\item[=)local= {\it \lanb{}op1 \lanb{}... opN\ranb{}\ranb{}}]
causes local functions of the constructor to be traced.  Note that
to untrace an individual local function, you must use the fully
qualified internal name, using the escape character
=\_= before the semicolon.
#+begin_example
)trace FRAC )local
)trace FRAC_;cancelGcd )off
#+end_example

\item[=)ops= {\it op1 \lanb{}... opN\ranb{}}]
By default, all operations from a domain or package are traced
when the domain or package is traced.  This option allows you to
specify that only particular operations should be traced.  The
command
%
#+begin_example
)trace Integer )ops min max _+ _-
#+end_example
%
traces four operations from the domain =Integer=.  Since
=+= and =-= are special
characters, it is necessary
to escape them with an underscore.
\end{description}

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)boot= ,
=)lisp= , and
=)ltrace= .

%Original Page 592

** )undo
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdundo

#+INDEX: undo


\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item=)undo=
\item=)undo= /integer/
\item=)undo= {\it integer \lanb{}option\ranb{}}
\item=)undo= =)redo=
\end{list}
%
where /option/ is one of
%
\begin{list}{}
\item=)after=
\item=)before=
\end{list}

\par\noindent*Command Description:*

This command is used to
restore the state of the user environment to an earlier
point in the interactive session.
The argument of an =)undo= is an integer which must designate some
step number in the interactive session.

#+begin_example
)undo n
)undo n )after
#+end_example
These commands return the state of the interactive
environment to that immediately after step =n=.
If =n= is a positive number, then =n= refers to step nummber
=n=. If =n= is a negative number, it refers to the =n=-th
previous command (that is, undoes the effects of the last $-n$
commands).

A =)clear all= resets the =)undo= facility.
Otherwise, an =)undo= undoes the effect of =)clear= with
options =properties=, =value=, and =mode=, and
that of a previous =undo=.
If any such system commands are given between steps $n$ and
$n + 1$ ($n > 0$), their effect is undone
for =)undo m= for any $0 < m \leq n$..

The command =)undo= is equivalent to =)undo -1= (it undoes
the effect of the previous user expression).
The command =)undo 0= undoes any of the above system commands
issued since the last user expression.

#+begin_example
)undo n )before
#+end_example
This command returns the state of the interactive
environment to that immediately before step =n=.
Any =)undo= or =)clear= system commands
given before step =n= will not be undone.

#+begin_example
)undo )redo
#+end_example
This command reads the file =redo.input=.
created by the last =)undo= command.
This file consists of all user input lines, excluding those
backtracked over due to a previous =)undo=.

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)history= .
The command =)history )write= will eliminate the ``undone'' command
lines of your program.

** )what
#+INDEX: ugSysCmdwhat
# label: ugSysCmdwhat

#+INDEX: what


\par\noindent*User Level Required:* interpreter

%Original Page 593

\par\noindent*Command Syntax:*
\begin{list}{}
\item=)what categories= /pattern1/ \lanb{}{\it pattern2 ...\ranb{}}
\item=)what commands= /pattern1/ \lanb{}{\it pattern2 ...\ranb{}}
\item=)what domains= /pattern1/ \lanb{}{\it pattern2 ...\ranb{}}
\item=)what operations= /pattern1/ \lanb{}{\it pattern2 ...\ranb{}}
\item=)what packages= /pattern1/ \lanb{}{\it pattern2 ...\ranb{}}
\item=)what synonym= /pattern1/ \lanb{}{\it pattern2 ...\ranb{}}
\item=)what things= /pattern1/ \lanb{}{\it pattern2 ...\ranb{}}
\item=)apropos= /pattern1/ \lanb{}{\it pattern2 ...\ranb{}}
\end{list}

\par\noindent*Command Description:*

This command is used to display lists of things in the system.  The
patterns are all strings and, if present, restrict the contents of the
lists.  Only those items that contain one or more of the strings as
substrings are displayed.  For example,
#+begin_example
)what synonym
#+end_example
displays all command synonyms,
#+begin_example
)what synonym ver
#+end_example
displays all command synonyms containing the substring ``=ver='',
#+begin_example
)what synonym ver pr
#+end_example
displays all command synonyms
containing the substring  ``=ver='' or  the substring
``=pr=''.
Output similar to the following will be displayed
#+begin_example
---------------- System Command Synonyms -----------------

user-defined synonyms satisfying patterns:
      ver pr

  )apr ........................... )what things
  )apropos ....................... )what things
  )prompt ........................ )set message prompt
  )version ....................... )lisp *yearweek*
#+end_example

Several other things can be listed with the =)what= command:

\begin{description}
\item[=categories=] displays a list of category constructors.
#+INDEX: what categories
\item[=commands=]  displays a list of  system commands available  at your
user-level.
#+INDEX: what commands
Your user-level
#+INDEX: user-level
is set via the  =)set userlevel= command.
#+INDEX: set userlevel
To get a description of a particular command, such as ``=)what='', issue
=)help what=.
\item[=domains=]   displays a list of domain constructors.
#+INDEX: what domains
\item[=operations=] displays a list of operations in  the system library.
#+INDEX: what operations
It  is recommended that you  qualify this command with one or
more patterns, as there are thousands of operations available.  For
example, say you are looking for functions that involve computation of
eigenvalues.  To find their names, try =)what operations eig=.
A rather large list of operations  is loaded into the workspace when
this command  is first issued.  This  list will be deleted  when you
clear the workspace  via =)clear all= or =)clear completely=.
It will be re-created if it is needed again.
\item[=packages=]  displays a list of package constructors.
#+INDEX: what packages
\item[=synonym=]  lists system command synonyms.
#+INDEX: what synonym
\item[=things=]    displays all  of the  above types for  items containing
#+INDEX: what things
the pattern strings as  substrings.
The command synonym  =)apropos= is equivalent to
#+INDEX: apropos
=)what things=.
\end{description}

\par\noindent*Also See:*
=)display= ,
=)set= , and
=)show= .

%Original Page 601

\setcounter{chapter}{3} % Appendix C
* Domains
# label: ugAppDomains

This is a listing of all domains in the Axiom library at the
time this book was produced.
Use the Browse facility (described in \sectionref{ugBrowse})
to get more information about these constructors.

\boxer{4.6in}{
This sample entry will help you read the following table:

DomainName{DomainAbbreviation}:{$\hbox{{\sf Category}}_{1}$%
...$\hbox{{\sf Category}}_{N}$}/with/%
{$\hbox{op}_{1}$...$\hbox{op}_{M}$}

where

| DomainName | is the full domain name, e.g., {\sf Integer}. |
| DomainAbbreviation | is the domain abbreviation, e.g., {\sf INT}. |
| $\hbox{{\sf Category}}_{i}$ | is a category to which the domain belongs. |
| $\hbox{op}_{j}$ | is an operation exported by the domain. |

}

\setcounter{chapter}{4} % Appendix D
* Packages
# label: ugAppPackages

This is a listing of all packages in the Axiom library at the
time this book was produced.
Use the Browse facility (described in \sectionref{ugBrowse})
to get more information about these constructors.

\boxer{5.0in}{
This sample entry will help you read the following table:

PackageName{PackageAbbreviation}:{$\hbox{{\sf Category}}_{1}$%
...$\hbox{{\sf Category}}_{N}$}/with/%
{$\hbox{op}_{1}$...$\hbox{op}_{M}$}

where

| PackageName | is the full package name, e.g., {\sf PadeApproximantPackage}. |
| PackageAbbreviation | is the package abbreviation, e.g., {\sf PADEPAC}. |
| $\hbox{{\sf Category}}_{i}$ | is a category to which the package belongs. |
| $\hbox{op}_{j}$ | is an operation exported by the package. |

}

\keydata{\keyop{#}aggregate}{1}{(\$)->NonNegativeInteger}{Aggregate}
   {$# a$ returns the number of items in \smath{a}.
}

\keydata{x\keyop{**}y}{2}{(\$, \$)->\$}{ElementaryFunctionCategory}
   {$x**y$ returns \smath{x} to the power \smath{y}.
Also, this operation returns, if $x$ is:
\begin{simpleList}
\item an equation: a new equation by raising both sides of 
$x$ to the power \smath{y}.
\item a float or small float: 
$\mbox*sign*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}}
$\mbox*exp*\opLeftPren{$y \log(|x|)\opRightPren{}}.
\end{simpleList}
See also \axiomType{InputForm} and \axiomType{OutputForm}.
}

\keydata{x\keyop{*}y}{2}{(Integer, \$)->\$}{AbelianGroup}
  {\opkey{The binary operator $*$ denotes multiplication.
Its meaning depends on the type of its arguments:}
\begin{simpleList}
\item if $x$ and \smath{y} are members of a ring (more generally, 
a domain of
category \axiomType{SemiGroup}), $x*y$ returns the product of 
$x$ and \smath{y}.
\item if $r$ is an integer and \smath{x} is an element of a ring, or
if $r$ is a scalar and \smath{x} is a vector, matrix, or direct product:
$r*x$ returns the left multiplication of \smath{r} by \smath{x}.
More generally, if $r$ is an integer and \smath{x} is a
member of a domain of category \axiomType{AbelianMonoid},
or $r$ is a member of domain \smath{R} and \smath{x} is a 
domain of category
\axiomType{Module(R)}, \axiomType{GradedModule}, or \axiomType{GradedAlgebra}
defined over $R$,
$r*x$ returns the left multiplication of \smath{r} by \smath{x}.
Here $x$ can be a vector, a matrix, or a direct product.
Similarly, $x*n$ returns the right integer multiple of \smath{x}.
\item if $a$ and \smath{b} are monad elements,
the product of $a$ and \smath{b} (see \axiomType{Monad}).
\item if $A$ and \smath{B} are matrices,
returns the product of $A$ and \smath{B}.
If $v$ is a row vector, \smath{v*A}
returns the product of $v$ and \smath{A}.
If $v$ is column vector, \smath{A*v}
returns the product of $A$ with column vector \smath{v}.
In each case, the operation calls \spadfun{error}
if the dimensions are incompatible.
\item if $s$ is an integer or float and \smath{c} is a color, 
$s*c$ returns
the weighted shade scaled by $s$.
\item if $s$ and \smath{t} are Cartesian tensors,
$s*t$ is the inner product of the tensors \smath{s} and \smath{t}.
This contracts the last index of $s$ with the first index of \smath{t},
that is,
$t*s = \mbox=contract=(t, \mbox=rank= t, s, 1)$,
$t*s = \sum\nolimits_{k=1$^N{t([i_1, .., i_N, k]*s[k, j_1, .., j_M])}}.
\item if $eq$ is an equation, \smath{r*eq}
multiplies both sides of $eq$ by r.
\item if $I$ and \smath{J} are ideals, the product of ideals.
\item See also \axiomType{OutputForm}, \axiomType{Monad},
\axiomType{LeftModule},
\axiomType{RightModule}, and
\axiomType{FreeAbelianMonoidCategory},
\end{simpleList}
See also \axiomType{InputForm} and \axiomType{OutputForm}.
}

\keydata{x\keyop{+}y}{2}{(Integer, \$)->\$}{AbelianGroup}
  {\opkey{The binary operator $+$ denotes addition.
Its meaning depends on the type of its arguments.
If $x$ and \smath{y} are:}
\begin{simpleList}
\item members of a ring (more generally,
of a domain of category \axiomType{AbelianSemiGroup}):
the sum of $x$ and \smath{y}.
\item matrices:
the matrix sum if $x$ and \smath{y} have the same dimensions,
and \spadfun{error} otherwise.
\item vectors: the component-wise sum if $x$ and \smath{y} have
the same length, and \spadfun{error} otherwise.
\item colors:  a color which additively mixes colors $x$ and \smath{y}.
\item equations: an equation created by adding the respective 
left- and right-hand
sides of $x$ and \smath{y}.
\item elements of graded module or algebra:
the sum of $x$ and \smath{y} in the module of elements
of the same degree as $x$ and \smath{y}.
\item ideals: the ideal generated by the union of $x$ and \smath{y}.
\end{simpleList}
See also \axiomType{FreeAbelianMonoidCategory},
\axiomType{InputForm} and \axiomType{OutputForm}.
}

\keydata{\optinit{x}\keyop{-}y}{1}{(\$)->\$}{AbelianGroup}
  {$- x$ returns the negative (additive inverse) of \smath{x},
where $x$ is a member of a ring
(more generally, a domain of category \axiomType{AbelianGroup}).
Also, $x$ may be a matrix, a vector, or a member of a graded module.
  \newitem
  $x - y$ returns \smath{x + (-y)}.
  \newitem
See also \axiomType{CancellationAbelianMonoid} and \axiomType{OutputForm}.
}

\keydata{x\keyop{/}y}{2}{(\$, \$)->\$}{Group}
{\opkey{The binary operator $/$ generally denotes binary
division.
Its precise meaning, however, depends on the type of its arguments:}
\begin{simpleList}
\item $x$ and \smath{y} are elements of a group: multiplies 
$x$ by the inverse 
$\mbox*inv*\opLeftPren{$y\opRightPren{}} of \smath{y}.
\item $x$ and \smath{y} are elements of a field: divides 
$x$ by \smath{y}, calling
\spadfun{error} if $y=0$.
\item $x$ is a matrix or a vector and \smath{y} is a scalar: 
divides each element of $x$ by \smath{y}.
\item $x$ and \smath{y} are floats or small floats: divides 
$x$ by \smath{y}.
\item $x$ and \smath{y} are fractions: returns the quotient 
as another fraction.
\item $x$ and \smath{y} are polynomials: returns the quotient
as a fraction of polynomials.
\end{simpleList}
See also \axiomType{AbelianMonoidRing}, \axiomType{InputForm} and 
\axiomType{OutputForm}.
}

\keydata{\keyop{0}}{0}{()->\$}{AbelianMonoid}{The additive
identity element for a ring (more generally, for an
\axiomType{AbelianMonoid}).
Also, for a graded module or algebra, the zero of degree 0 (see
\axiomType{GradedModule}).
See also \axiomType{InputForm}.
}

\keydata{\keyop{1}}{0}{()->\$}{GradedAlgebra}
{The multiplicative identity element for a ring
(more generally, for a \axiomType{Monoid} and \axiomType{MonadWithUnit}).
or a graded algebra.
See also \axiomType{InputForm}.
}

\keydata{x\keyop{<}y}{2}{(\$, \$)->Boolean}{OrderedSet}
  {\opkey{The binary operator $<$ denotes the boolean-valued
``less than'' function.
Its meaning depends on the type of its arguments.
The operation $x < y$ for \smath{x} and \smath{y}:}
\begin{simpleList}
\item elements of a totally ordered set (such as integer and 
floating point numbers):
tests if $x$ is less than y.
\item sets: tests if all the elements of $x$ are also elements of y.
\item permutations: tests if $x$ is less than \smath{y};
see \axiomType{Permutation} for details.
Note: this order relation is total if and only
if the underlying domain is of category \axiomType{Finite} or 
\axiomType{OrderedSet}.
\item permutation groups: tests if $x$ is a proper subgroup of y.
\item See also \axiomType{OutputForm}.
\end{simpleList}
}

\keydata{x\keyop{=}y}{2}{(S, S)->\$}{Equation}
  {\opkey{The meaning of binary operator $x = y$
depends on the value expected of the operation.
If the value is expected to be:}
\begin{simpleList}
\item a boolean: $x = y$ tests that \smath{x} and \smath{y} are equal.
\item an equation: $x = y$ creates an equation.
\item See also \axiomType{OutputForm}.
\end{simpleList}
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{alternating}}\opLeftPren{}/integer/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{ I -> SPOL RN}{}{}
  {$\mbox*alternating*\opLeftPren{$n\opRightPren{}} 
is the cycle index of the
   alternating group of degree $n$.
See \axiomType{CycleIndicators} for details.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{alternatingGroup}}\opLeftPren{}
/listOfIntegers/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(Integer))->PermutationGroup(Integer)}{PermutationGroupExamples}
{$\mbox*alternatingGroup*\opLeftPren{$li\opRightPren{}} 
constructs the alternating group
acting on the integers in the list $li$.
If $n$ is odd, the generators are in general the
$(n-2)$-cycle \smath{(li.3, ..., li.n)} and the
3-cycle $(li.1, li.2, li.3)$.
If $n$ is even, the generators are the product of the 2-cycle
$(li.1, li.2)$ with \smath{(n-2)}-cycle
$(li.3, ..., li.n)$ and the 3-cycle \smath{(li.1, li.2, li.3)}.
Duplicates in the list will be removed.
\newitem$\mbox*alternatingGroup*\opLeftPren{$n\opRightPren{}} 
constructs the alternating
group $A_n$ acting on the integers $1, ..., n$.
If $n$ is odd, the generators are in general the
$(n-2)$-cycle \smath{(3, ..., n)} and the 3-cycle \smath{(1, 2, 3)}.
If $n$ is even, the generators are the product of the 2-cycle
$(1, 2)$ with \smath{(n-2)}-cycle \smath{(3, ..., n)} and the 3-cycle
$(1, 2, 3)$ if \smath{n} is even.
}

}%
}%
{0}{()->Boolean}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{$\mbox*alternative?*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
tests if $2 \mbox*associator*(a, a, b) = 0 =
2 \mbox*associator*(a, b, b)$ for all $a$, \smath{b} in the algebra
$F$.
Note: in general,
$2 a=0$ does not necessarily imply \smath{a=0}.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{areEquivalent?}}\opLeftPren{}/listOfMatrices/,
{}/listOfMatrices/ $\,[$ , {}
/randomElements?/, {}/numberOfTries/$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{4}{(List(Matrix(R)), List(Matrix(R)), Boolean, Integer)->
Matrix(R)}{RepresentationPackage2}
{$\mbox*areEquivalent?*\opLeftPren{$lM, 
{} lM', {} b, {} numberOfTries\opRightPren{}} tests whether the
two lists of matrices, assumed of the same square shape, can be
simultaneously conjugated by a non-singular matrix.
If these matrices represent the same group generators, the
representations are equivalent.
The algorithm tries $numberOfTries$ times to create elements
in the generated algebras in the same fashion.
For details, consult HyperDoc.
  \newitem
  $\mbox*areEquivalent?*\opLeftPren{$aG0, 
{} aG1, {} numberOfTries\opRightPren{}} calls 
$\mbox*areEquivalent?*\opLeftPren{$aG0, {} aG1, 
{} true, {} 25\opRightPren{}}.
  \newitem
  $\mbox*areEquivalent?*\opLeftPren{$aG0, 
{} aG1\opRightPren{}} calls 
$\mbox*areEquivalent?*\opLeftPren{$aG0, 
{} aG1, {} true, {} 25\opRightPren{}}.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{antisymmetric?}}\opLeftPren{}
/matrix/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Boolean}{MatrixCategory}
{$\mbox*antisymmetric?*\opLeftPren{$m\opRightPren{}} 
tests if the matrix $m$ is square
and antisymmetric, that is, $m_{i, j$ = -m_{j, i}} for all

}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{antisymmetricTensors}}\opLeftPren{}
/matrices/, {}/positiveInteger/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(List(Matrix(R)), PositiveInteger)->List(Matrix(R))}
{RepresentationPackage1}
  {$\mbox*antisymmetricTensors*\opLeftPren{$A, 
{} n\opRightPren{}},
where $A$ is an \smath{m} by \smath{m} matrix,
returns a matrix obtained by applying to $A$
the irreducible, polynomial representation of the
general linear group $GL_m$ corresponding to the
partition $(1, 1, ..., 1, 0, 0, ..., 0)$ of \smath{n}.
A call to \spadfun{error} occurs if $n$ is greater than \smath{m}.
Note: this corresponds to the symmetrization of the representation
with the sign
representation of the symmetric group $S_n$.
The carrier spaces of the representation are the antisymmetric
tensors of the $n$-fold tensor product.
  \newitem$\mbox*antisymmetricTensors*\opLeftPren{$lA, 
{} n\opRightPren{}},
where $lA$ is a list of \smath{m} by \smath{m} matrices,
similarly applies the representation of $GL_m$ to each matrix \smath{A}
of $lA$, returning a list of matrices.
}

}%
{0}{()->List(A)}{AlgebraPackage}

basis of the space of all

a) = 0} and
$\mbox*associator*\opLeftPren{$x, {} a, {} b
\opRightPren{}} = $\mbox*associator*\opLeftPren{$a, {} x, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} = $\mbox*associator*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b, {} x\opRightPren{}} =
0 for all $a$, \smath{b} in \smath{R}.
Domain $R$ is a domain of category
\axiomType{FramedNonAssociativeAlgebra}.
}

}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{basisOfLeftAnnihilator}}\opLeftPren{}
/element/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{basisOfRightAnnihilator}}\opLeftPren{}
/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(A)->List(A)}{AlgebraPackage}
{\opkey{These operations return a basis of the space of all
$x$ in \smath{R} of category
\axiomType{FramedNonAssociativeAlgebra}, satisfying}
\begin{simpleList}
\item$\mbox*basisOfLeftAnnihilator*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}}:
 $0 = xa$.
\item$\mbox*basisOfRightAnnihilator*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}}:
  $0 = ax$.
\end{simpleList}
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{basisOfNucleus}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
 \optand \mbox{\axiomFun{basisOfLeftNucleus}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
 \optand \mbox{\axiomFun{basisOfMiddleNucleus}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{basisOfRightNucleus}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->List(A)}{AlgebraPackage}
{\opkey{Each operation returns a basis of the space of all
$x$ of \smath{R}, a domain of category
\axiomType{FramedNonAssociativeAlgebra}, satisfying for all
$a$ and \smath{b}:}
\begin{simpleList}
\item $\mbox*basisOfNucleus*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R}:
$\mbox*associator*\opLeftPren{$x, {} a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} = $\mbox*associator*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} x, {} b\opRightPren{}}
= $\mbox*associator*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b, 
{} x\opRightPren{}} = 0;
\item $\mbox*basisOfLeftNucleus*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R}:  
$\mbox*associator*\opLeftPren{$x, {} a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} = 0;
\item $\mbox*basisOfMiddleNucleus*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R}: 
$\mbox*associator*\opLeftPren{$a, {} x, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} = 0;
\item $\mbox*basisOfRightNucleus*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R}:  
$\mbox*associator*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b, {} x\opRightPren{}} = 0.
\end{simpleList}
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{basisOfLeftNucloid}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{basisOfRightNucloid}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->List(Matrix(R))}{AlgebraPackage}
{\opkey{Each operation returns a basis of the space of
endomorphisms of $R$, a domain of category
\axiomType{FramedNonAssociativeAlgebra}, considered as:}
\begin{simpleList}
  \item$\mbox*basisOfLeftNucloid*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}}: 
a right module.
  \item$\mbox*basisOfRightNucloid*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}}: 
a left module.
\end{simpleList}
Note: if $R$ has a unit, the left and right nucloid coincide with
the left and right nucleus.
}

{1}{(Integer)->Fraction(Integer)}{IntegerNumberTheoryFunctions}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{besselI}}\opLeftPren{}/complexDoubleFloat/,
{}/complexDoubleFloat/\opRightPren{}%
\optand \mbox{\axiomFun{besselJ}}\opLeftPren{}/complexDoubleFloat/, 
{}/complexDoubleFloat/\opRightPren{}%
\optand \mbox{\axiomFun{besselK}}\opLeftPren{}/complexDoubleFloat/, 
{}/complexDoubleFloat/\opRightPren{}%
\opand \mbox{\axiomFun{besselY}}\opLeftPren{}/complexDoubleFloat/, 
{}/complexDoubleFloat/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(Complex(DoubleFloat), 
Complex(DoubleFloat))->Complex(DoubleFloat)}{DoubleFloatSpecialFunctions}
{$\mbox*besselI*\opLeftPren{$v, 
{} x\opRightPren{}} is the modified Bessel function of the first
kind, $I(v, x)$, satisfying the differential equation
$x^2 {w''(x)$ + x w'(x) - (x^2+v^2)w(x) = 0}.
\bigitem$\mbox*besselJ*\opLeftPren{$v, 
{} x\opRightPren{}} is the Bessel function of the second
kind, $J(v, x)$,
satisfying the differential equation $x^2 {w''(x)$ + x w'(x)
+ (x^2-v^2)w(x) = 0}.
\bigitem$\mbox*besselK*\opLeftPren{$v, 
{} x\opRightPren{}} is the modified Bessel function of
the first kind, $K(v, x)$,
satisfying the differential equation $x^2 {w''(x)$ + x w'(x)
,- (x^2+v^2)w(x) = 0}.
Note: The default implementation uses the relation
$K(v, x) = \pi/2(I(-v, x) - I(v, x))/\sin(v \pi)$
so is not valid for integer values of $v$.
\bigitem$\mbox*besselY*\opLeftPren{$v, 
{} x\opRightPren{}} is the Bessel function of the second
kind, $Y(v, x)$,
satisfying the differential equation $x^2 {w''(x)$ + x w'(x)
+ (x^2-v^2)w(x) = 0}.
Note: The default implementation uses the relation \smath{Y(v, x) =
(J(v, x) \cos(v \pi) - J(-v, x))/\sin(v \pi)} so is not valid for
integer values of $v$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{Beta}}\opLeftPren{}/complexDoubleFloat/,
{}/complexDoubleFloat/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(Complex(DoubleFloat), 
Complex(DoubleFloat))->Complex(DoubleFloat)}{DoubleFloatSpecialFunctions}
{$\mbox*Beta*\opLeftPren{$x, 
{} y\opRightPren{}} 
is the Euler beta function, $B(x, y)$, defined by
$\mbox*Beta*\opLeftPren{$x, 
{} y\opRightPren{}} $\int_0^1{t^{x-1}(1-t)^{y-1} dt}$.
Note: this function is defined by
$\mbox*Beta*\opLeftPren{$x, 
{} y\opRightPren{}} $= 
{{\Gamma(x)\Gamma(y)} \over {\Gamma(x + y)}}$.
}

/integerNumber/, {}/integerNumber/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(I, I)->I}{IntegerCombinatoricFunctions}
{$\mbox*binomial*\opLeftPren{$x, 
{} y\opRightPren{}} returns the binomial coefficient
\smath{C(x, y) = x!/(y!
(x-y)!)}, where \texht{$x \geq y \geq 0$}{x >= y >= 0},

Arguments $x$ and \smath{y} can come from any
\axiomType{Expression} or \axiomType{IntegerNumberSystem} domain.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{bipolar}}\opLeftPren{}/x/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{bipolarCylindrical}}
\opLeftPren{}/x/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(R)->(Point(R))->Point(R)}{CoordinateSystems}
{$\mbox*bipolar*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}} 
returns a function for transforming bipolar
coordinates to
Cartesian coordinates; this function maps the
point $(u, v)$ to \smath{(x = a \sinh(v)/(\cosh(v)-\cos(u)),
y = a \sin(u)/(\cosh(v)-\cos(u)))}.
  \newitem\smath{\mbox*bipolarCylindrical*
\opLeftPren{}a\opRightPren{}} returns a function for transforming
bipolar cylindrical coordinates to Cartesian coordinates; this function
maps the point $(u, v, z)$ to
\smath{(x = a \sinh(v)/(\cosh(v)-\cos(u)), y = a
\sin(u)/(\cosh(v)-\cos(u)), z)}.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{biRank}}\opLeftPren{}
/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(A)->NonNegativeInteger}{AlgebraPackage}
  {$\mbox*biRank*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}\$R},
where $R$ is a domain of
category \axiomType{FramedNonAssociativeAlgebra},
returns the number of linearly independent elements
among $x$, \smath{x b_i}, \smath{b_i x}, 
$b_i x b_j$, \smath{i, j=1, ..., n},
where $b=[b_1, ..., b_n]$ is the fixed basis for \smath{R}.
Note: if $R$ has a unit, then
\spadfunFrom{doubleRank}{AlgebraPackage},
\spadfunFrom{weakBiRank}{AlgebraPackage}
and \spadfunFrom{biRank}{AlgebraPackage} coincide.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{box}}\opLeftPren{}/expression/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(\$))->\$}{ExpressionSpace}
{$\mbox*box*\opLeftPren{$e\opRightPren{}}, where \smath{e} 
is an expression, returns
$e$ with a box around it that prevents \smath{e} from being
evaluated when operators are applied to it.
For example, $\mbox*log*\opLeftPren{$1\opRightPren{}} 
returns $0$, but
$\mbox*log*\opLeftPren{${\mbox*box*}(1)\opRightPren{}} 
returns the formal kernel
$\mbox*log*\opLeftPren{$1\opRightPren{}}.
\newitem
$\mbox*box*\opLeftPren{$f_1, {} ..., f_n
\opRightPren{}}, where the $f_i$ are
expressions, returns $(f_1, ..., f_n)$ with a box around
them that prevents the $f_i$ from being evaluated when
operators are applied to them, and makes them applicable to a
unary operator.
For example, $\mbox*atan*\opLeftPren{${\mbox *box*} 
[x, {} 2]\opRightPren{}} returns the
formal kernel $\mbox*atan*\opLeftPren{$x, 
{} 2\opRightPren{}}.
\newitem$\mbox*box*\opLeftPren{$o\opRightPren{}}, 
where $o$ is an object of type
\axiomType{OutputForm} (normally unexposed), returns an output
form enclosing $o$ in a box.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{characteristicPolynomial}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it matrix\opt{, symbol}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->UP}{FiniteRankAlgebra}
{$\mbox*characteristicPolynomial*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}} 
returns the characteristic
polynomial of the regular representation of $a$ with respect
to any basis.
\newitem
$\mbox*characteristicPolynomial*\opLeftPren{$m\opRightPren{}} 
returns the
characteristic polynomial of the matrix $m$ expressed as
polynomial with a new symbol as variable.
\newitem
$\mbox*characteristicPolynomial*\opLeftPren{$m, 
{} sy\opRightPren{}} is similar except
that the resulting polynomial has variable $sy$.
\newitem
$\mbox*characteristicPolynomial*\opLeftPren{$m, 
{} r\opRightPren{}}, where $r$ is
a member of the coefficient domain of matrix $m$, evaluates
the characteristic polynomial at $r$.
In particular, if $r$ is the polynomial \smath{'x}, then it
returns the characteristic polynomial expressed as a polynomial in
$'x$.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{chebyshevT}}\opLeftPren{}/positiveInteger/,
{}/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(NonNegativeInteger, R)->R}{OrthogonalPolynomialFunctions}
{$\mbox*chebyshevT*\opLeftPren{$n, {} x\opRightPren{}} 
returns the \eth{$n$} Chebyshev polynomial of the
first kind, $T_n(x)$, defined by
$(1-tx)/(1-2tx+t^2) = \sum\nolimits_{n=0$^\infty {T_n(x)\, t^n}}.
}

\spadtype{AbelianMonoidRing},
\spadtype{FreeAbelianCategory},
and \spadtype{MonogenicLinearOperator}.

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{compile}}\opLeftPren{}
/symbol/, {}/listOfTypes/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{ (Symbol, List $) -> Symbol}{}{}
{$\mbox*compile*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} [T_1, {} ..., T_n]\opRightPren{}} 
forces the interpreter to compile
the function with name $f$ with signature 
$(T_1, ..., T_n) -> T$,
where $T$ is a type determined by type analysis of the
function body of $f$.
If the compilation is successful, the operation returns the name $f$.
The operation calls \spadfun{error} if $f$
is not defined beforehand in the interpreter,
or if the $T_i$'s are not valid types, or if the compiler fails.
See also \spadfun{function},
\spadfun{interpret}, \spadfun{lambda}, and \spadfun{compiledFunction}.
}

/expression/, {}/symbol/ $\,[$ , {}
/symbol/$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{ (S, SY) -> (D -> I)}{}{}
{\opkey{Argument $expression$ may be of any type that is
coercible to type \spadtype{InputForm} (most commonly used types).
These functions must be package called to define the type of the
function produced.}
\newitem
$\mbox*compiledFunction*\opLeftPren{$expr, 
{} x\opRightPren{}\$P}, where $P$ is
\spadtype{MakeUnaryCompiledFunction(E, S, T)}, returns an anonymous
function of type $S${T} defined by defined by \smath{x
\mapsto expr}.
The anonymous function is compiled and directly applicable to
objects of type $S$.
\newitem
$\mbox*compiledFunction*\opLeftPren{$expr, 
{} x, {} y\opRightPren{}\$P}, where $P$ is
\spadtype{MakeBinaryCompiledFunction(E, A, B, T)} returns an
anonymous function of type \spadsig{(A, B)}{T} defined by
$(x, y) \mapsto expr$.
The anonymous function is compiled and is then directly applicable
to objects of type $(A, B)$.
\newitem
See also \spadfun{compile}, \spadfun{function}, and
\spadfun{lambda}.
}

$\mbox*composite*\opLeftPren{$lsp\opRightPren{}}, 
where $lsp$ is a list
$[ sp_1, sp_2, ..., sp_n]$ of \spadtype{ThreeSpace} objects,
returns a single \spadtype{ThreeSpace} object containing
the union of all objects in the parameter list grouped as a single composite.
}

/threeSpace/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->List(\$)}{ThreeSpace}

takes the \spadtype{ThreeSpace} object $sp$
and returns a list of \spadtype{ThreeSpace} objects, 
one for each single composite
of $sp$. If \smath{sp} has no defined composites 
(composites need to be explicitly created), the list returned is empty.

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{concat}}\opLeftPren{}
/aggregate/, {}/aggregate/\opRightPren{}%
\opand \mbox{\axiomFun{concat!}}\opLeftPren{}
/aggregate/, {}/aggregate/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, S)->\$}{ExtensibleLinearAggregate}
{$\mbox*concat*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} x\opRightPren{}} returns list $u$ with additional element 
$x$ at the end. Note: equivalent to 
$\mbox*concat*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} [ x]\opRightPren{}}.
\newitem$\mbox*concat*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} v\opRightPren{}} returns an aggregate 
consisting of the elements of $u$ 
followed by the elements of $v$.
\newitem$\mbox*concat*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}}, 
where $u$ is a list of aggregates \smath{[ a, b, $...$, c]}, 
returns a single aggregate consisting of the elements of $a$ followed 
by those of $b$ followed $...$ by the elements of \smath{c}.
\newitem$\mbox*concat!*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} x\opRightPren{}}, where $u$ is 
extensible, destructively adds 
element $x$ to the end of aggregate \smath{u}; if \smath{u} is a stream, 
it must be finite.
\newitem$\mbox*concat!*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} v\opRightPren{}} destructively appends $v$ 
to the end of $u$; if
$u$ is a stream, it must be finite.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{conical}}\opLeftPren{}
/smallFloat/, {}/smallFloat/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(R, R)->(Point(R))->Point(R)}{CoordinateSystems}
{$\mbox*conical*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} returns a function of two parameters for
mapping conical coordinates to Cartesian coordinates.
The function maps the point $(\lambda, \mu, \nu)$ to \smath{x
= \lambda\mu\nu/(ab)}, \smath{y =
\lambda/a\sqrt((mu^2-a^2)(\nu^2-a^2)/(a^2-b^2))}, \smath{z =
\lambda/b\sqrt((mu^2-b^2)(nu^2-b^2)/(b^2-a^2))}.}

}%

quaternion, or octonian expression $u$. For example, 
if $u$ is the
complex expression $x + \%i y$, 
$\mbox*conjugate*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}}
returns $x - \% i y$.
\newitem$\mbox*conjugate*\opLeftPren{$pt\opRightPren{}} 
returns the conjugate of a partition $pt$.
see =PartitionsAndPermutations=
\newitem$\mbox*conjugate*\opLeftPren{$p, 
{} q\opRightPren{}} returns 
$\mbox*inv*\opLeftPren{$q) * p * q}
for elements $p$ and \smath{q} of a group. Note: this operation
is called /right action by conjugation/.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{constant}}\opLeftPren{}
/variableOrfunction/\opRightPren{}%
 \optand \mbox{\axiomFun{constantLeft}}\opLeftPren{}
/function/, {}/element/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{constantRight}}\opLeftPren{}
/function/, {}/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{    (()->C)       -> (A ->C)}{}{}
{\opkey{These operations add an argument to a function
and must be package-called from package $P$ as indicated.
See also \spadfun{curry}, \spadfun{curryLeft}, and \spadfun{curryRight}.}
\newitem
$\mbox*constant*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}\$P} 
returns the function $g$
such that $g(a)= f()$, where
function $f$ has type
\spadsig{}{C} and $a$ has type \smath{A}.
The function must be package-called from
$P =$ \spadtype{MappingPackage2(A, C)}.
\newitem
$\mbox*constantRight*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}\$P} 
returns the function $g$
such that $g(a, b)= f(a)$, where function \smath{f} has
type \spadsig{A}{C} and $b$ has type \smath{B}.
This function must be package-called from
$P =$ \spadtype{MappingPackage3(A, B, C)}.
\newitem
$\mbox*constantLeft*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}\$P} 
returns the function $g$
such that $g(a, b)= f(b)$, where function \smath{f} has
type \spadsig{B}{C} and $a$ has type \smath{A}.
The function must be package-called from
$P =$ \spadtype{MappingPackage3(A, B, C)}.
\newitem
$\mbox*constant*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}} 
tells the pattern matcher that $x$ should match
the symbol $'x$ and no other quantity, or calls 
\spadfun{error} if $x$ is not a symbol.
}

}%
}%

$\mbox*constantOpIfCan*\opLeftPren{$op\opRightPren{}}

}

This is equivalently written

}

{\it polynomial\opt{, symbol}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->R}{FiniteAbelianMonoidRing}
{$\mbox*content*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}} 
returns the greatest common divisor (\spadfun{gcd}) of the 
coefficients of polynomial $p$.
\newitem$\mbox*content*\opLeftPren{$p, 
{} v\opRightPren{}}, where $p$ is a multivariate 
polynomial type, returns
the $gcd$ of the coefficients of the polynomial \smath{p} 
viewed as a univariate polynomial with respect to the variable $v$.
For example, if $p = 7x^2y + 14xy^2$, the \smath{gcd} of the
coefficients with respect to $x$ is \smath{7y}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{continuedFraction}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it fractionOrFloat\opt{, options}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(F)->ContinuedFraction(Integer)}{NumericContinuedFraction}
{$\mbox*continuedFraction*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}} 
converts the floating point number $f$
to a reduced continued fraction.
\newitem$\mbox*continuedFraction*\opLeftPren{$r\opRightPren{}} 
converts the fraction
$r$ with components of type \smath{R} to a continued
fraction over $R$.
\newitem$\mbox*continuedFraction*\opLeftPren{$r, 
{} s, {} s'\opRightPren{}}, where $s$ and
$s'$ are streams over
a domain $R$, constructs a continued fraction in the
following way: if $s = [ a1, a2, $...$]$ and
$s' = [ b1, b2, $...$]$ then the result is the
continued fraction $r + a1/(b1 + a2/(b2 + $...$))$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{contract}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it idealOrTensors\opt{, options}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{3}{(\$, Integer, Integer)->\$}{CartesianTensor}
{$\mbox*contract*\opLeftPren{$I, {} lvar\opRightPren{}} 
contracts the ideal $I$ to the
polynomial ring $F[ lvar]$.
\newitem$\mbox*contract*\opLeftPren{$t, {} i, 
{} j\opRightPren{}} is the contraction of tensor
$t$ which sums along the \eth{\smath{i}} and \eth{\smath{j}}
indices.
For example, if $r = contract(t, 1, 3)$ for a rank 4 tensor
$t$, then \smath{r} is the rank 2 \smath{(= 4 - 2)} tensor
given by $r(i, j) = \sum\nolimits_{h=1$^dimt(h, i, h, j)}.
\newitem$\mbox*contract*\opLeftPren{$t, 
{} i, {} s, {} j\opRightPren{}} 
is the inner product of tensors
$s$ and \smath{t} which sums along the \smath{k_1}st index
of $t$ and the \smath{k_2}st index of \smath{s}.
For example, if $r = contract(s, 2, t, 1)$ for rank 3 tensors
$s$ and \smath{t}, then \smath{r} is the rank 4 \smath{(= 3
+ 3 - 2)} tensor given by \smath{r(i, j, k, l) =
\sum\nolimits_{h=1}^dim s(i, h, j)t(h, k, l)}.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{contractSolve}}\opLeftPren{}
/equation/, {}/symbol/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(Equation(Expression(R)))->List(Equation(Expression(R)))}
{TransSolvePackage}
{$\mbox*contractSolve*\opLeftPren{$eq, 
{} x\opRightPren{}} finds the solutions expressed in
terms of radicals of the equation of rational functions $eq$
with respect to the symbol $x$.
The result contains new symbols for common subexpressions in order
to reduce the size of the output.
Alternatively, an expression $u$ may be given for \smath{eq}
in which case the equation $eq$ is defined as \smath{u=0}
}

of point $pt$.

\medbreak\opkey{The following operations return a matrix
representation of the coordinates of an argument vector $v$
of the form $[ v_1... v_n]$ with respect to
the basis a domain $R$.

\spadtype{FramedAlgebra}.

a monic irreducible polynomial of degree $n$ over the finite field
$GF$.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{createNormalElement}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->\$}{FiniteAlgebraicExtensionField}
{$\mbox*createNormalElement*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
computes a normal element over the ground field
of a finite algebraic extension field $F$, that is,
an element $a$ such that \smath{a^{q^i}, 0 \leq i < {\mbox
*extensionDegree*}()\$F} is an $F$-basis, where
$q$ is the size of the ground field.
}

generates a normal and
primitive polynomial of degree $n$ over the field \smath{GF}.
}

}%
}%
{0}{()->\$}{FiniteFieldCategory}
{$\mbox*createPrimitiveElement*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
computes a generator of the
(cyclic) multiplicative group of a finite
field $F$.}

}%

{$\mbox*csch2sinh*\opLeftPren{$expression\opRightPren{}}

appearing in $f$ into \smath{1/{\sinh}(u)}.}

 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{cschIfCan}}\opLeftPren{}

}%
}%

{\opkey{Argument x can be a \spadtype{Complex}, \spadtype{Float},
\spadtype{DoubleFloat}, or

\newitem$\mbox*cschIfCan*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}}

/symmetricPolynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{ (SPOL RN, SPOL RN) -> SPOL RN}{}{}
{$\mbox*cup*\opLeftPren{$s_1, 
{} s_2\opRightPren{}}, introduced by Redfield,
is the scalar product of two cycle indices, where the
$s_i$ are of type \spadtype{SymmetricPolynomial} with
rational number coefficients.
See also \spadfun{cap}. See \spadtype{CycleIndicators} for details.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{curry}}\opLeftPren{}/function/\opRightPren{}%
 \optand \mbox{\axiomFun{curryLeft}}\opLeftPren{}
/function/, {}/element/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{curryRight}}\opLeftPren{}
/function/, {}/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{   ((A, B)->C, B) -> (A ->C)}{}{}
{\opkey{These functions drop an argument from a function.}
\newitem
$\mbox*curry*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} a\opRightPren{}} returns the function $g$
such that $g()= f(a)$, where function \smath{f} has type
\spadsig{A}{C} and element $a$ has type \smath{A}.
\newitem
$\mbox*curryRight*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} returns the function $g$ such that
$g(a) = f(a, b)$, where function \smath{f} has type
\spadsig{(A, B)}{C} and element $b$ has type \smath{B}.
\newitem
$\mbox*curryLeft*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} a\opRightPren{}} is the function $g$
such that $g(b) = f(a, b)$, where function \smath{f} has type
\spadsig{(A, B)}{C} and element $a$ has type \smath{A}.
\newitem
See also \spadfun{constant}, \spadfun{constantLeft}, 
and \spadfun{constantRight}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{curve}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it listOfPoints\opt{, options}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(Point(R)))->\$}{ThreeSpace}
{$\mbox*curve*\opLeftPren{$
[ p_0, p_1, $...$, p_n]\opRightPren{}} creates a
space curve defined by the list of points $p_0$ through
$p_n$ and returns a \spadtype{ThreeSpace} object whose
component is the curve.
\newitem$\mbox*curve*\opLeftPren{$sp\opRightPren{}} 
checks to see if the
\spadtype{ThreeSpace} object $sp$ is composed of a single
curve defined by a list of points; if so, the list of points
defining the curve is returned.
Otherwise, the operation calls \spadfun{error}.
\newitem$\mbox*curve*\opLeftPren{$c_1, 
{} c_2\opRightPren{}} creates a plane curve from two
component functions $c_1$ and \smath{c_2}.
see =ComponentFunction=
\newitem\smath{curve(sp, [
[ p_0], [ p_1], $...$, [
p_n]])} adds a space curve defined by a list of points
$p_0$ through \smath{p_n} to a \spadtype{ThreeSpace} object
$sp$.
Each $p_i$ is from a domain 
$\mbox*PointDomain*\opLeftPren{$m, 
{} R\opRightPren{}}, where
$R$ is the \spadtype{Ring} over which the point elements are
defined and $m$ is the dimension of the points.
\newitem $\mbox*curve*\opLeftPren{$s, 
{} [ p_0, p_1, $...$, p_n]\opRightPren{}} adds
the space curve component designated by the list of points
$p_0$ through \smath{p_n} to the \spadtype{ThreeSpace} object
$sp$.
\newline $\mbox*curve*\opLeftPren{$c_1, {} c_2, 
{} c_3\opRightPren{}} creates a space curve from
three component functions $c_1$, \smath{c_2}, and
$c_3$.}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{curve?}}\opLeftPren{}/threeSpace/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Boolean}{ThreeSpace}
{$\mbox*curve?*\opLeftPren{$sp\opRightPren{}} 
tests if the \spadtype{ThreeSpace} object $sp$ contains
a single curve object.
}

}%
}%

curves from the palette $p$.
This option is expressed in the form $curveColor ==p$.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{cycle}}\opLeftPren{}
/listOfPermutations/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(S))->\$}{PermutationCategory}
{$\mbox*cycle*\opLeftPren{$ls\opRightPren{}} 
converts a cycle $ls$, a list with no repetitions, to
the permutation, which
maps $ls.i$ to \smath{ls.(i+1)} (index modulo the length of the list).
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{cycleEntry}}\opLeftPren{}
/aggregate/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{UnaryRecursiveAggregate}
{$\mbox*cycleEntry*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} 
returns the head of a top-level cycle
contained in aggregate $u$, or 
$\mbox*empty*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}} if none
exists.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{cycleLength}}\opLeftPren{}
/aggregate/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->NonNegativeInteger}{UnaryRecursiveAggregate}
{$\mbox*cycleLength*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} 
returns the length of a top-level cycle
contained in aggregate $u$, or 0 if \smath{u} has no such
cycle.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{cyclePartition}}\opLeftPren{}
/permutation/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Partition}{Permutation}
{$\mbox*cyclePartition*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}} returns 
the cycle structure of a permutation $p$ including cycles of length 1.
The permutation is assumed to be a member of
\spadtype{Permutation(S)} where $S$ is a finite set.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{cycleRagits}}\opLeftPren{}
/radixExpansion/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->List(Integer)}{RadixExpansion}
{$\mbox*cycleRagits*\opLeftPren{$rx\opRightPren{}} returns the 
cyclic part of the ragits of the fractional part of a radix expansion. 
For example, if $x = 3/28 = 0.10 714285 714285 ...$,
then \code{cycleRagits(x) = [7, 1, 4, 2, 8, 5]}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{cycleSplit!}}\opLeftPren{}
/aggregate/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{UnaryRecursiveAggregate}
{$\mbox*cycleSplit!*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} 
splits the recursive aggregate (for example, a list) $u$ into two
aggregates by dropping off the cycle. The value returned is the cycle entry,
or $nil$ if none exists.
For example, if $w = {\mbox *concat*$(u, v)} 
is the cyclic list where $v$ is the
head of the cycle, \smath{\mbox*cycleSplit!*
\opLeftPren{}w\opRightPren{}} will drop $v$ off \smath{w}. Thus
$w$ is destructively changed to \smath{u}, and \smath{v}
is returned.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{cycles}}\opLeftPren{}
/listOfListOfElements/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(List(S)))->\$}{PermutationCategory}
{$\mbox*cycles*\opLeftPren{$lls\opRightPren{}} 
coerces a list of list of cycles $lls$
to a permutation.
Each cycle, represented as a list $ls$ with no repetitions,
is coerced to the permutation, which maps $ls.i$ to
$ls.(i+1)$ (index modulo the length of the list).
These permutations are then multiplied.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{cycleTail}}\opLeftPren{}
/aggregate/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{UnaryRecursiveAggregate}
{$\mbox*cycleTail*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} 
returns the last node in the cycle of
a recursive aggregate (for example, a list) $u$, 
or empty if none exists.
}

}%
}%
{ I -> SPOL RN    --cyclic group}{}{}
{$\mbox*cyclic*\opLeftPren{$n\opRightPren{}} 
returns the cycle index of the
cyclic group of degree $n$.
\spadtype{CycleIndicators} for details.
}

/listOfMatrices/, {}/vector/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(List(Matrix(R)), Vector(R))->Vector(Vector(R))}{RepresentationPackage2}
{$\mbox*cyclicSubmodule*\opLeftPren{$lm, 
{} v\opRightPren{}}, where $lm$ is a list of
$n$ by \smath{n} square matrices and \smath{v} is a vector

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{cylindrical}}\opLeftPren{}/point/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(Point(R))->Point(R)}{CoordinateSystems}
{$\mbox*cylindrical*\opLeftPren{$pt\opRightPren{}} 
transforms $pt$ from polar
coordinates to Cartesian coordinates,
by mapping the point $(r, theta, z)$ to
$x = r \cos(theta)$, \smath{y = r  \sin(theta)}, \smath{z}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{D}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it expression\opt{, options}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{DifferentialRing}
{$\mbox*D*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}} returns the 
derivative of $x$.
This function is a simple differential operator where no variable
needs to be specified.
\newitem$\mbox*D*\opLeftPren{$x, {} [ s_1, 
... s_n]\opRightPren{}} computes
successive partial derivatives, that is, \smath{D(... {\bf
D}(x, s_1)..., s_n)}.
\newitem$\mbox*D*\opLeftPren{$u, {} x\opRightPren{}} 
computes the partial derivative of
$u$ with respect to \smath{x}.
\newitem$\mbox*D*\opLeftPren{$u, {} 
deriv\optinner{, n}\opRightPren{}} differentiates $u$
$n$ times using a derivation which extends \smath{deriv} on
$R$.
Argument $n$ defaults to 1.
\newitem$\mbox*D*\opLeftPren{$p, {} d, 
{} x'\opRightPren{}} extends the $R$-derivation
$d$ to an extension \smath{R} in \smath{R[ x]}
where $Dx$ is given by \smath{x'}, and returns \smath{Dp}.
\newitem\smath{D(x, [ s_1, ..., s_n], [
n_1, ..., n_m])} computes multiple partial derivatives,
that is, $\mbox*D*\opLeftPren{$... *D*(x, s_1, n_1)..., 
s_n, n_m\opRightPren{}}.
\newitem$\mbox*D*\opLeftPren{$u, {} x, 
{} n\opRightPren{}} computes multiple partial derivatives,
that is, \eth{$n$} derivative of \smath{u} with respect to
$x$.
\newitem $\mbox*D*\opLeftPren{$of\optinner{, n}\opRightPren{}}, 
where $of$ is an object
of type \spadtype{OutputForm} (normally unexposed), returns an
output form for the \eth{$n$} derivative of \smath{f}, for
example, $f'$, \smath{f''}}, \smath{f'''}, \smath{f^{{\tt
iv}}}, and so on.
\newitem $\mbox*D*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$A} 
provides the operator corresponding to the
derivation in the differential ring $A$.
}

}%
}%
{1}{(Color)->\$}{Palette}
{$\mbox*dark*\opLeftPren{$color\opRightPren{}} returns

}

/polynomial/, {}/primeInteger/\opRightPren{}%

{2}{(U, Integer)->List(Record(factor:U, degree:Integer))}
{ModularDistinctDegreeFactorizer}

}%
}%

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{definingPolynomial}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->UP}{MonogenicAlgebra}
{$\mbox*definingPolynomial*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R} 
returns the minimal polynomial for
a \spadtype{MonogenicAlgebra} domain $R$, that is, one which 
$\mbox*generator*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R} satisfies.
\newitem$\mbox*definingPolynomial*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}} 
returns an expression $p$ such that \smath{p(x) = 0}, 
where $x$ is an \spadtype{AlgebraicNumber} 
or an object of type \spadtype{Expression}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{degree}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it polynomial\opt{, symbol}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->E}{AbelianMonoidRing}
{\opkey{The meaning of degree(u\optinner{, s}) depends on the type of 
$u$.}
\begin{simpleList}
\item if $u$ is a polynomial:
$\mbox*degree*\opLeftPren{$u, {} x\opRightPren{}} 
returns the degree of polynomial $u$ with respect to the variable 
$x$.
Similarly, $\mbox*degree*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} lv\opRightPren{}}, where $lv$ is 
a list of variables, returns
a list of degrees of polynomial $u$ with respect 
to each of the variables
in $lv$.
\item if $u$
is an element of an \spadtype{AbelianMonoidRing} or
\spadtype{GradedModule} domain:
$\mbox*degree*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} 
returns the maximum of the exponents of the terms of $u$.
\item if $u$ is a series:
$\mbox*degree*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} 
returns the degree of the leading term of $u$.
\item if $u$ is an element of a domain of category 
\spadtype{ExtensionField}: 
$\mbox*degree*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}}
returns the degree of the minimal polynomial of $u$ 
if $u$ is algebraic
with respect to the
ground field $F$, and =\%infinity= otherwise.
\item if $u$ is a permutation:
$\mbox*degree*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} 
returns the number of points moved by the permutation.
\item if $u$ is a permutation group:
$\mbox*degree*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} 
returns the number of points moved by all permutations of the group $u$.
\seeOther{\spadfun{degree}}
\end{simpleList}
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{delete}}\opLeftPren{}
/aggregate/, {}/integerOrSegment/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, Integer)->\$}{LinearAggregate}
{$\mbox*delete*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} i\opRightPren{}} returns a copy of 
linear aggregate $u$ with
the \eth{$i$} element deleted. Note: for lists,
\code{delete(a, i) == =concat=(a(0..i-1), a(i + 1, ..))}.
\newitem$\mbox*delete*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} i..j\opRightPren{}} returns a copy 
of $u$ with the \eth{\smath{i}}
through \eth{$j$} element deleted.
Note: for lists, \code{delete(a, i..j) = concat(a(0..i-1), a(j+1..))}.
\newitem$\mbox*delete!*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} i\opRightPren{}} destructively deletes 
the \eth{$i$} element of \smath{u}.
\newitem$\mbox*delete!*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} i..j\opRightPren{}} destructively deletes 
elements $u$.\smath{i} 
through $u$.\smath{j} of \smath{u}.
}

/basicOperator/, {}/string/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%

\opRightPren{}} destructively removes property $s$ from \smath{op}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{denom}}\opLeftPren{}
/expression/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{denominator}}\opLeftPren{}
/expression/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->D}{QuotientFieldCategory}
{\opkey{Argument x can be from domain \spadtype{Fraction(R)} for 
some domain $R$, or of type \spadtype{Expression}}
if the result is of type $R$.
\newitem
$\mbox*denom*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}} returns the 
denominator of $x$ as an object
of domain $R$; if \smath{x} is of type \spadtype{Expression}, 
it returns
an object of domain \spadtype{SMP(R, Kernel(Expression R))}.
\newitem
$\mbox*denominator*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}} 
returns the denominator of $x$ as an element
of \spadtype{Fraction(R)}; if $x$ is of type \spadtype{Expression},
it returns an object of domain Expression(R).
}

/fractionOrContinuedFraction/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%

{$\mbox*denominator*\opLeftPren{$frac\opRightPren{}}

\newitem$\mbox*denominators*\opLeftPren{$cf\opRightPren{}}

If the continued fraction is finite, then the stream will be
finite.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{depth}}\opLeftPren{}/stack/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
