% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{dequeue}}\opLeftPren{}/queue/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{dequeue!}}\opLeftPren{}/queue/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->S}{QueueAggregate}
{$\mbox*dequeue*\opLeftPren{$[ x, y, ..., z]\opRightPren{}} 
creates a
dequeue with first (top or front) element $x$, second
element $y$, \smath{...}, and last (bottom or back) element
$z$.
\newitem$\mbox*dequeue!*\opLeftPren{$q\opRightPren{}} 
destructively extracts the first (top)
element from queue $q$.
The element previously second in the queue becomes the first
element.
A call to \spadfun{error} occurs if $q$ is empty.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{derivationCoordinates}}\opLeftPren{}
/vectorOfElements/, {}/derivationFunction/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(Vector(\$), (R)->R)->Matrix(R)}{MonogenicAlgebra}
{$\mbox*derivationCoordinates*\opLeftPren{$v, 
{} {}'\opRightPren{}} returns a matrix 
$M$ such that \smath{v' = M v}.
Argument $v$ is a vector of elements from \smath{R}, a domain
of category \spadtype{MonogenicAlgebra} over a ring $R$.
Argument $'$ is a derivation function defined on \smath{R}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{derivative}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it basicOperator\opt{, property}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(BasicOperator)->Union(List((List(A))->A), "failed")}
{BasicOperatorFunctions1}
{$\mbox*derivative*\opLeftPren{$op\opRightPren{}} 
returns the value of the \mbox="\%diff"=
property of $op$ if it has one, and \mbox="failed"= otherwise.
\newitem$\mbox*derivative*\opLeftPren{$op, 
{} dprop\opRightPren{}} attaches $dprop$ as the
\mbox="\%diff"= property of $op$.
Note: if $op$ has a \mbox="\%diff"= property \smath{f}, then
applying a derivation $D$ to \smath{op}(a) returns
$f(a) D(a)$.
Argument $op$ must be unary.
\newitem$\mbox*derivative*\opLeftPren{$op, 
{} [f_1, {} ..., f_n]\opRightPren{}} attaches
$[ f_1, ..., f_n]$ as the \mbox="\%diff"= property
of $op$.
Note: if $op$ has such a \mbox="\%diff"= property, then applying
a derivation $D$ to \smath{op(a_1, ..., a_n)} returns
\smath{f_1(a_1, ..., a_n) D(a_1) + \cdots + fn(a_1, ..., a_n)
D(a_n)}.
\newitemsee =$D$=
}

}

Note: the underlying coefficient domain of $m$ is assumed to

}

}%
}%
{1}{(List(R))->\$}{MatrixCategory}

consisting of the diagonal elements of $m$.
\newitem
$\mbox*diagonal*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}},
where $f$ is a function of type \spadsig{(A, A)}{T}
is the function $g$
such that $g(a) = f(a, a)$.
See \spadtype{MappingPackage} for related functions.
}

}%
}%
{1}{(List(R))->\$}{MatrixCategory}
{$\mbox*diagonalMatrix*\opLeftPren{$l\opRightPren{}},

\newitem$\mbox*diagonalMatrix*\opLeftPren{$
[ m_1, ..., m_k]\opRightPren{}}

$m_1$, ..., \smath{m_k} down the diagonal,

}%

or rank of Lie algebra $R$.

{TransSolvePackage}
{$\mbox*dioSolve*\opLeftPren{$eq\opRightPren{}} 
computes a basis of all minimal solutions
for a linear homomogeneous Diophantine equation $eq$, then
all minimal solutions of the inhomogeneous equation.

for $eq$ in which case the equation
$eq$ is defined as \smath{u=0}.
}

}%
}%

{}/finiteFieldElement/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%

}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{discriminant}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it polynomial\opt{, symbol}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->R}{FramedAlgebra}
{$\mbox*discriminant*\opLeftPren{$p\optinner{, x}\opRightPren{}} 
returns the discriminant of the polynomial
$p$ with respect to the variable \smath{x}.
If $x$ is univariate, the second argument may be omitted.
\newitem$\mbox*discriminant*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R}
returns $\mbox*determinant*\opLeftPren{$
{\mbox *traceMatrix*}()\$R\opRightPren{}} of a
\spadtype{FramedAlgebra} domain $R$.
\newitem$\mbox*discriminant*\opLeftPren{$
[ v_1, .., v_n]\opRightPren{}} returns \smath{\mbox*determinant*
\opLeftPren{}traceMatrix([ v_1, .., v_n])\opRightPren{}} 
where the $v_i$ each have 
$n$ elements.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{display}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it text\opt{, width}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Void}{ScriptFormulaFormat}
{$\mbox*display*\opLeftPren{$t\optinner{, w}\opRightPren{}},
where $t$ is either IBM SCRIPT Formula Format or TeX{} text,
outputs $t$ so that each line has length \smath{\leq w}.
The default value of $w$ is that length set by
the system command \spadsyscom{)set output length}.
\newitem$\mbox*display*\opLeftPren{$op, 
{} f\opRightPren{}} attaches $f$ 
as the \mbox="\%display"= property
of $op$.
\newitem
$\mbox*display*\opLeftPren{$op\opRightPren{}} 
returns the \mbox="\%display"= property of $op$ if it has one 
attached, and \mbox="failed"= otherwise.
\newitem Value $f$ either has type \spadsig{OutputForm}{OutputForm}
or else \spadsig{List(OutputForm)}{OutputForm}.
Argument $op$ must be unary.
Note: if $op$ has a \mbox="\%display"= 
property $f$ of the former type,
then $op(a)$ gets converted to \spadtype{OutputForm} as \smath{f(a)}.
If $f$ has the latter type,
then $op(a_1, ..., a_n)$ gets converted to
\spadtype{OutputForm} as $f(a_1, ..., a_n)$.
}

}%
}%

/polynomial/, {}/boolean/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(FP, Boolean)->Record(cont:F, 
factors:List(Record(irr:FP, pow:Integer)))}{DistinctDegreeFactorize}
{$\mbox*distdfact*\opLeftPren{$p, 
{} squareFreeFlag\opRightPren{}} produces the complete

is assumed square free.}

{\it expression\opt{, f}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{ExpressionSpace}
{$\mbox*distribute*\opLeftPren{$f\optinner{, g}\opRightPren{}} 
expands all the kernels in
$f$ that contain \smath{g} in their arguments and that are
formally enclosed by a \spadfunFrom{box}{ExpressionSpace} or a
\spadfunFrom{paren}{ExpressionSpace} expression.
By default, $g$ is the list of all kernels in \smath{f}.
}

}%
}%

{$\mbox*divide*\opLeftPren{$x, {} y\opRightPren{}}

$y$.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{draw}}\opLeftPren{}/functionOrExpression/,
{}/range/ $\,[$ , {}
/options/$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{((DoubleFloat)->DoubleFloat, Segment(Float))->
TwoDimensionalViewport}{TopLevelDrawFunctionsForCompiledFunctions}
{$f$, \smath{g}, and \smath{h} below denote user-defined
functions which map one or more \spadtype{DoubleFloat} values to a
\spadtype{DoubleFloat} value.
\bigitem$\mbox*draw*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} a..b\opRightPren{}} draws the \twodim{} graph of 
$y = f(x)$ as \smath{x} 
ranges from $\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} to
$\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem$\mbox*draw*\opLeftPren{$curve(f, g), 
{} a..b\opRightPren{}} draws the \twodim{} graph of
the parametric curve $x = f(t), y = g(t)$ as \smath{t}
ranges from $\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem$\mbox*draw*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} a..b, {} c..d\opRightPren{}} 
draws the \threedim{} graph of
$z = f(x, y)$ as \smath{x} ranges from 
$\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} to
$\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
and $y$ ranges from \smath{\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{}c, 
{} d\opRightPren{}} to
$\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$c, {} d\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem$\mbox*draw*\opLeftPren{$curve(f, g, h), 
{} a..b\opRightPren{}} draws a \threedim{} graph
of the parametric curve $x = f(t), y = g(t), z = h(t)$ as
$t$ ranges from \smath{\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{}a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem$\mbox*draw*\opLeftPren{$surface(f, g, h), 
{} a..b, {} c..d\opRightPren{}} draws the
\threedim{} graph of the parametric
surface $x = f(u, v)$, \smath{y = g(u, v)}, 
$z = h(u, v)$ as \smath{u} ranges from 
$\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} to 
$\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
and $v$ ranges from \smath{\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{}c, 
{} d\opRightPren{}} to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$c, 
{} d\opRightPren{}}.
\medbreak\bigopkey{Arguments $f$, \smath{g}, and \smath{h}
below
denote an \spadtype{Expression} involving the variables indicated as arguments.
For example, $f(x, y)$ denotes an expression involving the
variables $x$
and $y$.}
\bigitem$\mbox*draw*\opLeftPren{$f(x), 
{} x = a..b\opRightPren{}} draws the \twodim{} graph of
$y = f(x)$ as
$x$ ranges from \smath{\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{}a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem$\mbox*draw*\opLeftPren{$curve(f(t), g(t)), 
{} t = a..b\opRightPren{}} draws the \twodim{} graph of the
parametric curve $x = f(t), y = g(t)$ as \smath{t} ranges from 
$\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} to 
$\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem$\mbox*draw*\opLeftPren{$f(x, y), {} x = a..b, 
{} y = c..d\opRightPren{}} draws the
\threedim{} graph of $z = f(x, y)$ as \smath{x} ranges from
$\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} to 
$\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} and $y$ 
ranges from
$\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$c, {} d\opRightPren{}} to 
$\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$c, {} d\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem$\mbox*draw*\opLeftPren{$curve(f(t), g(t), h(t)), 
{} t = a..b\opRightPren{}} draws the
\threedim{} graph of the parametric curve $x = f(t)$,
$y = g(t)$, \smath{z = h(t)} as \smath{t} ranges from
$\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem\smath{*draw*(surface(f(u, v), g(u, v), h(u, v)), u = a..b,
v = c..d)} draws the \threedim{} graph of the parametric surface
$x = f(u, v)$, \smath{y = g(u, v)}, \smath{z = h(u, v)} as
$u$ ranges from \smath{\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{}a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} and
$v$ ranges from \smath{\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{}c, 
{} d\opRightPren{}} to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$c, 
{} d\opRightPren{}}.
\medbreak Each of the \spadfun{draw} operations optionally take
options given as
extra arguments.
\smallbreak\opoption{adaptive}{true} turns on adaptive plotting.
\smallbreak\opoption{clip}{true} turns on \twodim{} clipping.
\smallbreak\opoption{colorFunction}{f} specifies the color based
on a function.
\smallbreak\opoption{coordinates}{p} specifies a change of
coordinate systems of point $p$:
$bipolar$,
$bipolarCylindrical$,
$conical$,
$elliptic$,
$ellipticCylindrical$,
$oblateSpheroidal$,
$parabolic$,
$parabolicCylindrical$,
$paraboloidal$,
$prolateSpheroidal$,
$spherical$, and
$toroidal$
\smallbreak\opoption{curveColor}{p} specifies a color index 
for \twodim{} graph curves from the pallete $p$.
\smallbreak\opoption{pointColor}{p} specifies a color index 
for \twodim{} graph points
from the palette $p$.
\smallbreak\opoption{range}{[ a..b]} provides a user-specified range
for implicit curve plots.
\smallbreak\opoption{space}{sp} adds the current graph to 
\spadtype{ThreeSpace} object
$sp$.
\smallbreak\opoption{style}{s} specifies the drawing style in
which the graph will be plotted: $wire$, \smath{solid},
$shade$, \smath{smooth}.
\smallbreak\opoption{title}{s} titles the graph with string $s$.
\smallbreak\opoption{toScale}{true} causes the graph to be drawn to scale.
\smallbreak\opoption{tubePoints}{n} specifies the number of 
points $n$ defining
the circle which creates the tube around a \threedim{} curve. 
The default value is 6.
\smallbreak\opoption{tubeRadius}{r} specifies a \spadtype{Float} 
radius $r$
for a tube plot around a \threedim{} curve.
\smallbreak\opoption{unit}{[ a, b]} marks off the units of a \twodim{} graph
in increments $a$ along the x-axis, \smath{b} along the y-axis.
\smallbreak\opoption{var1Steps}{n} indicates the number of 
subdivisions $n$
of the first range variable.
\smallbreak\opoption{var2Steps}{n} indicates the number of
subdivisions $n$
of the second range variable.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{elt}}\opLeftPren{}/structure/, {}
/various/ $\,[$ , {}
/.../$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->R}{CartesianTensor}
{\opkey{$\mbox*elt*\opLeftPren{$u, {} v\opRightPren{}}, 
usually written as $u.v$ or
$u(v)$, regards the structure \smath{u} as a function and
applies structure $u$ to argument \smath{v}.
Many types export \spadfun{elt} with multiple arguments;
$\mbox*elt*\opLeftPren{$u, {} v, 
{} w...\opRightPren{}} is generally written
$u(v, w...)$.
The interpretation of $u$ depends on its type.
If $u$ is:}
\begin{simpleList}
\item an indexed aggregate such as a list, stream, vector, or string:
$u.i$, \smath{1 \leq i \leq maxIndex(u)}, is equivalently
written $u(i)$ and
returns the \eth{$i$} element of \smath{u}.
Also, $u(i, y)$ returns \smath{u(i)} if \smath{i} is an
appropriate index for
$u$, and \smath{y} otherwise.
\item a linear aggregate:
$u(i..j)$ returns the aggregate of elements of \smath{u(k)}
for $k=i, i+1, ..., j$
in that order.
\item a basic operator: $u(x)$ applies the unary operator
$u$ to \smath{x};
similarly, $u.[x_1, ..., x_n]$ applies the \smath{n}-ary operator
$u$ to \smath{x_1, ..., x_n}.
Also,
$u(x, y)$, \smath{u(x, y, z)}, and \smath{u(x, y, z, w)} respectively
apply the binary, ternary, or 4-ary operator $u$ to arguments.
\item a univariate polynomial or rational function:
$u(y)$ evaluates the rational function or polynomial with
the distinguished variable replaced by the value of $y$;
this value may either be another rational function or polynomial
or a member of the underlying coefficient domain.
\item a list: $u.first$ is equivalent to 
$\mbox*first*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} and returns
the first element of list $u$.
Also, $u.last$ is equivalent to 
$\mbox*last*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} and returns
the last element of
list $u$.
Both of these call \spadfun{error} if $u$ is the empty list.
Similarly, $u.rest$ is equivalent to 
$\mbox*rest*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} and
returns the list $u$
beginning at its second element, or calls \spadfun{error} 
if $u$ has less than
two elements.
\item a library:
$u(name)$ returns the entry in the library stored under the
key $name$.
\item a linear ordinary differential operator:
$u(x)$ applies the differential operator \smath{u} to the
value $x$.
\item a matrix or two-dimensional array:
$u(i, j\optinner{, x$)}, \smath{1 \leq i \leq nrows(u), 
1 \leq j \leq ncols(m)}, returns the
element in the \eth{$i$} row and \eth{\smath{j}} 
column of the matrix $m$.
If the indices are out of range and an extra argument 
$x$ is provided,
then $x$ is returned; otherwise, \spadfun{error} is called.
Also, $u([i_1, ..., i_m], [j_1, ..., j_m])$ returns
the $m$-by-\smath{n} matrix consisting of elements 
$u(i_k, j_l)$ of \smath{u}.
\item a permutation group:
$u(i)$ returns the \smath{i}-th generator of the group \smath{u}.
\item a point: $u.i$ returns the \eth{\smath{i}} component 
of the point $u$.
\item a rewrite rule:
$u(f\optinner{, n$)} applies rewrite rule \smath{u} to 
expression $f$
at most $n$ times, where \smath{n=\infty} by default.
When the left-hand side of $u$ matches a subexpression of \smath{f},
the subexpression is replaced by the right-hand side of $u$ 
producing a new $f$.
After $n$ iterations or when no further match occurs, the 
transformed $f$
is returned.
\item a ruleset:
$u(f\optinner{, n$)} applies ruleset \smath{u} to expression 
$f$ at most \smath{n}
times, where $n=\infty$ by default.
Similar to last case, except that on each iteration, each rule in 
the ruleset is
applied in turn in attempt to find a match.
\item an \axiomType{SExpression} $(a_1, ..., a_n {$. {}b)}
(where $b$ denotes the \spadfun{cdr} of the last node):
$u.i$ returns \smath{a_i}; similarly
$u.[i_1, ..., i_m]$ returns \smath{(a_{i_1}, ..., a_{i_m})}.
\item a univariate series:
$u(r)$ returns the coefficient of the term of degree
$r$ in \smath{u}.
\item a symbol: $u[a_1, ..., a_n]$ returns \smath{u}
subscripted by $a_1, ..., a_n$.
\item a cartesian tensor:
$u(r)$ gives a component of a rank 1 tensor;
$u([i_1, ..., l_n])$ gives a component of a rank \smath{n} tensor;
$u()$ gives the component of a rank 0 tensor.
Also: $u(i, j)$,
$u(i, j, k)$,
and $u(i, j, k, l)$ gives a component of a rank 2, 3, and 4
tensors respectively.
\item See also \axiomType{QuadraticForm},
\axiomType{FramedNonAssociativeAlgebra}, and
\axiomType{FunctionFieldCategory}.
\end{simpleList}
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{eval}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it expression\opt{, options}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{FunctionSpace}
{\opkey{Many domains have forms of the \spadfun{eval}
defined. Here are some the most common forms.}
\newitem
$\mbox*eval*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}} unquotes all the 
quoted operators in $f$.
\newitem
$\mbox*eval*\opLeftPren{$f, {} x = v\opRightPren{}} 
replaces symbol or expression $x$ by
$v$ in \smath{f};
if $x$ is an expression, it must be retractable to a single
\axiomType{Kernel}.
\newitem
$\mbox*eval*\opLeftPren{$f, {} [x_1 = v_1, 
{} ..., x_n = v_n]\opRightPren{}} returns $f$
with symbols
or expressions $x_i$
replaced by $v_i$ in parallel;
if $x_i$ is an expression, it must be retractable to a
single \axiomType{Kernel}.
\newitem
$\mbox*eval*\opLeftPren{$f, {} [x_1, {} 
..., x_n]\opRightPren{}} unquotes all
the quoted operations in $f$ whose name is one of the \smath{x_i}.'s.
\newitem
$\mbox*eval*\opLeftPren{$f, {} x\opRightPren{}} 
unquotes all quoted operators in $f$
whose name is $x$.
\newitem
$\mbox*eval*\opLeftPren{$e, {} s, 
{} f\opRightPren{}}
replaces every subexpression of $e$ of the form
$s(a_1, ..., a_n)$ by \smath{f(a_1, ..., a_n)}.
The function $f$ can have type
\spadsig{Expression}{Expression} if $s$ is a unary operator;
otherwise $f$
must have signature \spadsig{List(Expression)}{Expression}.
\newitem
$\mbox*eval*\opLeftPren{$e, {} [s_1, 
{} ..., s_n], [f_1, ..., f_n]\opRightPren{}},
replaces every subexpression of $e$ of the form
$s_i(a_1, ..., a_{n_i$)} by \smath{f_i(a_1, ..., a_{n_i})}.
If all the $s_i$'s are unary operators, the functions
$f_i$ can have signature \spadsig{Expression}{Expression};
otherwise, the $f_i$ must have signature
\spadsig{List(Expression)}{Expression}.
\newitem
$\mbox*eval*\opLeftPren{$p, {} el\opRightPren{}}, 
where $p$ is a permutation,
returns the image of element /el/ under $p$.
\newitem
$\mbox*eval*\opLeftPren{$s\opRightPren{}}, 
where \spad{s} is of type \axiomType{SymmetricPolynomial} with
rational number coefficients, returns the sum of the 
coefficients of a cycle index.
See \axiomType{CycleIndicators} for details.
\newitem
$\mbox*eval*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} s\opRightPren{}}, where \spad{s} is of type 
\axiomType{SymmetricPolynomial}
with rational number coefficients and \spad{f} is a function of type
\spadsig{Integer}{Algebra Fraction Integer},
evaluates the cycle index s by applying
the function \spad{f} to each integer in a monomial partition,
forms their product and sums the results over all monomials.
See \axiomType{EvaluateCycleIndicators} for details.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{evaluate}}\opLeftPren{}
/operator/, {}/function/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(BasicOperator, (A)->A)->BasicOperator}{BasicOperatorFunctions1}
{$\mbox*evaluate*\opLeftPren{$op\opRightPren{}} 
returns the value of the \mbox="\%eval"= property
of \axiomType{BasicOperator}
object $op$ if it has one, and \mbox="failed"= otherwise.
\newitem
$\mbox*evaluate*\opLeftPren{$op, 
{} f\opRightPren{}} attaches $f$ as the \mbox="\%eval"=
property of $op$.
If $op$ has an \mbox="\%eval"= property \smath{f}, then applying
$op$ to a
returns the result of $f(a)$.
If $f$ takes a single argument, then
applying $op$ to a value \smath{a} returns the result \smath{f(a)}.
If $f$ takes a list of arguments, then
applying $op$ to \smath{a_1, ..., a_n} returns the
result of $f(a_1, ..., a_n)$.
\newitem
Argument $f$ may also be an anonymous function of
the form $u +-> g(u)$. In this case,
$g$ /must/ be additive,
that is, $g(a + b) = g(a) + g(b)$ for any
$a$ and \smath{b} in \smath{R}.
This implies that $g(n a) = n g(a)$ for any \smath{a}
in $R$ and integer \smath{n > 0}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{expand}}\opLeftPren{}/expression/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(F)->F}{TranscendentalManipulations}
{$\mbox*expand*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}} performs the 
following expansions
on \axiomType{Expression} $f:$
\begin{simpleList}
\item Logs of products are expanded into sums of logs.
\item Trigonometric and hyperbolic trigonometric functions of
sums are expanded into sums of products of trigonometric
and hyperbolic trigonometric functions.
\item Formal powers of the form $(a/b)^c$ are expanded into
$a^c  b^{(-c)$}.
\end{simpleList}
\newitem
$\mbox*expand*\opLeftPren{$ir\opRightPren{}},
where $ir$ is an \axiomType{IntegrationResult},
returns the list of possible real functions corresponding to $ir$.
\newitem
$\mbox*expand*\opLeftPren{$lseg\opRightPren{}},
where $lseg$ is a list of segments, returns a list with all segments
expanded.
For example, \code{expand [1..4, 7..9] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9]}.
\newitem
$\mbox*expand*\opLeftPren{$l..h \mbox{ \tt by } k\opRightPren{}} 
returns
a list of explicit elements.
For example, \code{expand(1..5 by 2) = [1, 3, 5]}.
\newitem
$\mbox*expand*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}} 
returns an unfactored form of factored object $f$.
}

/element/, {}/element/ $\,[$ , {}
/element/$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->Record(coef1:\$, coef2:\$, generator:\$)}{EuclideanDomain}
{\opkey{Argments $x$, \smath{y}, and \smath{z} are members
of a domain of category \axiomType{EuclideanDomain}.}
\newitem$\mbox*extendedEuclidean*\opLeftPren{$x, 
{} y\opRightPren{}} returns a record
$rec$ containing three fields: \smath{coef1}, \smath{coef2},
and $generator$ where \smath{rec.coef1*x+rec.coef2*y =
rec.generator} and $rec.generator$ is a \smath{gcd} of
$x$ and \smath{y}.
The $gcd$ is unique only up to associates if
=canonicalUnitNormal= is not asserted.
Note: See \spadfun{principalIdeal} for a version of this operation
which accepts an arbitrary length list of arguments.
\newitem$\mbox*extendedEuclidean*\opLeftPren{$x, 
{} y, {} z\opRightPren{}} either returns a record
$rec$ of two fields \smath{coef1} and \smath{coef2} where
$rec.coef1*x+rec.coef2*y=z$, and \mbox="failed"= if \smath{z}
cannot be expressed as such a linear combination of $x$ and
$y$.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{function}}\opLeftPren{}
/expression/, {}/name/ $\,[$ , {}
/options/$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(S, Symbol)->Symbol}{MakeFunction}
{\opkey{Most domains provide an operation which converts
objects to type \axiomType{InputForm}.
Argument $e$ below denotes an object from such a domain.
These operations create user-functions from already computed results.}
\newitem$\mbox*function*\opLeftPren{$e, {} f
\opRightPren{}} creates a function $f() == e$.
\newitem$\mbox*function*\opLeftPren{$e, {} f, 
{} [x_1, {} ..., x_n]\opRightPren{}} 
creates a function 
$f(x_1, ..., x_n) == e$.
\newitem$\mbox*function*\opLeftPren{$e, {} f, 
{} x\opRightPren{}} creates a function $f(x) == e$.
\newitem$\mbox*function*\opLeftPren{$e, 
{} f, {} x, {} y\opRightPren{}} 
creates a function $f(x, y) == e$.
\newitem$\mbox*function*\opLeftPren{$expr, 
{} [x_1, {} ..., x_n], f\opRightPren{}},
where $expr$ is an input form and
where $f$ and the \smath{x_i}'s are symbols,
returns the input form
corresponding to $f(x_1, ..., x_n) == i$.
See also \spadfun{unparse}.
}

}

{$\mbox*gcd*\opLeftPren{$x, {} y\opRightPren{}}

category $GcdDomain$.
\newitem$\mbox*gcd*\opLeftPren{$[x_1, 
{} ..., x_n]\opRightPren{}} returns the

\newitem$\mbox*gcd*\opLeftPren{$p_1, {} p_2, 
{} prime\opRightPren{}} computes the $gcd$ of the univariate
polynomials $p_1$ and \smath{p_2} modulo the prime integer 
$prime$.}

Record(mval:Matrix(F), invmval:Matrix(F), genIdeal:\$)}{PolynomialIdeals}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{generate}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it function\opt{, element}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(()->S)->\$}{Stream}
{$\mbox*generate*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}},
where $f$ is a function of no arguments,
creates an infinite stream all of whose elements are equal to
the value of $f()$. Note: \smath{\mbox*generate*
\opLeftPren{}f) = [f(), f(), f(), ...]}.
\newitem$\mbox*generate*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} x\opRightPren{}},
where $f$ is a function of one argument,
creates an infinite stream whose first element is $x$
and whose \eth{$n$} element (\smath{n > 1}) is \smath{f} applied to the
previous element.
Note: $\mbox*generate*\opLeftPren{$f, x) = 
[x, f(x), f(f(x)), ...]}.
\newitem See also \axiomType{HallBasis}.
}

}%
}%
{0}{()->\$}{FiniteAlgebraicExtensionField}
{$\mbox*generator*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R} returns 
a root of the defining polynomial
of a domain of category \axiomType{FiniteAlgebraicExtensionField} $R$.
This element generates the field as an algebra over the ground field.
\newitem
See also \axiomType{MonogenicAlgebra} and \axiomType{FreeNilpotentLie}.
}

group /gp/.
}

}%
}%
{0}{()->NonNegativeInteger}{FunctionFieldCategory}
{$\mbox*genus*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}}*\$*\smath{R} 
returns the genus of
the algebraic function field $R$.
If $R$ has several

returned.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{getMultiplicationMatrix}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
 \optand \mbox{\axiomFun{getMultiplicationTable}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->Matrix(PrimeField(p))}{FiniteFieldNormalBasis}
{$\mbox*getMultiplicationMatrix*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R} 
returns a matrix multiplication table
for domain \axiomType{FiniteFieldNormalBasis(p, n)},
a finite extension field of degree $n$ over the domain
\axiomType{PrimeField(p)} with $p$ elements.
Each element of the matrix is a member of the underlying prime field.
\newitem
$\mbox*getMultiplicationTable*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R} 
is similar except that the
multiplication table for the normal basis of the field
is represented by a vector of lists of records, each record
having two fields: $value$, an element of the prime field over
which the domain is built, and $index$, a small integer.
This table is used to perform multiplications between field elements.
}

}%
}%

{UserDefinedVariableOrdering}
{$\mbox*getVariableOrder*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}}

[a_1, ..., a_n] ]} such that the ordering on the variables was given
by $\mbox*setVariableOrder*\opLeftPren{$[b_1, 
{} ..., b_m], [a_1, ..., a_n]\opRightPren{}}.}

}%
}%

#+INDEX: Zech logarithm

\axiomType{FiniteFieldCyclicGroup(p, extdeg)}.
This table is used to perform additions in the field quickly.}

}%
}%

List(Matrix(Expression(Fraction(Integer))))}{RadicalEigenPackage}

elements of type \axiomType{Expression}.}
\newitem
$\mbox*gramschmidt*\opLeftPren{$lv\opRightPren{}} 
converts the list of column vectors
$lv$ into a set of orthogonal column vectors of Euclidean
length 1 using the Gram-Schmidt algorithm.
#+INDEX: Gram-Schmidt algorithm
}

}%
}%
{ I -> SPOL RN}{}{}

}%
}%
{0}{()->\$}{Color}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{groebner}}\opLeftPren{}
/listOfPolynomials/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(Dpol))->List(Dpol)}{GroebnerPackage}
{$\mbox*groebner*\opLeftPren{$lp\opRightPren{}} 
computes a Gr\"obner basis for a polynomial
ideal generated by the list of polynomials $lp$.
\newitem $\mbox*groebner*\opLeftPren{$I\opRightPren{}} 
returns a set of generators of ideal
$I$ that are a Gr\"obner basis for \smath{I}.
\newitem $\mbox*groebner*\opLeftPren{$lp, {} 
infoflag\opRightPren{}} computes a Gr\"obner basis
for a polynomial ideal generated by the list of polynomials
$lp$.
Argument $infoflag$ is used to get information on the
computation.
If $infoflag$ is \mbox="info"=, then summary information 
is displayed for
each s-polynomial generated.
If $infoflag$ is \mbox="redcrit"=, the reduced critical pairs are
displayed.
To get the display of both kinds of information, use
$\mbox*groebner*\opLeftPren{$lp, {} "info", 
{} "redcrit"\opRightPren{}}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{groebner?}}\opLeftPren{}/ideal/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Boolean}{PolynomialIdeals}
{$\mbox*groebner?*\opLeftPren{$I\opRightPren{}} 
tests if the generators of the ideal
$I$ are a Gr\"obner basis.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{groebnerIdeal}}\opLeftPren{}
/listOfPolynomials/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(DPoly))->\$}{PolynomialIdeals}
{$\mbox*groebnerIdeal*\opLeftPren{$lp\opRightPren{}} 
constructs the ideal generated by the
list of
polynomials $lp$ assumed to be a Gr\"obner basis.
Note: this operation avoids a Gr\"obner basis computation.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{groebnerFactorize}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it listOfPolynomials\opt{options}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(Dpol))->List(List(Dpol))}{GroebnerFactorizationPackage}
{$\mbox*groebnerFactorize*\opLeftPren{$lp
\optinner{, bool}\opRightPren{}} returns
a list of list of polynomials, each inner list denoting a Gr\"obner basis.
The union of the solutions of the bases is the solution of the system of
equations given by $lp$.
Information about partial results is printed if a
second argument is given with value $true$.
\newitem
$\mbox*groebnerFactorize*\opLeftPren{$lp, 
{} nonZeroRestrictions\optinner{, bool}\opRightPren{}},
where $nonZeroRestrictions$ is a list of polynomials, is similar.
Here, however, the solutions to the system of equations are computed
under the restriction that the polynomials in the second argument
do not vanish.
Information about partial results is printed if a
third argument with value $true$ is given.
}

{1}{(\$)->NonNegativeInteger}{ExpressionSpace}

Note: $\mbox*height*\opLeftPren{$d) = # d}.
}

}%
{3}{(S, \$, Integer)->\$}{LinearAggregate}
{$\mbox*insert*\opLeftPren{$x, {} u,

$x$ as its \eth{\smath{i}} element.

inserted beginning at the \eth{$i$} element.
\newitem

destructively inserts item $x$ into
bag $u$.
\newitem

destructively inserts item $x$ as a
leaf into binary search
tree or binary tournament \spad{u}.
\newitem

{} i\opRightPren{}} destructively inserts $x$ into

\newitem

{} i\opRightPren{}} destructively inserts aggregate $v$
into $u$ at position \smath{i}.
\newitem
$\mbox*insert!*\opLeftPren{$x, {} d, 
{} n\opRightPren{}} destructively inserts $n$ copies of
$x$ into dictionary \smath{d}.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{integralBasis}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{integralBasisAtInfinity}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->Vector(\$)}{FunctionFieldCategory}
{\opkey{Domain $F$ is the domain of functions on a fixed curve.
see =FunctionFieldCategory=}
\newitem$\mbox*integralBasisAtInfinity*\opLeftPren{$
\opRightPren{}\$F} returns the local
integral basis at infinity.
\newitem$\mbox*integralBasis*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
returns the integral basis for
the curve.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{integralCoordinates}}\opLeftPren{}
/function/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Record(num:Vector(UP), den:UP)}{FunctionFieldCategory}
{$\mbox*integralCoordinates*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}},
where $f$ is a function on a curve defined by domain \smath{F},
returns the coordinates of $f$ with respect to the 
$\mbox*integralBasis*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F}
as polynomials $A_i$ together with a common denominator \smath{d}.
Specifically, the operation returns a record having selector
$num$ with value \smath{[A_1, ..., A_n]} and selector \smath{den} with
value $d$ such that
$f = (A_1 w_1 +...+ A_n w_n) / d$ where 
$(w_1, ..., w_n)$ is the
integral basis.
see =FunctionFieldCategory=
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{integralDerivationMatrix}}\opLeftPren{}
/function/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{((UP)->UP)->Record(num:Matrix(UP), den:UP)}{FunctionFieldCategory}
{$\mbox*integralDerivationMatrix*\opLeftPren{$d\opRightPren{}} 
extends the derivation $d$ and
returns the coordinates of the derivative of $f$ with respect to
the $\mbox*integralBasis*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
as a matrix of polynomials and a common denominator $Q$.
Specifically, the operation returns a record having selector
$num$ with value \smath{M}
and selector $den$ with value \smath{Q} such that
the \eth{$i$} row of \smath{M} divided by \smath{Q} form the
coordinates of $f$ with respect to integral basis
$(w1, ..., wn)$.
see =FunctionFieldCategory=
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{integralMatrix}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{integralMatrixAtInfinity}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->Matrix(Fraction(UP))}{FunctionFieldCategory}
{\opkey{Domain $F$ is a domain of functions on a fixed curve. These
operations return a matrix which transform the natural basis to an 
integral basis.
see =FunctionFieldCategory=
}
\newitem
$\mbox*integralMatrix*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}} returns 
$M$ such that
$(w_1, ..., w_n) = M (1, y, ..., y^{n-1$)},
where $(w_1, ..., w_n)$ is the integral basis returned by
$\mbox*integralBasis*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F}.
\newitem
$\mbox*integralMatrixAtInfinity*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
returns matrix $M$
which transforms the natural basis
such that $(v_1, ..., v_n) = M (1, y, ..., y^{n-1$)}
where $(v_1, ..., v_n)$ is the local integral basis at
infinity returned by \smath{\mbox*integralBasisAtInfinity*
\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}\$F}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{integralRepresents}}
\opLeftPren{}/vector/, {}/commonDenominator/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(Vector(UP), UP)->\$}{FunctionFieldCategory}
{$\mbox*integralRepresents*\opLeftPren{$
[A_1, {} ..., A_n], d\opRightPren{}} is the inverse
of the operation
\spadfunFrom{integralCoordinates}{FunctionFieldCategory} defined
for domain $F$, a domain of functions on a fixed curve. Given
the coordinates as polynomials $[A_1, ..., A_n]$ over
a common denominator $d$, this operation returns the function
represented as$(A_1 w_1+...+A_n w_n)/d$ where
$(w_1, ..., w_n)$ is the integral basisreturned by
$\mbox*integralBasis*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F}.
see =FunctionFieldCategory=}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{integrate}}\opLeftPren{}

 $\,[$ , {}
/options/$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{UnivariatePolynomialCategory}
{$\mbox*integrate*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}} 
returns the integral of a
univariate polynomial or power series $f$ with respect to
its distinguished variable.
\newitem$\mbox*integrate*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} x\opRightPren{}} returns the integral of
$f(x)dx$, where \smath{x} is viewed as a real variable.
\newitem$\mbox*integrate*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} x = a..b\optinner{, "noPole"}\opRightPren{}}
returns the integral of $f(x)dx$ from \smath{a} to \smath{b}.
If it is not possible to check whether $f$ has a pole for
$x$ between \smath{a} and \smath{b}, then a third argument
\mbox="noPole"= will make this function assume that$f$
has no such pole.This operation calls \spadfun{error} if $f$
has a pole for $x$ between \smath{a} and \smath{b} or if
a third argument different from \mbox="noPole"= is given.}

as one of the following strings: ="input", "output"= or ="closed".=
}

/polynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(FP)->Boolean}{DistinctDegreeFactorize}
{$\mbox*irreducible?*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}} 
tests whether the polynomial $p$ is irreducible.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{irreducibleFactor}}\opLeftPren{}
/element/, {}/integer/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(R, Integer)->\$}{Factored}
{$\mbox*irreducibleFactor*\opLeftPren{$base, {} 
exponent\opRightPren{}} creates a factored
object with a single factor whose $base$ is asserted to be
irreducible (flag = \mbox="irred"=).
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{irreducibleRepresentation}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it listOfIntegers\opt{, permutations}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(List(Integer), Permutation(Integer))->Matrix(Integer)}
{irreducibleRepresentationPackage}
{$\mbox*irreducibleRepresentation*\opLeftPren{$lambda
\optinner{, pi}\opRightPren{}} returns
a matrix giving the irreducible representation corresponding to
partition $lambda$, represented as a list of integers, in
Young's natural form of the permutation $pi$ in the
symmetric group whose elements permute $1, 2, ..., n$.
If a second argument is not given, the permutation is taken to be
the following two generators of the symmetric group, namely
$(1 2)$ (2-cycle) and \smath{(1 2 ... n)}
(\smath(n)-cycle).
}

/pattern/\opRightPren{}%
}%

tests if the expression $expr$ matches the pattern \smath{pat}.
\newitem
$\mbox*is?*\opLeftPren{$expression, {} op\opRightPren{}} 
tests if $expression$ is a kernel and is its operator is op.
}

}%

}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{isExpt}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it expression\opt{, operator}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Union(Record(var:Kernel(\$), exponent:Integer), "failed")}
{FunctionSpace}
{$\mbox*isExpt*\opLeftPren{$p\optinner{, op}\opRightPren{}} 
returns a record with two fields:
$var$ denoting a kernel \smath{x},
and $exponent$ denoting an integer \smath{n},
if expression $p$
has the form $p = x^n$ and \smath{n \not= 0}.
If a second argument $op$ is given,
$x$ must have the form \smath{op(a)} for some \smath{a}.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{isMult}}\opLeftPren{}/expression/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Union(Record(coef:Integer, var:Kernel(\$)), "failed")}{FunctionSpace}
{$\mbox*isMult*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}} returns
a record with two fields:
$coef$ denoting an integer \smath{n},
and $var$ denoting a kernel \smath{x},
if $p$ has the form \smath{n * x} and \smath{n \not= 0},
and \mbox="failed"= if this is not possible.
}

/differentialPolynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%

{$\mbox*isobaric?*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}}

$p$ has the same weight.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{isPlus}}\opLeftPren{}/expression/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Union(List(\$), "failed")}{FunctionSpace}
{$\mbox*isPlus*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}} 
returns $[m_1, ..., m_n]$ if
$p$ has the form \smath{m_1 +...+ m_n} for 
$n > 1$ and \smath{m_i \not= 0},
and \mbox="failed"= if this is not possible.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{isTimes}}\opLeftPren{}/expression/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Union(List(\$), "failed")}{FunctionSpace}
{$\mbox*isTimes*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}} 
returns $[a_1, ..., a_n]$ if
$p$ has the form
$a_1*...*a_n$ for \smath{n > 1} and \smath{m_i \not= 1},
and \mbox="failed"= if this is not possible.
}


% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{Is}}\opLeftPren{}
/subject/, {}/pattern/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(List(Subject), Pat)->
PatternMatchListResult(Base, Subject, List(Subject))}{PatternMatch}
{$Is(expr, pat)$ matches the pattern \smath{pat} on the
expression $expr$ and returns a list of matches \smath{[v_1
= e_1, ..., v_n = e_n]} or \mbox="failed"= if matching
fails.
An empty list is returned if either $expr$ is exactly equal
to $pat$ or if \smath{pat} does not match \smath{expr}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{jacobi}}\opLeftPren{}/integer/,
{}/integer/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(Integer, Integer)->Integer}{IntegerNumberTheoryFunctions}
{$\mbox*jacobi*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} returns the Jacobi symbol $J(a/b)$.
#+INDEX: Jacobi symbol
When $b$ is odd, \smath{J(a/b) = \prod\nolimits_{p \in
*factors*(b)}{L(a/p)}}.
Note: by convention, 0 is returned if 
$\mbox*gcd*\opLeftPren{$a, b) \not= 1}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{jacobiIdentity?}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->Boolean}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{$\mbox*jacobiIdentity?*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}} 
tests if $(a b) c + (b c) a + (c a) b = 0$
for all $a$, \smath{b}, \smath{c} in a domain
of \spadtype{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}. For example,
this relation holds for crossed products of three-dimensional vectors.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{janko2}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it \optinit{listOfIntegers}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(Integer))->PermutationGroup(Integer)}{PermutationGroupExamples}
{$\mbox*janko2*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}} constructs the janko 
group acting on the integers $1, ..., 100$.
\newitem
$\mbox*janko2*\opLeftPren{$\optinner{li}\opRightPren{}} constructs 
the janko group acting on the 100 integers given in the list $li$.
The default value of $li$ is \smath{[1, ..., 100]}.
This operation removes duplicates in the list and calls
\spadfun{error} if $li$ does not have exactly 100 distinct entries.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{jordanAdmissible?}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{jordanAlgebra?}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->Boolean}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{$\mbox*jordanAdmissible?*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F},
where $F$ is a member of
\spadtype{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra(R)} over
a commutative ring $R$,
tests if 2 is invertible
in $R$ and if the algebra defined
by $\{a, b\$} defined by \smath{(1/2)(a b+b a)} is a Jordan 
algebra, that is,
satisfies the Jordan identity.
\newitem
$\mbox*jordanAlgebra?*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
tests if the algebra is commutative,
that $\mbox*characteristic*\opLeftPren{$)\$F \not= 2},
and $(a b) a^2 - a (b a^2) = 0$ for all \smath{a} and \smath{b}
in the algebra (Jordan identity). Example: for every associative algebra
$(A, +, @)$, you can construct a Jordan algebra \smath{(A, +, *)},
where $a*b := (a@b+b@a)/2$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{kernel}}\opLeftPren{}/operator/,
{}/expression/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(BasicOperator, \$)->\$}{ExpressionSpace}
{$\mbox*kernel*\opLeftPren{$op, {} x\opRightPren{}} 
constructs $op$(\smath{x}) without evaluating it.
\newitem
$\mbox*kernel*\opLeftPren{$op, {} [f_1, 
{} ..., f_n]\opRightPren{}} constructs $op(f1, ..., fn)$
without evaluating it.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{kernels}}\opLeftPren{}/expression/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->List(Kernel(\$))}{ExpressionSpace}
{$\mbox*kernels*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}} returns the 
list of all the top-level kernels appearing in
expression $f$,
but not the ones appearing in the arguments of the top-level kernels.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{key?}}\opLeftPren{}/key/, {}
/dictionary/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{keys}}\opLeftPren{}/dictionary/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(Key, \$)->Boolean}{KeyedDictionary}
{$\mbox*key?*\opLeftPren{$k, {} d\opRightPren{}} 
tests if $k$ is a key in dictionary \smath{d}.
Dictionary $d$ is an element of a domain of category
\spadtype{KeyedDictionary(K, E)}, where $K$
and $E$ denote the domains of keys and entries.
\newitem
$\mbox*keys*\opLeftPren{$d\opRightPren{}} 
returns the list the keys in table $d$.
}

/[integer/, {}/integer]/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->\$}{CartesianTensor}
{$\mbox*kroneckerDelta*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}} 
is the rank 2 tensor defined by
$\mbox*kroneckerDelta*\opLeftPren{$i, j) = 1} 
if $i=j$, and 0 otherwise.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{label}}\opLeftPren{}
/outputForm/, {}/outputForm/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{}{}{}
{$\mbox*label*\opLeftPren{$o_1, {} o_2\opRightPren{}}, 
where $o_1$ and \smath{o_2} are
objects of type \spadtype{OutputForm} (normally unexposed),
returns
an output form displaying equation $o_2$ with label
$o_1$.
}


% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{laguerreL}}\opLeftPren{}/nonNegativeInteger/,
{}/x/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{laguerreL}}\opLeftPren{}/nonNegativeInteger/, 
{}/nonNegativeInteger/, {}/x/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(NonNegativeInteger, R)->R}{OrthogonalPolynomialFunctions}
{$\mbox*laguerreL*\opLeftPren{$n, {} x\opRightPren{}} 
is the \eth{$n$} Laguerre
polynomial, $L[n](x)$, defined by \smath{{exp({{-t
x}\over{1-t}})/(1-t)} = \sum\nolimits_{n=0}^\infty {L[n](x)
t^n/n!}}.
\newitem $\mbox*laguerreL*\opLeftPren{$m, 
{} n, {} x\opRightPren{}} is the associated Laguerre
polynomial, $L_m[n](x)$, defined as the \eth{\smath{m}}
derivative of $L[n](x)$.
}

{}/listOfSymbols/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{ ($, List Symbol) -> $}{}{}
{$\mbox*lambda*\opLeftPren{$i, {} [x_1, 
{} ... x_n]\opRightPren{}} returns the input form
corresponding to $(x_1, ..., x_n) \mapsto i$ if \smath{n
> 1}.
See also \spadfun{compiledFunction}, \spadfun{flatten}, and \spadfun{unparse}.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{laplace}}\opLeftPren{}/expression/,
{}/symbol/, {}/symbol/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{3}{(F, Symbol, Symbol)->F}{LaplaceTransform}
{$\mbox*laplace*\opLeftPren{$f, {} t, 
{} s\opRightPren{}} returns the Laplace transform of $f(t)$,
defined by $\int_{t=0$^\infty{exp(-s t)f(t) dt}}.
If the transform cannot be computed, the
formal object $\mbox*laplace*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} t, {} s\opRightPren{}} is returned.
}

\opt{, nonNegativeInteger}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->S}{UnaryRecursiveAggregate}
{$\mbox*last*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} returns the last 
element of $u$.
\newitem
$\mbox*last*\opLeftPren{$u, {} n\opRightPren{}}

\geq 0}) elements
of $u$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{laurent}}\opLeftPren{}
/expression/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{laurentIfCan}}\opLeftPren{}
/expression/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->ULS}{UnivariatePuiseuxSeriesConstructorCategory}
{$\mbox*laurent*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} converts 
$u$ to a Laurent series, or
calls \spadfun{error}
if this is not possible.
\newitem
$\mbox*laurentIfCan*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} converts the 
Puiseux series $u$
to a Laurent series, or returns \mbox="failed"= if this is not possible.
\newitem
$\mbox*laurent*\opLeftPren{$f, {} x = a\opRightPren{}} 
expands the expression $f$ as a
Laurent series in powers of $(x - a)$.
\newitem
$\mbox*laurent*\opLeftPren{$f, {} n\opRightPren{}} 
expands the expression $f$ as a Laurent series in
powers of $x$; at least \smath{n} terms are computed.
\newitem
$\mbox*laurent*\opLeftPren{$n \mapsto a_n, x = a, 
n_0..\optinner{n_1}\opRightPren{}} returns
a Laurent series defined by
$\sum\nolimits_{n = n_0$^{n_1}{a_n (x - a)^n}}, where
$n_1$ is \smath{\infty} by default.
\newitem
$\mbox*laurent*\opLeftPren{$a_n, {} n, 
{} x=a, {} n_0..\optinner{n_1}\opRightPren{}} returns
a Laurent series defined by
$\sum\nolimits_{n=n_0$^{n_1}{a_n(x - a)^n}},
where $n_1$ is \smath{\infty} by default.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{laurentRep}}\opLeftPren{}
/expression/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->ULS}{UnivariatePuiseuxSeriesConstructorCategory}
{$\mbox*laurentRep*\opLeftPren{$f(x)\opRightPren{}} 
returns $g(x)$
where the Puiseux series $f(x) = g(x^r)$ is 
represented by $[r, g(x)]$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{lazy?}}\opLeftPren{}/stream/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Boolean}{LazyStreamAggregate}
{$\mbox*lazy?*\opLeftPren{$s\opRightPren{}} tests
if the first node of the stream $s$ is a lazy 
evaluation mechanism which could produce an additional entry to $s$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{lazyEvaluate}}\opLeftPren{}
/stream/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{LazyStreamAggregate}
{$\mbox*lazyEvaluate*\opLeftPren{$s\opRightPren{}} 
causes one lazy evaluation of stream
$s$.
Caution: $s$ must be a ``lazy node'' satisfying
$\mbox*lazy?*\opLeftPren{$s) = true}, as there is no error check.
A call to this function may or may not produce an explicit first
entry.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{lcm}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it elements\opt{, element}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(\$))->\$}{GcdDomain}
{$\mbox*lcm*\opLeftPren{$x, {} y\opRightPren{}} 
returns the least common multiple of $x$ and \smath{y}.
\newitem
$\mbox*lcm*\opLeftPren{$lx\opRightPren{}} returns the 
least common multiple of the elements of
the list $lx$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{ldexquo}}\opLeftPren{}/lodOperator/,
{}/lodOperator/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->Union(\$, "failed")}{LinearOrdinaryDifferentialOperator}
{$\mbox*ldexquo*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
returns
$q$ such that \smath{a = b*q}, or \mbox="failed"= 
if no such $q$ exists.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftDivide}}\opLeftPren{}
/lodOperator/, {}/lodOperator/\opRightPren{}%
\optand \mbox{\axiomFun{leftQuotient}}\opLeftPren{}
/lodOperator/, {}/lodOperator/\opRightPren{}%
\opand \mbox{\axiomFun{leftRemainder}}\opLeftPren{}
/lodOperator/, {}/lodOperator/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->Record(quotient:\$, remainder:\$)}
{LinearOrdinaryDifferentialOperator}
{$\mbox*leftDivide*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} returns
a record with two fields: ``quotient'' $q$
and ``remainder'' $r$
such that $a = b q + r$ and the degree of \smath{r} is less
than the degree of $b$.
This operation is called ``left division.''
Operation $\mbox*leftQuotient*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} returns $q$, and
$\mbox*leftRemainder*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} returns $r$.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leader}}\opLeftPren{}
/differentialPolynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->V}{DifferentialPolynomialCategory}
{$\mbox*leader*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}} 
returns the derivative of the highest rank
appearing in the differential polynomial $p$, or
calls \spadfun{error} if $p$ is in the ground ring.}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leadingCoefficient}}\opLeftPren{}
/polynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->R}{AbelianMonoidRing}
{$\mbox*leadingCoefficient*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}}

term of polynomial $p$.
See also \spadtype{IndexedDirectProductCategory} and
\spadtype{MonogenicLinearOperator}.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leadingIdeal}}\opLeftPren{}/ideal/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{PolynomialIdeals}
{$\mbox*leadingIdeal*\opLeftPren{$I\opRightPren{}} is the 
ideal generated by the leading terms of the elements of the ideal $I$.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leadingMonomial}}\opLeftPren{}
/polynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{AbelianMonoidRing}
{$\mbox*leadingMonomial*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}} 
returns the monomial of polynomial $p$ with the highest degree.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leaf?}}\opLeftPren{}/aggregate/\opRightPren{}%
\optand \mbox{\axiomFun{leafValues}}\opLeftPren{}/aggregate/\opRightPren{}%
\opand \mbox{\axiomFun{leaves}}\opLeftPren{}/aggregate/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Boolean}{RecursiveAggregate}
{\opkey{These operations apply to a recursive aggregate $a$.
See, for example,
\spadtype{BinaryTree}.}
\newitem$\mbox*leaf?*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}} 
tests if $a$ is a terminal node.
\newitem$\mbox*leaves*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}} 
returns the list of values at the leaf nodes
in left-to-right order.}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{left}}\opLeftPren{}
/binaryRecursiveAggregate/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{BinaryRecursiveAggregate}
{$\mbox*left*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}} 
returns the left child of binary aggregate $a$.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftAlternative?}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->Boolean}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{$\mbox*leftAlternative?*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F},
where $F$ is a domain of \spadtype{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra},
tests if $2*\mbox=associator=(a, a, b) = 0$
for all $a$, \smath{b} in \smath{F}.
Note: in general, you do not know whether $2*a=0$ implies \smath{a=0}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftCharacteristicPolynomial}}
\opLeftPren{}/polynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->SparseUnivariatePolynomial(R)}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{\smath{\mbox*leftCharacteristicPolynomial*
\opLeftPren{}p\opRightPren{}\$F} returns the
characteristic polynomial of the left regular representation of
$p$ of domain \smath{F} with respect to any basis.
Argument $p$ is a member of a domain of category
\spadtype{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra(R)} where $R$ is
a commutative ring.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftDiscriminant}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it \optinit{listOfVectors}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(Vector(\$))->R}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{$\mbox*leftDiscriminant*\opLeftPren{$[v_1, 
{} ..., v_n]\opRightPren{}\$F}
where $F$ is a domain
of category \spadtype{FramedNonAssociativeAlgebra} over a
commutative ring $R$,
returns the determinant
of the $n$-by-\smath{n} matrix whose element at the
\eth{$i$} row and \eth{\smath{j}} column is given by the
left trace of the product
$v_i*v_j$.
Same as \spadfun{determinant}(\smath{\mbox*leftTraceMatrix*
\opLeftPren{}[v_1, {} ..., v_n]\opRightPren{}}).
If no argument is given, $v_1, ..., v_n$ are taken to
elements of the fixed $R$-basis.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftGcd}}\opLeftPren{}/lodOperator/,
{}/lodOperator/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->\$}{LinearOrdinaryDifferentialOperator}
{$\mbox*leftGcd*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
computes the value $g$ of highest degree such that
$a = aa*g$ and \smath{b = bb*g} for some values \smath{aa} and 
$bb$.
The value $g$ is computed using left-division.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftLcm}}\opLeftPren{}/lodOperator/,
{}/lodOperator/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->\$}{LinearOrdinaryDifferentialOperator}
{$\mbox*leftLcm*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
computes the value $m$ of lowest
degree such that $m = a*aa = b*bb$ for some values
$aa$ and \smath{bb}.
The value $m$ is computed using left-division.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftMinimalPolynomial}}\opLeftPren{}
/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->SparseUnivariatePolynomial(R)}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{$\mbox*leftMinimalPolynomial*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}} 
returns the polynomial
determined by the smallest non-trivial linear combination of left
powers of $a$, an element of a domain of category
\spadtype{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}.
Note: the polynomial has no a constant term because, in general, the
algebra has no unit.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftNorm}}\opLeftPren{}/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->R}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{$\mbox*leftNorm*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}} 
returns the determinant of the left regular representation of $a$,
an element of a domain of category \spadtype{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftPower}}\opLeftPren{}
/monad/, {}/nonNegativeInteger/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, NonNegativeInteger)->\$}{MonadWithUnit}
{$\mbox*leftPower*\opLeftPren{$a, {} n
\opRightPren{}} returns the \eth{$n$} left power of monad \smath{a},
that is, $\mbox*leftPower*\opLeftPren{$a, n) := 
a {\mbox*leftPower*}(a, n-1)}.
If the monad has a unit then \smath{\mbox*leftPower*
\opLeftPren{}a, 0) := 1}.
Otherwise, define $\mbox*leftPower*\opLeftPren{$a, 1) = a}
See \spadtype{Monad} and \spadtype{MonadWithUnit} for details.
See also \spadfun{leftRecip}.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftRankPolynomial}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->SparseUnivariatePolynomial(Polynomial(R))}{FramedNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{$\mbox*leftRankPolynomial*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
calculates the left minimal
polynomial of a generic element of an algebra of domain $F$,
a domain of category \spadtype{FramedNonAssociativeAlgebra} over a
commutative ring $R$.
This generic element is an element of the algebra defined by the
same structural constants over the polynomial ring in symbolic
coefficients with respect to the fixed basis.
}

}%
}%
{1}{(A)->NonNegativeInteger}{AlgebraPackage}
{$\mbox*leftRank*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}} 
returns the number of linearly independent
elements in $x b_1$, ..., \smath{x b_n}, where
$b=[b_1, ..., b_n]$ is a basis.
Argument $x$ is an element of a domain of category
\spadtype{FramedNonAssociativeAlgebra} over a commutative ring
$R$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftRegularRepresentation}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it element\opt{, vectorOfElements}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, Vector(\$))->Matrix(R)}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{\opkey{This operation is defined on a domain $F$ of
category \spadtype{NonAssociativeAlgebra}.}
\newline\smath{leftRegularRepresentation(a\optinner{, [v_1,
..., v_n]})} returns the matrix of the linear map defined by
left multiplication by $a$ with respect to the basis
$[v_1, ..., v_n]$.
If a second argument is missing, the basis is taken to be the
fixed basis for $F$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftTraceMatrix}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it \opt{vectorOfElements}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(Vector(\$))->Matrix(R)}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{\opkey{This operation is defined on a domain $F$ 
of category \spadtype{NonAssociativeAlgebra}.}
\newline$\mbox*leftTraceMatrix*\opLeftPren{$
\optinner{v}\opRightPren{}}, where $v$
is an optional vector $[v_1, ..., v_n]$, returns
the $n$-by-\smath{n} matrix \smath{M} such that
$M_{i, j$} is the left
trace of the product $v_i*v_j$ of elements from the
basis $[v_1, ..., v_n]$.
If the argument is missing, the basis is taken to be the 
fixed basis for $F$.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftTrace}}\opLeftPren{}
/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->R}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{$\mbox*leftTrace*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}} returns 
the trace of the left regular representation of $a$,
an element of a domain of category \spadtype{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}.
}

{}/various/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, Character)->\$}{StringAggregate}
{$\mbox*leftTrim*\opLeftPren{$s, {} c\opRightPren{}} 
returns string $s$ with all leading characters
$c$ deleted. For example,
\spadfun{leftTrim}=(" abc ", " ")= returns ="abc "=.
\newitem
$\mbox*leftTrim*\opLeftPren{$s, {} cc\opRightPren{}} 
returns $s$ with all leading characters in
$cc$ deleted. For example, \code{leftTrim("(abc)", charClass "()")}
returns \code{"abc"}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{leftUnit}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{leftUnits}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->Union(Record(particular:\$, basis:List(\$)), "failed")}
{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{\opkey{These operations are defined on a domain $F$ of
category \spadtype{NonAssociativeAlgebra}.}
\newitem$\mbox*leftUnit*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
returns a left unit of the algebra (not
necessarily unique), or \mbox="failed"= if there is none.
\newitem$\mbox*leftUnits*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
returns the affine space of all
left units of an algebra $F$, or \mbox="failed"= if
there is none, where $F$ is a domain of category
\spadtype{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}.
The normal result is returned as a record with selector
$particular$ for an element of \smath{F}, and \smath{basis}
for a list of elements of $F$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{legendreSymbol}}\opLeftPren{}
/integer/, {}/integer/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(Integer, Integer)->Integer}{IntegerNumberTheoryFunctions}
{$\mbox*legendreSymbol*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} p\opRightPren{}} returns the Legendre symbol
$L(a/p)$, \smath{L(a/p) = (-1)^{(p-1)/2} \mod p} for prime
$p$.
This is 0 if $a = 0$, 1 if \smath{a} is a quadratic residue
$\mod p$, and \smath{-1} otherwise.
Note: because the primality test is expensive, use
$\mbox*jacobi*\opLeftPren{$a, {} p\opRightPren{}} 
if you know that $p$ is prime.
}

{}/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(NonNegativeInteger, R)->R}{OrthogonalPolynomialFunctions}
{$\mbox*LegendreP*\opLeftPren{$n, {} x\opRightPren{}} 
is the \eth{$n$} Legendre
polynomial, $P[n](x)$, defined by \smath{{1\over
\sqrt(1-2xt+t^2)} ={ \sum\nolimits_{n=0}^\infty {P[n](x) t^n}}}.
}

}%
}%
{0}{()->\$}{CartesianTensor}
{$\mbox*leviCivitaSymbol*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}} 
is the rank $dim$ tensor defined
by $\mbox*leviCivitaSymbol*\opLeftPren{$)
(i_1, ... i_dim)}, which is
$+1$, \smath{-1} or \smath{0} according to whether the
permutation $i_1, ..., i_dim$ is an even
permutation, an odd permutation, or not a permutation of
$i_0, ..., i_0+dim-1$, respectively, where
$i_0$ is the minimum index.
}

}%
}%
{0}{()->Boolean}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}

}%
}%
{0}{()->Boolean}{FiniteRankNonAssociativeAlgebra}
{$\mbox*lieAlgebra?*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
tests if the algebra of
$F$
is anticommutative and
that the Jacobi identity $(a*b)*c + (b*c)*a + (c*a)*b = 0$
is satisfied for all $a$, \smath{b}, \smath{c} in \smath{F}.
}

/listOfRationalFunctions/\opRightPren{}%
}%

logand:Fraction(Polynomial(F))))), "failed")}
{RationalFunctionIntegration}
{$\mbox*limitedIntegrate*\opLeftPren{$f, {} x, 
{} [g_1, {} ..., g_n]\opRightPren{}} returns
fractions $[h, [c_i, g_i]]$ such

among $[g_1, ..., g_n]$, \smath{dc_i/dx = 0},

}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{linearDependenceOverZ}}\opLeftPren{}

/vector/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(Vector(R))->Union(Vector(Integer), "failed")}{IntegerLinearDependence}
{$\mbox*linearlyDependenceOverZ*\opLeftPren{$
[v_1, {} ..., v_n]\opRightPren{}} tests
if the elements $v_i$ of a ring (typically algebraic numbers or
\spadtype{Expression}s) are linearly dependent over the integers.
If so, the operation returns
$[c_1, ..., c_n]$ such that
$c_1 v_1 + \cdots + c_n v_n = 0$ (for which not all the
$c_i$'s are 0).
If linearly independent over the integers,
\mbox="failed"= is returned.
$\mbox*linearlyDependentOverZ?*\opLeftPren{$[v1, 
{} ..., vn]\opRightPren{}} returns $true$
if the $vi$'s are linearly dependent over the integers, 
and $false$ otherwise.
}

\largerbreak Arguments $f$, \smath{g}, and \smath{h}
appearing below as symbols without arguments denote user-defined
functions which map one or more \spadtype{DoubleFloat} values to
\spadtype{DoubleFloat} values.
\largerbreak Values $a$, \smath{b}, \smath{c}, and \smath{d}
denote numerical values.
\bigitem$\mbox*makeObject*\opLeftPren{$curve(f, g, h), 
{} a..b\opRightPren{}} returns the space
$sp$ of the domain \spadtype{ThreeSpace} with the addition
of the graph of the parametric curve $x = f(t)$, \smath{y =
g(t)}, $z = h(t)$ as \smath{t} ranges from 
$\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}}
to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem$\mbox*makeObject*\opLeftPren{$curve(f(t), g(t), h(t)), 
{} t = a..b\opRightPren{}}
returns the space $sp$ of the domain \spadtype{ThreeSpace}
with the addition of the graph of the parametric curve \smath{x =
f(t)}, $y = g(t)$, \smath{z = h(t)} as \smath{t} ranges from
$\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem$\mbox*makeObject*\opLeftPren{$f, {} a..b, 
{} c..d\opRightPren{}} returns the space
$sp$ of the domain \spadtype{ThreeSpace} with the addition
of the graph of $z = f(x, y)$ as \smath{x} ranges from
$\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
and $y$ ranges from
$\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$c, {} d\opRightPren{}} 
to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$c, {} d\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem$\mbox*makeObject*\opLeftPren{$f(x, y), 
{} x = a..b, {} y = c..d\opRightPren{}} returns
the space $sp$ of the domain \spadtype{ThreeSpace} with the
addition of the graph of $z = f(x, y)$ as \smath{x} ranges
from $\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} and 
$y$ ranges
from $\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$c, {} d\opRightPren{}} 
to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$c, {} d\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem$\mbox*makeObject*\opLeftPren{$surface(f, g, h), 
{} a..b, {} c..d\opRightPren{}} returns
the space $sp$ of the domain \spadtype{ThreeSpace} with the
addition of the graph of the parametric surface \smath{x = f(u,
v)}, $y = g(u, v)$, \smath{z = h(u, v)} as \smath{u} ranges
from $\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
and $v$ ranges
from $\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$c, {} d\opRightPren{}} 
to $\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$c, {} d\opRightPren{}}.
\bigitem \smath{makeObject(surface(f(u, v), g(u, v), h(u, v)), u =
a..b, v = c..d)} returns the space $sp$ of the domain
\spadtype{ThreeSpace} with the addition of the graph of the
parametric surface $x = f(u, v)$, \smath{y = g(u, v)},
$z = h(u, v)$ as \smath{u} ranges from 
$\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} to
$\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
and $v$ ranges from \smath{\mbox*min*\opLeftPren{}c, 
{} d\opRightPren{}} to
$\mbox*max*\opLeftPren{$c, {} d\opRightPren{}}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{map}}\opLeftPren{}/function/, {}
/structure/ $\,[$ , {}
/structure/$]$\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{map!}}\opLeftPren{}/function/, {}
/structure/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{((R)->R, \$)->\$}{AbelianMonoidRing}
{$\mbox*map*\opLeftPren{$fn, {} u\opRightPren{}} 
maps the one-argument function $fn$ onto
the components of a structure, returning a new structure.
Most structures allow $f$ to have different source and
target domains.
Specifically, the function $f$ is mapped onto the following
components of the structure as follows.
If $u$ is: \begin{simpleList} \item a series: the
coefficients of the series.
\item a polynomial: the coefficients of the non-zero monomials.
\item a direct product of elements: the elements.
\item an aggregate, tuple, table, or a matrix: all its elements.
\item an operation of the form $op(a_1, ..., a_n)$: each
$a_i$, returning \smath{op(f(a_1), ..., f(a_n))}.
\item a fraction: the numerator and denominator.
\item complex: the real and imaginary parts.
\item a quaternion or octonion: the real and all imaginary parts.
\item a finite or infinite series or stream: all the coefficients.
\item a factored object: onto all the factors.
\item a segment $a..b$ or a segment binding of the form
$x=a..b$: each of the elements from \smath{a} to \smath{b}.
\item an equation: both sides of the equation.
\end{simpleList} $\mbox*map*\opLeftPren{$fn, 
{} u, {} v\opRightPren{}} maps the two argument
function $fn$ onto the components of a structure, returning
a new structure.
Arguments $u$ and \smath{v} can be matrices, finite
aggregates such as lists, tables, and vectors, and infinite
aggregates such as streams and series.
\bigitem $\mbox*map!*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} u\opRightPren{}}, where $u$ is homogeneous
aggregate, destructively replaces each element $x$ of
$u$ by \smath{f(x)}.
\bigitem see =\spadfun{match=} }

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{mapCoef}}\opLeftPren{}
/function/, {}/freeAbelianMonoid/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{mapGen}}\opLeftPren{}
/function/, {}/freeAbelianMonoid/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{((E)->E, \$)->\$}{FreeAbelianMonoidCategory}
{$\mbox*mapCoeff*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} m\opRightPren{}} maps unary function $f$ onto the
coefficients of a free abelian monoid of the form
$e_1 a_1 +...+ e_n a_n$ returning
$f(e_1) a_1 +...+ f(e_n) a_n$.
\newitem$\mbox*mapGen*\opLeftPren{$fn, 
{} m\opRightPren{}} similarly returns
$e_1 f(a_1) +...+ e_n f(a_n)$.
see =FreeAbelianMonoidCategory=
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{mapDown!}}\opLeftPren{}/tree/,
{}/value/, {}/function/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{((E)->E, \$)->\$}{FreeAbelianMonoidCategory}
{\opkey{These operations make a preorder traversal (node then
left branch
then right branch) of a tree $t$ of type
\spadtype{BalancedBinaryTree(S)}, destructively mapping values of
type $S$ from the root to the leaves of the tree, then
returning the modified tree as value; $p$ is a value of type
$S$.}
\newitem$\mbox*mapDown!*\opLeftPren{$t, 
{} p, {} f\opRightPren{}}, where $f$ is a function
of type \spadsig{(S, S)}{S}, replaces the successive interior
nodes of $t$ as follows.
The root value $x$ is replaced by \smath{q = f(x, p)}.
Then \spadfun{mapDown!} is recursively applied to \smath{(l, q,
f)} and $(r, q, f)$ where \smath{l} and \smath{r} are
respectively the left and right subtrees of $t$.
\newitem$\mbox*mapDown!*\opLeftPren{$t, 
{} p, {} f\opRightPren{}}, where $f$ is a function
of type \spadsig{(S, S, S)}{List S}, is similar.
The root value of $t$ is first replaced by \smath{p}.
Then $f$ is applied to three values: the value at the
current, left, and right node (in that order) to produce a list of
two values \spad{l} and \spad{r}, which are then passed
recursively as the second argument of \spadfun{mapDown!} to
the left and right subtrees.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{mapExponents}}\opLeftPren{}
/function/, {}/polynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{((E)->E, \$)->\$}{FiniteAbelianMonoidRing}
{$\mbox*mapExponents*\opLeftPren{$fn, 
{} u\opRightPren{}} maps function $fn$ onto the
exponents of the non-zero monomials of polynomial $u$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{mapUp!}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it \optinit{tree, }tree, function}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{((E)->E, \$)->\$}{FreeAbelianMonoidCategory}
{\opkey{These operations make an endorder traversal (left branch then
right branch then node) of a tree $t$ of type
\spadtype{BalancedBinaryTree(S)}, destructively mapping values of
type $S$ from the leaves to the root of the tree, then
returning the modified tree as value; $p$ is a value of type
$S$.}
\newitem$\mbox*mapUp!*\opLeftPren{$t, 
{} f\opRightPren{}}, where $f$ has type
\spadsig{(S, S)}{S}, replaces the value at each interior node by
$f(l, r)$, where \smath{l} and \smath{r} are the values at
the immediate left and right nodes.
\newitem$\mbox*mapUp!*\opLeftPren{$t, 
{} t_1, {} f\opRightPren{}} 
makes an endorder traversal of
both $t$ and \smath{t_1} (of identical shape) in parallel.
The value at each successive interior node of $t$ is
replaced by $f(l, r, l_1, r_1)$, where \smath{l} and
$r$ are the values at the immediate left and right nodes of
$t$, and \smath{l_1} and \smath{r_1} are corresponding
values of $t_1$.
}

{$\mbox*match?*\opLeftPren{$s, {} t,

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{match}}\opLeftPren{}/list/, {}
/list/ $\,[$ , {}/option/$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(List(A), List(B))->(A)->B}{ListToMap}
{$\mbox*match*\opLeftPren{$la, 
{} lb\optinner{, u}\opRightPren{}},
where $la$ and \smath{lb} are lists of equal length,
creates a function that can be used by \spadfun{map}.
The target of a source value $x$ in \smath{la} is the
value $y$ with the corresponding index in \smath{lb}.
Optional argument $u$ defines the target for a source
value $a$ which is not in \smath{la}.
If $u$ is a value of the source domain, then \smath{a} is 
replaced by $u$,
which must be a member of $la$.
If $u$ is a value of the target domain, the value returned 
by the map for
$a$ is \smath{u}.
If $u$ is a function \smath{f}, then the value returned is \smath{f(a)}.
If no third argument is given, an error occurs when such a $a$ is found.
}

Duplicates

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{merge}}\opLeftPren{}/various/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{merge!}}\opLeftPren{}/various/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->\$}{ExtensibleLinearAggregate}
{$\mbox*merge*\opLeftPren{$[s1, {} s2, {} 
..., sn]\opRightPren{}} will create a new
\spadtype{ThreeSpace} object that has the components of all the ones in
the list; groupings of components into composites are maintained.
\newitem
$\mbox*merge*\opLeftPren{$s1, {} s2\opRightPren{}} 
will create a new \spadtype{ThreeSpace}
object that
has the components of $s1$ and \smath{s2}; groupings
of components into composites are maintained.
\newitem
$\mbox*merge*\opLeftPren{$\optfirst{p, }a, b\opRightPren{}} 
returns an aggregate $c$ which
merges $a$ and \smath{b}.
The result is produced by examining each element $x$ of \smath{a}
and $y$ of \smath{b} successively.
If $p(x, y)$ is \smath{true}, then \smath{x} is inserted into  the
result.
Otherwise $y$ is inserted.
If $x$ is chosen, the next element  of \smath{a} is examined, and so on.
When all the elements of one aggregate are examined, the remaining elements 
of the other are appended. For example, $\mbox*merge*\opLeftPren{$<, 
{} [1, {} 3], {} [2, {} 7, 
{} 5]\opRightPren{}} returns $[1, 2, 3, 7, 5]$.
By default, function $p$ is \smath{\leq}.
\newitem
$\mbox*merge!*\opLeftPren{$\optfirst{p}, u, v\opRightPren{}} 
destructively merges the elements $u$ and \smath{v} into
$u$ using comparison function \smath{p}.
Function $p$ is \smath{\leq} by default.
}

{\it u\opt{, v, w, x}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{4}{(\$, List(List(List(R))), Boolean, Boolean)->\$}{ThreeSpace}
{\opkey{Argument $sp$ below is a \spadtype{ThreeSpace}
object $sp$.
Argument $lc$ is a list of curves.
Each curve is either a list of points (objects of type
\spadtype{Point}) or else a list of lists of small floats.}
\newitem$\mbox*mesh*\opLeftPren{$lc\opRightPren{}} 
returns a \spadtype{ThreeSpace} object
defined by $lc$.
\newitem$\mbox*mesh*\opLeftPren{$sp\opRightPren{}} 
returns the list of curves contained in
space $sp$.
\newitem$\mbox*mesh*\opLeftPren{$
\optfirst{sp, }, lc, close1, close2\opRightPren{}} adds the
list of curves $lc$ to the \spadtype{ThreeSpace} object
$sp$.
Boolean arguments $close1$ and \smath{close2} tell how the
curves and surface are to be closed.
If $close1$ is \smath{true}, each individual curve will be
closed, that is, the last point of the list will be connected to
the first point.
If $close2$ is \smath{true}, the first and last curves are
regarded as boundaries and are connected.
By default, the argument $sp$ is empty.
}

{} q\optinner{, v}\opRightPren{}} divides the polynomial
$p$ by the monic polynomial \smath{q}, returning the record

exponent $exp$. The variable name must be given by context
(as through a declaration for the result).
\newitem
$\mbox*monomial*\opLeftPren{$c, 
{} [x_1, {} ..., x_k], 
[n_1, ..., n_k]\opRightPren{}} creates a term
$c x_1^{n_1$... x_k^{n_k}}
of a multivariate power series or polynomial
from coefficient $c$, variables \smath{x_j} and exponents
$n_j$.

{} x, {} n\opRightPren{}} creates a term $c x^n$
of a polynomial or series
from a coefficient $c$, variable \smath{x}, and exponent \smath{n}.
\newitem
$\mbox*monomial*\opLeftPren{$c, 
{} [n_1, {} ..., n_k]\opRightPren{}}
creates a \spadtype{CliffordAlgebra} element $c e(n_1), ..., c e(n_k)$
from a coefficient $c$ and basis elements \smath{c(i_j)}
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{new}}\opLeftPren{}{\it \opt{various}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->\$}{ScriptFormulaFormat}
{$\mbox*new*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R} create a new object
of type $R$. When \smath{R} is an aggregate,
$new$ creates an empty object.
Other variations are as follows:
\begin{simpleList}
\item$\mbox*new*\opLeftPren{$s\opRightPren{}}, where s is a symbol,
returns a new symbol whose name starts with \%$s$.
\item$\mbox*new*\opLeftPren{$n, {} x\opRightPren{}} 
returns $\mbox*fill!*\opLeftPren{$new(n), 
{} x\opRightPren{}},
an aggregate of $n$ elements, each with value \smath{x}.
\item$\mbox*new*\opLeftPren{$m, {} n, 
{} r\opRightPren{}\$R} creates an $m$-by-\smath{n} array
or matrix of type $R$ all of whose entries are \smath{r}.
\item$\mbox*new*\opLeftPren{$d, {} pre, 
{} e\opRightPren{}},
where $d$,  smath{pre},  and smath{e} are strings,
constructs the name of a new writable file with $d$
as its directory, $pre$ as a prefix of its name and \smath{e}
as its extension. When $d$ or \smath{e} is the empty string,
a default is used.
The operation calls \spadfun{error} if a new file cannot be
written in the given directory.
\end{simpleList}
}

}%

{SymmetricGroupCombinatoricFunctions}
{$\mbox*nextColeman*\opLeftPren{$alpha, {} beta, 
{} C\opRightPren{}} generates the next
Coleman-matrix of column sums
/alpha/ and row sums /beta/ according to the lexicographical
order from bottom-to-top.
The first Coleman matrix is created using $C = *new*(1, 1, 0)$.
Also, $\mbox*new*\opLeftPren{$1, {} 1, 
{} 0\opRightPren{}} indicates that $C$ is the 
last Coleman matrix.
See \spadtype{SymmetricGroupCombinatoricFunctions} for details.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{nextLatticePermutation}}\opLeftPren{}
/integers/, {}/integers/, {}
/boolean/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{3}{(List(Integer), List(Integer), Boolean)->List(Integer)}
{SymmetricGroupCombinatoricFunctions}
{$\mbox*nextLatticePermutation*\opLeftPren{$lambda, 
{} lattP, {} constructNotFirst\opRightPren{}}
generates the
lattice permutation according to the proper partition 
$lambda$ succeeding
the lattice permutation $lattP$ in lexicographical order as
long as $constructNotFirst$ is \smath{true}.
If $constructNotFirst$ is \smath{false}, the first
lattice permutation is returned. The result $nil$ 
indicates that $lattP$ has no successor.
See \spadtype{SymmetricGroupCombinatoricFunctions} for details.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{nextPartition}}\opLeftPren{}
/vectorOfIntegers/, {}/vectorOfIntegers/, {}
/integer/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{3}{(List(Integer), Vector(Integer), Integer)->
Vector(Integer)}{SymmetricGroupCombinatoricFunctions}
{$\mbox*nextPartition*\opLeftPren{$gamma, 
{} part, {} number\opRightPren{}} 
generates the partition of
$number$ which follows \smath{part} according to the
right-to-left lexicographical order.
The partition has the property that its components do not exceed
the corresponding components of $gamma$.
the first partition is achieved by $part==[]=$.
Also, =[]= indicates that $part$ is the last partition.
See \spadtype{SymmetricGroupCombinatoricFunctions} for details.
}
