% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{norm}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it element\opt{, option}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->R}{ComplexCategory}
{$\mbox*norm*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}} returns:
\begin{simpleList}
\item for complex $x$: 
$\mbox*conjugate*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}}
.
\item for floats: the absolute value.
\item for quaternions or octonions: the sum of the squares of its coefficients.
\item for a domain of category \spadtype{FiniteRankAlgebra}:
the determinant of the regular representation of $x$ with 
respect to any basis.
\end{simpleList}
$\mbox*norm*\opLeftPren{$x\optinner{, p}\opRightPren{}}, 
where $p$ is a
positiveInteger and $x$ is
an element of a domain of category \spadtype{FiniteAlgebraExtensionField}
over ground field $F$,
returns the norm of $x$ with respect to the field of extension
degree $d$ over the ground field of size.
The default value of $p$ is 1.
The operation calls \spadfun{error} if $p$ does not divide
the extension degree of $x$.
Note: $\mbox*norm*\opLeftPren{$x, p) = \prod_{i=0}^{n/p} x^{q^{pi}}}
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{normal?}}\opLeftPren{}/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Boolean}{FiniteAlgebraicExtensionField}
{$\mbox*normal?*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}},
where $a$ is a member of a domain of category
$FiniteAlgebraicExtensionField$ over a field \smath{F},
tests whether the element $a$
is normal over the ground field $F$, that is, if
$a^{q^i$, 0 \leq i \leq *extensionDegree*()-1} is 
an $F$-basis,
where $q = *size*()$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{normalElement}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->\$}{FiniteAlgebraicExtensionField}
{$\mbox*normalElement*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$R},
where $R$ is a domain of category
$FiniteAlgebraicExtensionField$ over a field \smath{F},
returns a element, normal over the ground field $F$,
that is, $a^{q^i$, 0 \leq i < *extensionDegree*()} 
is an $F$-basis,
where $q = *size*()$.
At the first call, the element is computed by
\spadfunFrom{createNormalElement}{FiniteAlgebraicExtensionField}
then cached in a global variable.
On subsequent calls, the element is retrieved by referencing the
global variable.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{order}}\opLeftPren{}/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Integer}{FloatingPointSystem}
{$\mbox*order*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}} returns:
\begin{simpleList}
\item if $p$ is a float: the magnitude of \smath{p}
(Note: $base^{*order*(x)$ \leq |x| < base^{(1 +
*order*(x))}}.)
\item if $p$ is a differential polynomial:
the maximum number of differentiations of a
differential indeterminate among all those appearing in $p$.
\item if $p$ is a differential variable:
the number of differentiations of the differential indeterminate
appearing in $p$.
\item if $p$ is an element of finite field: the order of an
element in the multiplicative group of the field (the function
calls \spadfun{error} if $p$ is 0).
\item if $p$ is a univariate power series:
the degree of the lowest order non-zero term in $f$.
(A call to this operation results
in an infinite loop if $f$ has no non-zero terms.)
\item if $p$ is a \smath{q}-adic integer: the
exponent of the highest power of $q$ dividing \smath{p}
(see \spadtype{PAdicIntegerCategory}).
\item if $p$ is a permutation: the order of a permutation
$p$ as a group element.
\item if $p$ is permutation group: the order of the group.
\end{simpleList}
$\mbox*order*\opLeftPren{$p, {} q\opRightPren{}} 
returns the order of the differential
polynomial $p$ in differential indeterminate \smath{q}.
\newitem
$\mbox*order*\opLeftPren{$p, {} q\opRightPren{}} 
returns the order of multivariate series
$p$
viewed as a series in $q$
(this operation results in an infinite loop if $f$ has
no non-zero terms).
\newitem
$\mbox*order*\opLeftPren{$p, {} q\opRightPren{}} 
returns the largest $n$ such that
$q^n$ divides polynomial \smath{p}, that is, the order of
$p(x)$ at \smath{q(x)=0}.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{pade}}\opLeftPren{}
/integer/, {}/integer/, {}/series/
 $\,[$ , {}/series/$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{3}{(NonNegativeInteger, NonNegativeInteger, 
UnivariateTaylorSeries(R, x, pt))->
Union(Fraction(UnivariatePolynomial(x, R)), "failed")}
{PadeApproximantPackage}
{$\mbox*pade*\opLeftPren{$nd, {} dd, 
{} s \optinner{, ds}\opRightPren{}} computes the quotient of
polynomials (if it exists) with numerator degree at most $nd$
and denominator degree at most $dd$.
If a single univariate Taylor series $s$ is given, the quotient

numerator series of the function and $ds$ is the denominator
series.
}

{$\mbox*parabolicCylindrical*\opLeftPren{$pt\opRightPren{}}

parabolic cylindrical coordinates to Cartesian coordinates: the
function produced will map the point $(u, v, z)$ to \smath{x =
1/2(u^2 - v^2)}, $y = u v$, \smath{z}.
}

}%
}%
{1}{(Point(R))->Point(R)}{CoordinateSystems}
{$\mbox*paraboloidal*\opLeftPren{$pt\opRightPren{}} 
transforms $pt$ from paraboloidal
coordinates to Cartesian coordinates: the function produced will
map the point $(u, v, phi)$ to \smath{x = u v {\bf
cos}(\phi)}, $y = u v *sin*(\phi)$, \smath{z = 1/2 (u^2
,- v^2)}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{paren}}\opLeftPren{}
/expressions/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{ExpressionSpace}
{$\mbox*paren*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}} returns (\smath{f})
unless $f$ is a list \smath{[f_1, ..., f_n]} in
which case it returns $(f_1, ..., f_n)$.
This prevents $f$ or the constituent \smath{f_i}
from being evaluated when operators are applied to it.
For example, \code{log(1)} returns 0, but \code{log(paren 1)}
returns the formal kernel \code{log((1))}.
Also, *atan*/(*paren [*x, 2*]*)/ returns the 
formal kernel *atan*/((x, 2))/.
}

}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{physicalLength}}\opLeftPren{}
/flexibleArray/\opRightPren{}%
\opand \mbox{\axiomFun{physicalLength!}}\opLeftPren{}
/flexibleArray/, {}/positiveInteger/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(Integer)->Stream(List(Integer))}{PartitionsAndPermutations}
{\opkey{These operations apply to a flexible array $a$ and concern the
``physical length'' of $a$, the maximum number of elements that \smath{a}
can hold.
When a destructive operation (such as \spadfun{concat!}) is applied
that increases the number
of elements of $a$ beyond this number, new storage is allocated
(generally to be about 50\% larger than current storage allocation)
and the elements from the old storage are copied over to the new storage area.}

\newitem$\mbox*physicalLength*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}} 
returns the physical length of $a$.
\newitem$\mbox*physicalLength!*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} n\opRightPren{}} causes
new storage to be allocated for the elements
of $a$ with a physical length of \smath{n}. The \spadfun{maxIndex}
elements from the old storage area are copied.
An \spadfun{error} is called if $n$ is less than 
\spadfun{maxIndex}$(a)$.}

/element/, {}/positiveInteger/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, PositiveInteger)->\$}{NonAssociativeAlgebra}
{\opkey{Argument $a$ is a member of a domain of 
category \spadtype{NonAssociativeAlgebra}}
\newitem
$\mbox*plenaryPower*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} n\opRightPren{}} is recursively defined to be
$\mbox*plenaryPower*\opLeftPren{$a, n-1) * 
*plenaryPower*(a, n-1)} for $n>1$ and \smath{a} for \smath{n=1}.
}

}%

{1}{(List(R))->\$}{PointCategory}
{$\mbox*point*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}} returns a 
\spadtype{ThreeSpace} object which is composed of one component, 
the point $p$.
$\mbox*point*\opLeftPren{$l\opRightPren{}} creates a point 
defined by a list $l$.
\newitem
\newitem
$\mbox*point*\opLeftPren{$sp\opRightPren{}} checks to see if 
the \spadtype{ThreeSpace}
object $sp$
is composed of only a single point and, if so, returns the point, or
calls \spadfun{error} if $sp$ has more than one point.
\newitem
$\mbox*point*\opLeftPren{$sp, {} l\opRightPren{}} 
adds a point component defined by a list
$l$ to the \spadtype{ThreeSpace} object \smath{sp}.
\newitem
$\mbox*point*\opLeftPren{$sp, {} i\opRightPren{}} 
adds a point component into a component
list of the \spadtype{ThreeSpace} object $sp$ at the index given 
by $i$.
\newitem
$\mbox*point*\opLeftPren{$sp, {} p\opRightPren{}} 
adds a point component defined by the point $p$
described as a list, to the \spadtype{ThreeSpace} object $sp$.
}

/outputForm/, {}/listOfOutputForms/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{}{}{}
{$\mbox*prefix*\opLeftPren{$o, {} lo\opRightPren{}},
where $o$ is an object of type \spadtype{OutputForm} (normally unexposed)
and $lo$ is a list of objects of type \spadtype{OutputForm},
creates an output form depicting the $n$ary prefix application
of $o$ to a tuple of arguments given by list \smath{lo}.
}

/string/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->Boolean}{StringAggregate}
{$\mbox*prefix?*\opLeftPren{$s, {} t\opRightPren{}} 
tests if the string $s$ is the initial
substring of $t$.}

/listOfIntegers/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->List(Integer)}{RadixExpansion}
{$\mbox*prefixRagits*\opLeftPren{$rx\opRightPren{}} 
returns the non-cyclic part of the
ragits of the fractional part of a radix expansion.
For example, if $x = 3/28 = 0.10 714285 714285 ...$, then
$\mbox*prefixRagits*\opLeftPren{$x)=[1, 0]}.
}

where $o_1$ and \smath{o_2} are objects of type

creates an output form for $o_1$ presubscripted by \smath{o_2}.
}

{} o_2\opRightPren{}},

}

List(PolynomialIdeals(Fraction(Integer),

{IdealDecompositionPackage}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{prime}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it outputForm\opt{, positiveInteger}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{}{}{}
{$\mbox*prime*\opLeftPren{$o\optinner{, n}\opRightPren{}},
where $o$ is an object of type \spadtype{OutputForm} 
(normally unexposed),
creates an output form for $o$ following by \smath{n}
primes (that is, a prime like `` ' '').
By default, $n = 1$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{prime?}}\opLeftPren{}/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Boolean}{UniqueFactorizationDomain}
{$\mbox*prime?*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}} 
tests if $x$ cannot be written as the
product of two non-units, that is, $x$ is an irreducible
element.
Argument $x$ may be an integer, a polynomial, an ideal, or,
in general, any element of a domain of category
\spadtype{UniqueFactorizationDomain}.
}

/element/, {}/integer/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(R, Integer)->\$}{Factored}
{$\mbox*primeFactor*\opLeftPren{$base, 
{} exponent\opRightPren{}} creates a factored object with
a single factor whose $base$ is asserted to be prime (flag =
\mbox="prime"=).
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{primeFrobenius}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it finiteFieldElement\opt{, nonNegativeInteger}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, NonNegativeInteger)->\$}{FieldOfPrimeCharacteristic}
{\opkey{Argument $a$ is a member of a domain of category
\spadtype{FieldOfPrimeCharacteristic(p)}.}
\newitem
$\mbox*primeFrobenius*\opLeftPren{$a\optinner{, s}\opRightPren{}} 
returns $a^{p^s$}.
The default value of $s$ is 1.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{primes}}\opLeftPren{}
/integer/, {}/integer/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(I, I)->List(I)}{IntegerPrimesPackage}
{$\mbox*primes*\opLeftPren{$a, {} b\opRightPren{}} 
returns a list of all primes $p$ with \smath{a \leq p \leq b}.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{primitive?}}\opLeftPren{}
/finiteFieldElement/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->Boolean}{FiniteFieldCategory}
{$\mbox*primitive?*\opLeftPren{$b\opRightPren{}} 
tests whether the element $b$
of a finite field is a generator of the (cyclic) multiplicative group of the
field, that is, is a primitive element.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{primitiveElement}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it expressions\opt{, expression}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(F, F)->Record(primelt:F, pol1:SparseUnivariatePolynomial(F), 
pol2:SparseUnivariatePolynomial(F), prim:SparseUnivariatePolynomial(F))}
{FunctionSpacePrimitiveElement}
{$\mbox*primitiveElement*\opLeftPren{$a_1, 
{} a_2\opRightPren{}} returns a record with four
components: a primitive element $a$ with selector
$primelt$, and three polynomials \smath{q_1}, \smath{q_2},
and $q$ with selectors \smath{pol1}, \smath{pol2}, and
$prim$.
The prime element $a$ is such that the algebraic extension
generated by $a_1$ and \smath{a_2} is the same as that
generated by $a$, \smath{a_i = q_i(a)} and \smath{q(a) = 0}.
The minimal polynomial for $a_2$ may involve \smath{a_1}, but
the minimal polynomial for $a_1$ may not involve \smath{a_2}.
This operations uses \spadfun{resultant}.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{primitiveMonomials}}\opLeftPren{}
/polynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->List(\$)}{PolynomialCategory}
{$\mbox*primitiveMonomials*\opLeftPren{$p\opRightPren{}} 
gives the list of monomials of the
polynomial $p$ with their coefficients removed.
Note: $\mbox*primitiveMonomials*\opLeftPren{$
\sum {a_i X^{(i)}}) = [X^{(1)}, ..., X^{(n)}]}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{primitivePart}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it polynomial\opt{, symbol}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{FiniteAbelianMonoidRing}
{$\mbox*primitivePart*\opLeftPren{$p\optinner{, v}
\opRightPren{}} returns
the unit normalized form of polynomial $p$ divided 
by the \spadfun{content} of $p$ with respect to variable \smath{v}.
If no $v$ is given, the content is removed with respect to all variables.
}


% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{principalIdeal}}\opLeftPren{}
/listOfPolynomials/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(\$))->Record(coef:List(\$), generator:\$)}
{PrincipalIdealDomain}
{$\mbox*principalIdeal*\opLeftPren{$[f_1, 
{} ..., f_n]\opRightPren{}} returns a record whose
``generator'' component is a generator of the ideal generated by
$[f_1, ..., f_n]$ whose ``coef'' component is a list of
coefficients $[c_1, ..., c_n]$ such that
$generator = \sum_i c_i \, f_i$.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{print}}\opLeftPren{}/outputForm/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(OutputForm)->Void}{PrintPackage}
{$\mbox*print*\opLeftPren{$o\opRightPren{}} 
writes the output form $o$ on standard
output using the two-dimensional formatter.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{product}}\opLeftPren{}
/element/, {}/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->\$}{GradedAlgebra}
{$\mbox*product*\opLeftPren{$f(n), 
{} n = a..b\opRightPren{}} returns
$\prod\nolimits_{n=a$^b{f(n)}} as a formal product.
\newitem$\mbox*product*\opLeftPren{$f(n), 
{} n\opRightPren{}} returns the formal product
$P(n)$ verifying \smath{{P(n+1)/P(n)} = f(n)}.
\newitem$\mbox*product*\opLeftPren{$s, 
{} t\opRightPren{}}, where $s$ and \smath{t} are
cartesian tensors, returns the outer product of $s$ and
$t$.
For example, if $r = *product*(s, t)$ for rank 2 tensors
$s$ and \smath{t}, then \smath{r} is a rank 4 tensor given
by $r_{i, j, k, l$ = s_{i, j} t_{k, l}}.
\newitem$\mbox*product*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}}, where $a$ and \smath{b} are
elements of a graded algebra returns the degree-preserving linear
product.
See \spadtype{GradedAlgebra} for details.}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{prolateSpheroidal}}\opLeftPren{}
/smallFloat/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(R)->(Point(R))->Point(R)}{CoordinateSystems}
{$\mbox*prolateSpheroidal*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}} returns a
function to transform prolate spheroidal coordinates to Cartesian coordinates.
This function will map the point
$(\xi, \eta, \phi)$ to
$x = a sinh(\xi) sin(\eta) cos(\phi)$,
$y = a sinh(\xi) sin(\eta) sin(\phi)$,
$z = a cosh(\xi) cos(\eta)$.
}

}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->List(String)}{ScriptFormulaFormat}
{$\mbox*prologue*\opLeftPren{$t\opRightPren{}} 
extracts the prologue section of a
IBM SCRIPT Formula Formatter or TeX{} formatted object $t$.
}

{\it basicOperator\opt{, prop}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->AssociationList(String, None)}{BasicOperator}
{$\mbox*properties*\opLeftPren{$op\opRightPren{}} 
returns the list of all the properties currently attached to $op$.
\newitem
$\mbox*property*\opLeftPren{$op, {} s\opRightPren{}} 
returns the value of property $s$ if
it is attached to $op$, and \mbox="failed"= otherwise.
}


% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{pseudoDivide}}\opLeftPren{}
/polynomial/, {}/polynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->Record(coef:R, quotient:\$, remainder:\$)}
{UnivariatePolynomialCategory}
{$\mbox*pseudoDivide*\opLeftPren{$p, 
{} q\opRightPren{}} returns $(c, q, r)$, when
$p' := p \mbox{ \bf leadingCoefficient$(q)^{deg(p) - {\rm
deg}(q) + 1}= c p} is pseudo right-divided by $q$, that is,
$p' = s q + r$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{pseudoQuotient}}\opLeftPren{}
/polynomial/, {}/polynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->\$}{UnivariatePolynomialCategory}
{$\mbox*pseudoQuotient*\opLeftPren{$p, 
{} q\opRightPren{}} returns $r$, the quotient when
$p' := p leadingCoefficient(q)^{deg p - deg q + 1$}
is pseudo right-divided by $q$, that is,
$p' = s q + r$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{pseudoRemainder}}\opLeftPren{}
/polynomial/, {}/polynomial/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->\$}{UnivariatePolynomialCategory}
{$\mbox*pseudoRemainder*\opLeftPren{$p, 
{} q\opRightPren{}} = $r$, for polynomials
$p$ and \smath{q}, returns the remainder when
$p' := p leadingCoefficient(q)^{deg p - deg q + 1$}
is
pseudo right-divided by $q$, that is, \smath{p' = s q + r}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{puiseux}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it expression\opt{, options}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(FE)->Any}{ExpressionToUnivariatePowerSeries}
{$\mbox*puiseux*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}} 
returns a Puiseux expansion of the expression
$f$.
Note: $f$ should have only one variable; the series will be
expanded in powers of that variable.
Also, if $x$ is a symbol,
$\mbox*puiseux*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}} returns \smath{x} 
as a Puiseux series.
\newitem
$\mbox*puiseux*\opLeftPren{$f, {} x = a\opRightPren{}} 
expands the expression $f$ as a
Puiseux series in powers of $(x - a)$.
\newitem
$\mbox*puiseux*\opLeftPren{$f, {} n\opRightPren{}} 
returns a Puiseux expansion of the expression
$f$.
Note: $f$ should have only one variable; the series will be
expanded in powers of that variable and terms will be computed up
to order at least $n$.
\newitem
$\mbox*puiseux*\opLeftPren{$f, {} x = a, 
{} n\opRightPren{}} expands the expression $f$ as a
Puiseux series in powers of $(x - a)$; terms will be
computed up to order at least $n$.
\newitem
$\mbox*puiseux*\opLeftPren{$n =+->= a(n), 
{} x = a, {} r_0.., {} r\opRightPren{}} 
returns
$\sum\nolimits_{n = r_0, r_0 + r, r_0 + 2 r, ...$ a(n) (x - a)^n}.
\newitem
$\mbox*puiseux*\opLeftPren{$a(n), 
{} n, {} x = a, {} r_0.., 
{} r\opRightPren{}} returns
$\sum\nolimits_{n = r_0, r_0 + r, r_0 + 2 r, ...$ a(n) (x - a)^n}.
\newitem Note: Each of the last two commands have alternate forms
whose third argument is the finite segment $r_0..r_1$
producing a similar series with
a finite number of terms.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{pushdown}}\opLeftPren{}
/polynomial/, {}/symbol/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{pushdterm}}\opLeftPren{}
/monomial/, {}/symbol/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%

{} var\opRightPren{}} pushes all top level
occurences of the variable $var$ into the coefficient domain
for the monomial $monom$.
}

{}/variable/\opRightPren{}%
}%

{MPolyCatRationalFunctionFactorizer}

{} var\opRightPren{}} converts the anonymous univariate
polynomial $upoly$ to a polynomial in \smath{var} over
rational functions.}

/rationalFunction/, {}/variable/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(Fraction(Polynomial(R)), OV)->PRF}{MPolyCatRationalFunctionFactorizer}

{}/variable/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(PRF, OV)->PRF}{MPolyCatRationalFunctionFactorizer}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{radicalOfLeftTraceForm}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->List(A)}{AlgebraPackage}
{$\mbox*radicalOfLeftTraceForm*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F} 
returns the basis for the
null space
of $\mbox*leftTraceMatrix*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}\$F},
where $F$ is a domain of category 
\spadtype{FramedNonAssociativeAlgebra}.
If the algebra is associative, alternative
or a Jordan algebra,
then this space equals the radical (maximal nil ideal) of the algebra.
}

}%
{2}{(F, F)->F}{AlgebraicManipulations}
{$\mbox*ratDenom*\opLeftPren{$f\optinner{, u}\opRightPren{}}
rationalizes the denominators appearing in $f$.
If no second argument is given, then all algebraic quantities
are moved into the numerators.
If the second argument is given as an algebraic kernel
$a$, then \smath{a} is removed from the denominators.
Similarly, if $u$ is a list of algebraic kernels

$a_i$'s from the denominators in \smath{f}.
}

octonion, it tests that all imaginary parts are 0.
\newitem

\newitem

}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{rightDivide}}\opLeftPren{}
/lodOperator/, {}/lodOperator/\opRightPren{}%
\optand \mbox{\axiomFun{rightQuotient}}\opLeftPren{}
/lodOperator/, {}/lodOperator/\opRightPren{}%
\opand \mbox{\axiomFun{rightRemainder}}\opLeftPren{}
/lodOperator/, {}/lodOperator/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->Record(quotient:\$, remainder:\$)}
{LinearOrdinaryDifferentialOperator}
{$\mbox*rightDivide*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} returns the pair $q, r$ such that
$a = qb + r$ and the degree of
$r$ is less than the degree of \smath{b}.
The pair is returned as a record with
fields $quotient$ and \smath{remainder}.
This process is called ``right division''. Also:
$\mbox*rightQuotient*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} returns only $q$.
$\mbox*rightRemainder*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} b\opRightPren{}} returns only $r$.

}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{reduce}}\opLeftPren{}/op/,
{}/aggregate/ $\,[$ , {}/identity/, 
{}/element/$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{((S, S)->S, \$)->S}{Collection}
{$\mbox*reduce*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} u\optinner{, ident, a}\opRightPren{}} reduces the binary
operation $f$ across \smath{u}.
For example, if $u$ is \smath{[x_1, x_2, ..., x_n]} then
$\mbox*reduce*\opLeftPren{$f, {} u\opRightPren{}} 
returns $f(... f(x_1, x_2), ..., x_n)$.
An optional identity element of $f$
provided as a third argument affects the result
if $u$ has less than two elements.
If $u$ is empty, the third argument is
returned if given, and a call to \spadfun{error} occurs
otherwise.
If $u$ has one element and the third argument is
given, the value returned is $f(ident, x_1)$.
Otherwise $x_1$ is returned.
Thus both $\mbox*reduce*\opLeftPren{$+, 
{} u\opRightPren{}} and $\mbox*reduce*\opLeftPren{$+, 
{} u, {} 0\opRightPren{}}
return $\sum\nolimits_{i=1$^n{x_i}}.
Similarly, $\mbox*reduce*\opLeftPren{$*, 
{} u\opRightPren{}} and 
$\mbox*reduce*\opLeftPren{$*, {} u, 
{} 1\opRightPren{}}
return $\prod\nolimits_{i=1$^n{x_i}}.
An optional fourth argument $z$ acts as an
``absorbing element''.
$\mbox*reduce*\opLeftPren{$f, {} u, {} x, 
{} z\opRightPren{}} reduces the binary operation $f$ across 
$u$,
stopping when an ``absorbing element'' $z$ is encountered.
For example $\mbox*reduce*\opLeftPren{$or, {} u, 
{} false, {} true\opRightPren{}} will
stop iterating across $u$ returning
$true$ as soon as an \smath{x_i = true} is found.
Note: if $u$ has one element \smath{x},
$\mbox*reduce*\opLeftPren{$f, {} u\opRightPren{}} 
returns $x$, or calls \spadfun{error} if \smath{u} is empty.
}

/basis/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{reducedContinuedFraction}}\opLeftPren{}
/element/, {}/stream/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%

{} b\opRightPren{}} returns a

That is, the result is the same as
$\mbox*continuedFraction*\opLeftPren{$b_0, {} 
[1, {} 1, {} 1, {} ...], 
[b_1, b_2, b_3, ...]\opRightPren{}}.
}

}

{RealZeroPackageQ}
{$\mbox*refine*\opLeftPren{$pol, {} int,

}%
{2}{((S)->Boolean, \$)->\$}{ExtensibleLinearAggregate}
{\opkey{Argument $u$ is any extensible aggregate such as a list.}
\newitem
$\mbox*remove*\opLeftPren{$pred, {} u\opRightPren{}} 
returns a copy of $u$ removing all elements \smath{x} such that 
$p(x)$ is \smath{true}.
Argument $u$ may be any homogeneous aggregate including
infinite streams.
Note: for lists and streams, \code{remove(p, u) == [x for x in u | not p(x)]}.
\newitem
$\mbox*remove!*\opLeftPren{$pred, {} u\opRightPren{}} 
destructively removes all elements $x$ of \smath{u} such that 
$\mbox*pred*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}} is \smath{true}.
The value of $u$ after all such elements are removed is returned.
\newitem
$\mbox*remove!*\opLeftPren{$x, {} u\opRightPren{}} 
destructively removes all values $x$ from \smath{u}.
\newitem
$\mbox*remove!*\opLeftPren{$k, {} t\opRightPren{}},
where $t$ is a keyed dictionary,
searches the table $t$ for the key \smath{k},
removing and returning the entry if there.
If $t$ has no such key, it returns \mbox="failed"=.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{romberg}}\opLeftPren{}/floatFunction/,
{}/fourFloats/, {}/threeIntegers/
\opRightPren{}%
\optand \mbox{\axiomFun{rombergOpen}}\opLeftPren{}/floatFunction/, 
{}/fourFloats/, {}/twoIntegers/\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{rombergClose}}\opLeftPren{}/floatFunction/, 
{}/fourFloats/, {}/twoIntegers/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{}{}{}
{$\mbox*romberg*\opLeftPren{$fn, {} a, 
{} b, {} epsrel, {} epsabs, 
{} nmin, 
{} nmax, {} nint\opRightPren{}}
uses an adaptive romberg method to numerically integrate function
$fn$ over the closed interval from \smath{a} to \smath{b},
with relative accuracy $epsrel$ and absolute accuracy
$epsabs$;
the refinement levels for the checking of convergence
vary from $nmin$ to \smath{nmax}.
The method is called ``adaptive'' since it requires an additional
parameter $nint$ giving the number of subintervals over which
the integrator independently applies the convergence criteria using
$nmin$ and \smath{nmax}.
This is useful when a large number of points are needed only
in a small fraction of the entire interval.
Parameter $fn$ is a function of type \spadsig{Float}{Float};
$a$, \smath{b}, \smath{epsrel}, and \smath{epsabs} are floats;
$nmin$, \smath{nmax}, and \smath{nint} are integers.
The operation returns a record containing:
=value=, an estimate of the integral;
=error=, an estimate of the error in the computation;
=totalpts=, the total integral number of
function evaluations, and
=success=, a boolean value that is $true$ if
the integral was computed within the user specified error criterion.
See \spadtype{NumericalQuadrature} for details.
\bigitem$\mbox*rombergClosed*\opLeftPren{$fn, 
{} a, {} b, {} epsrel, {} epsabs, 
{} nmin, {} nmax\opRightPren{}}
similarly uses the
Romberg method to numerically integrate function $fn$
over the closed interval $a$ to \smath{b},
but is not adaptive.
\bigitem$\mbox*rombergOpen*\opLeftPren{$fn, 
{} a, {} b, {} epsrel, {} epsabs, 
{} nmin, {} nmax\opRightPren{}} is similar
to \spadfun{rombergClosed}, except that it
integrates function $fn$ over
the open interval from $a$ to \smath{b}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{rubiksGroup}}\opLeftPren{}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{0}{()->PermutationGroup(Integer)}{PermutationGroupExamples}
{$\mbox*rubiksGroup*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}} 
constructs the permutation group representing Rubic's Cube
acting on integers $10i+j$ for
$1 \leq i \leq 6, 1 \leq j \leq 8$.
The faces of Rubik's Cube are labelled: Front, Right, Up, 
Down, Left, Back and numbered from 1 to 6.
The pieces on each face (except the unmoveable center piece) 
are clockwise numbered
from 1 to 8 starting with the piece in the upper left corner.
The moves of the cube are represented as permutations on these pieces,
represented as a two digit integer $ij$ where 
$i$ is the number of the face
and $j$ is the number of the piece on this face.
The remaining ambiguities are resolved by looking at the 6 generators
representing  90-degree turns of the faces.
}

/float/, {}
/float/, {}/integer/, {}
/function/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{}{}{}
{$\mbox*rungaKutta*\opLeftPren{$y, {} n, 
{} a, {} b, {} eps, {} h, 
{} ncalls, {} derivs\opRightPren{}}
uses a $4$--th order Runga-Kutta method to numerically
integrate the ordinary differential equation $dy/dx = f(y, x)$ 
from $x_1$ to \smath{x_2},
where $y$ is an \smath{n}--vector of
$n$ variables.
Initial and final values are provided by solution vector $y$.
The local truncation error is kept within $eps$ by changing
the local step size.
Argument $h$ is a trial step size and
$ncalls$ is the maximum number of single steps the integrator is
allowed to take.
Argument $derivs$
is a
function of type \spadsig{(Vector Float, Vector Float, Float)}{Void},
which computes the right-hand side of the ordinary differential
equation, then replaces the elements of the first argument
by updated elements.
\bigitem$\mbox*rungaKuttaFixed*\opLeftPren{$y, 
{} n, {} x_1, {} x_2, {} ns, 
{} derivs\opRightPren{}} is similar to
\spadfun{rungaKutta} except that it uses $ns$ fixed
steps to integrate the solution vector $y$
from $x_1$ to \smath{x_2}, returning the values
in $y$.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{scan}}\opLeftPren{}/binaryFunction/,
{}/aggregate/, {}/element/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{3}{((S, R)->R, A, R)->B}{FiniteLinearAggregateFunctions2}
{$\mbox*scan*\opLeftPren{$f, {} a, 
{} r\opRightPren{}} successively applies 
$\mbox*reduce*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} x, {} r\opRightPren{}} to
more and more leading sub-aggregates $x$ of aggregrate \smath{a}.
More precisely, if $a$ is \smath{[a1, a2, ...]}, then
$\mbox*scan*\opLeftPren{$f, {} a, 
{} r\opRightPren{}} returns
$[reduce(f, [a1], r), reduce(f, [a1, a2], r), ...]$.
Argument $a$ can be any linear aggregate including streams.
For example, if $a$ is a list or an infinite stream of 
the form $[x_1, x_2, ...]$,
then \code{scan(+, a, 0)} returns a list or stream
of the form $[x_1, x_1 + x_2, ...]$.
}

}%
}%
{1}{(S)->\$}{UniversalSegment}
{$\mbox*segment*\opLeftPren{$i\optinner{, j}\opRightPren{}} returns
the segment $i..j$.
If not qualified by a *by* clause, this notation for
integers $i$ and \smath{j}
denotes the tuple of integers $i$, \smath{i+1}, ..., \smath{j}.
When $j$ is omitted, 
$\mbox*segment*\opLeftPren{$i\opRightPren{}}
denotes the half open segment

For example, $\mbox*segment*\opLeftPren{$x = a..b\opRightPren{}}

$a..b$.
}

Argument $u$ can be any extensible linear aggregate or

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{sequences}}\opLeftPren{}

{}/listOfIntegers/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(List(Integer), List(Integer))->Stream(List(Integer))}
{PartitionsAndPermutations}
{$\mbox*sequences*\opLeftPren{$[l_0, {} l_1, 
{} l_2, {} .., {} l_n]\opRightPren{}} 
is the set of 
all sequences
formed from $l_0$ 0's, \smath{l_1} 1's, \smath{l_2} 2's, ..., 
$l_n$ \smath{n}'s.
\newitem
$\mbox*sequences*\opLeftPren{$l1, {} l2\opRightPren{}} 
is the stream of all sequences that can be composed from
the multiset defined from two lists of integers $l1$ and \smath{l2}.
For example, the pair $([1, 2, 4], [2, 3, 5])$ represents multiset
with 1 $2$, 2 \smath{3}'s, and 4 \smath{5}'s.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{series}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it specifications\opt{, ...}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(Stream(Coef))->\$}{UnivariateTaylorSeriesCategory}
{$\mbox*series*\opLeftPren{$expression\opRightPren{}} 
returns a series expansion of the expression $f$.
Note: $f$ must have only one variable. The series will be 
expanded in powers
of that variable.
\newitem
$\mbox*series*\opLeftPren{$sy\opRightPren{}}, 
where $sy$ is a symbol, returns \smath{sy} as a series.
\newitem
$\mbox*series*\opLeftPren{$st\opRightPren{}},
where $t$ is a stream \smath{[a_0, a_1, a_2, ...]} 
of coefficients $a_i$
from some ring,
creates the Taylor series $a_0 + a_1 x + a_2 x^2 +...$.
Also, if $st$ is a stream of elements of type 
\spadtype{Record(k:NonNegativeInteger, c:R)},
where $k$ denotes an exponent and \smath{c}, 
a non-zero coefficient from some ring $R$,
it creates a stream of non-zero terms.
The terms in $st$ must be ordered by increasing order of exponents.
\newitem
$\mbox*series*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} x = a\optinner{, n}\opRightPren{}} 
expands the expression $f$ as a
series in powers of $(x - a)$ with \smath{n} terms.
If $n$ is missing, the number of terms is governed by
the value set by the system command \spadsyscom{)set streams calculate}.
\newitem
$\mbox*series*\opLeftPren{$f, {} n\opRightPren{}} 
returns a series expansion of the expression
$f$.
Note: $f$ should have only one variable; the series will be
expanded in powers of that variable and terms will be computed up
to order at least $n$.
\newitem
$\mbox*series*\opLeftPren{$i =+->= a(i), 
{} x = a, {} m..\optinner{n, k}\opRightPren{}} 
creates the series
$\sum\nolimits_{i = m..n {\ \tt by \ $ k}{a(i)  (x - a)^i}}.
Here $m$, \smath{n}, and \smath{k} are rational numbers.
Upper-limit $n$ and stepsize \smath{k} are optional and 
have default values
$n = \infty$ and \smath{k = 1}.
\newitem
$\mbox*series*\opLeftPren{$a(i), {} i, 
{} x=a, {} m..\optinner{n, k}\opRightPren{}} returns
$\sum\nolimits_{i = m..n *by* k${a(n) (x - a)^n}}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{seriesSolve}}\opLeftPren{}/eq/,
{}/y/, {}/x/, {}
/c/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(Equation(Expression(R)))->List(Equation(Expression(R)))}
{TransSolvePackage}
{\bigopkey{$eq$ denotes an equation to be solved;
alternatively, an expression $u$ may be given for \smath{eq} 
in which case the equation
$eq$ is defined as \smath{u=0}.
\largerbreak$leq$ denotes a list \smath{[ eq_1... eq_n]} of 
equations; alternatively,
a list of expressions $[ u_1... u_n]$
may be given of $leq$ in which case the equations \smath{eq_i} are
defined by $u_i=0$.
}
\bigitem$\mbox*seriesSolve*\opLeftPren{$eq, {} y, 
{} x=a, {} \optinner{y(a)=}b\opRightPren{}} 
returns a Taylor series solution of
$eq$ around \smath{x=a} with initial condition \smath{y(a)=b}.
Note: $eq$ must be of the form
$f(x, y)y'(x) + g(x, y) = h(x, y)$.
\bigitem$\mbox*seriesSolve*\opLeftPren{$eq, 
{} y, {} x=a, {} 
[ b_0, ..., b_{(n-1)}]\opRightPren{}} returns
a Taylor series solution of $eq$ around 
$x=a$ with initial conditions
$y(a)=b_0$,
$y'(a)=b_1$,
$...$
$y^{(n-1)$(a)=b_{(n-1)}}.
Equation $eq$ must be of the form
$f(x, y, y', ..., y^{(n-1)$)*y^{(n)}(x)+
g(x, y, x', ..., y^{(n-1)}) = h(x, y, y', ..., y^{(n-1)})}.
\bigitem\smath{seriesSolve(leq, [ y_1, ..., y_n], x =
a, [ y_1(a)=b_1, ..., y_n(a)=b_n])} returns a Taylor
series
solution of the equations $eq_i$ around \smath{x = a}
with initial conditions $y_i(a)=b_i$.
Note: each $eq_i$ must be of the form
\smath{f_i(x, y_1, y_2, ..., y_n)y_1'(x) +
g_i(x, y_1, y_2, ..., y_n) = h(x, y_1, y_2, ..., y_n)}.
\bigitem\smath{seriesSolve(leq, [ y_1, ..., y_n], x =
a, [ b_1, ..., b_n])} is equivalent to the same
command with
fourth argument $[ y_1(a)=b_1, ..., y_n(a)=b_n]$.
}

}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{setDifference}}\opLeftPren{}
/list/, {}/list/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, \$)->\$}{List}
{$\mbox*setDifference*\opLeftPren{$l_1,

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{setelt}}\opLeftPren{}
/structure/, {}/index/, {}
/value/ $\,[$ , {}/option/$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{3}{(\$, Dom, Im)->Im}{EltableAggregate}
{$\mbox*setelt*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} x, {} y\opRightPren{}}, also written $u.x := y$,
sets the image of $x$ to be \smath{y} under \smath{u},
regarded as a function mapping values from the domain of $x$ to
the domain of $y$. Specifically, if \smath{u} is:
\begin{simpleList}
\item a list: $u.first := x$ is equivalent to
$\mbox*setfirst!*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} x\opRightPren{}}.
Also,
$u.rest := x$ is equivalent to 
$\mbox*setrest!*\opLeftPren{$u, {} x\opRightPren{}}, and
$u.last := x$ is equivalent to 
$\mbox*setlast!*\opLeftPren{$u, {} x\opRightPren{}}.
\item a linear aggregate,
$u(i..j) := x$ destructively replaces each element in the
segment $u(i..j)$ by \smath{x}. The value \smath{x} is returned.
Note: This function has the same effect as 
\code{for k in i..j repeat u.k := x; x}.
The length of $u$ is unchanged.
\item a recursive aggregate,
$u.value := x$ is equivalent to 
$\mbox*setvalue!*\opLeftPren{$u, {} x\opRightPren{}} and 
sets the value part of node \spad{u} to \spad{x}.
Also, if \spad{u} is a \spadtype{BinaryTreeAggregate},
$u.left := x$ is equivalent to 
$\mbox*setleft!*\opLeftPren{$u, {} x\opRightPren{}} 
and sets the left child
of \spad{u} to \spad{x}. Simiarly,
$u.right := x$ is equivalent to 
$\mbox*setright!*\opLeftPren{$u, {} x\opRightPren{}}.
See also \spadfun{setchildren!}.
\item a table of category TableAggregate(Key, Entry):
u(k) := e is equivalent to $(*insert*([k, e], t); e)$, 
where $k$ is
a key and $e$ is an entry.
\item a library:
$u.k := v$ saves the value \smath{v} in the library \smath{u}, so that
it can later be extracted by $u.k$.
\end{simpleList}
$\mbox*setelt*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} i, {} j, 
{} r\opRightPren{}}, also written, $u(i, j) := r$, sets
the element in the
\eth{$i$} row and \eth{\smath{j}} column of matrix or
two-dimensional array $u$
to $r$.
\newitem
$\mbox*setelt*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} rowList, {} colList, {} r\opRightPren{}},
also written $u([i_1, i_2, ..., i_m], [j_1, j_2, ..., j_n]) := r$,
where $u$ is a matrix or two-dimensional array and
$r$ is another \smath{m} by \smath{n} matrix or array,
destructively alters the matrix $u$:
the $x_{i_k, j_l$} is set to \smath{r(k, l)}.
}

/formattedObject/, {}/listOfStrings/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, List(String))->List(String)}{ScriptFormulaFormat}
{$\mbox*setEpilogue!*\opLeftPren{$t, 
{} strings\opRightPren{}} sets the epilogue section of a

Argument $t$ is either an IBM SCRIPT Formula

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{setfirst!}}\opLeftPren{}
/aggregate/, {}/value/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, S)->S}{UnaryRecursiveAggregate}
{$\mbox*setfirst!*\opLeftPren{$a, 
{} x\opRightPren{}} destructively 
changes the first element of recursive

}%
}%

{RationalFunctionSign}
{$\mbox*sign*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}}, 
where $x$ is an element of an ordered ring,

\end{simpleList}
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{simplify}}\opLeftPren{}
/expression/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(F)->F}{TranscendentalManipulations}
{$\mbox*simplify*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}} 
performs the following simplifications on $f:$
\begin{simpleList}
\item rewrites trigs and hyperbolic trigs in terms of $sin$,
$cos$, \smath{sinh}, \smath{cosh}.
\item rewrites $sin^2$ and \smath{sinh^2} in terms of 
$cos$ and \smath{cosh}.
\item rewrites $e^a e^b$ as \smath{e^{a+b}}.
\end{simpleList}
}

}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{simpson}}\opLeftPren{}/floatFunction/,
{}/fourFloats/, {}/threeIntegers/
\opRightPren{}%
\optand \mbox{\axiomFun{simpsonClosed}}\opLeftPren{}/floatFunction/, 
{}/fourFloats/, {}/twoIntegers/\opRightPren{}%
\opand \mbox{\axiomFun{simpsonOpen}}\opLeftPren{}/floatFunction/, 
{}/fourFloats/, {}/twoIntegers/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{}{}{}
{$\mbox*simpson*\opLeftPren{$fn, {} a, 
{} b, {} epsrel, {} epsabs, 
{} nmin, 
{} nmax, {} nint\opRightPren{}} uses the
adaptive simpson method to numerically integrate function $fn$
over the closed interval from $a$ to \smath{b}, with relative
accuracy $epsrel$ and absolute accuracy \smath{epsabs};
the refinement levels for the checking of convergence
vary from $nmin$ to \smath{nmax}.
The method is called ``adaptive'' since it requires an additional
parameter $nint$ giving the number of subintervals over which
the integrator independently applies the convergence criteria using
$nmin$ and \smath{nmax}.
This is useful when a large number of points are needed only
in a small fraction of the entire interval.
Parameter $fn$ is a function of type \spadsig{Float}{Float};
$a$, \smath{b}, \smath{epsrel}, and \smath{epsabs} are floats;
$nmin$, \smath{nmax}, and \smath{nint} are integers.
The operation returns a record containing:
=value=, an estimate of the integral;
=error=, an estimate of the error in the computation;
=totalpts=, the total integral number of
function evaluations, and
=success=, a boolean value which is $true$ if
the integral was computed within the user specified error criterion.
See \spadtype{NumericalQuadrature} for details.
\bigitem$\mbox*simpsonClosed*\opLeftPren{$fn, 
{} a, {} b, {} epsrel, {} epsabs, 
{} nmin, {} nmax\opRightPren{}} similarly uses
the Simpson method to numerically integrate function $fn$
#+INDEX: Simpson's method
over the closed interval $a$ to \smath{b},
but is not adaptive.
\bigitem$\mbox*simpsonOpen*\opLeftPren{$fn, 
{} a, {} b, {} epsrel, {} epsabs, 
{} nmin, {} nmax\opRightPren{}} is similar
to \spadfun{simpsonClosed}, except that it
integrates function $fn$ over
the open interval from $a$ to \smath{b}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{solve}}\opLeftPren{}/u/, {}
/v/ $\,[$ , {}/w/$]$\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(Equation(Expression(R)))->List(Equation(Expression(R)))}
{TransSolvePackage}
{\bigopkey{$eq$ denotes an equation to be solved; alternatively,
an expression $u$ may be given for \smath{eq} in which case the
equation $eq$ is defined as \smath{u=0}.
\largerbreak$leq$ denotes a list \smath{[ eq_1... eq_n]} of 
equations; alternatively,
a list of expressions $[ u_1... u_n]$
may be given for $leq$ in which case the equations \smath{eq_i} are
defined by $u_i=0$.
\largerbreak$epsilon$ is either a rational number or a float.
}
\bigitem$\mbox*complexSolve*\opLeftPren{$eq, {} 
epsilon\opRightPren{}} finds all the real solutions
to precision $epsilon$
of the univariate equation $eq$ of rational functions with
respect to the unique variable appearing in $eq$.
The complex solutions are either expressed
as rational numbers or floats depending on the type of $epsilon$.
\bigitem$\mbox*complexSolve*\opLeftPren{$[ eq_1... eq_n], 
epsilon\opRightPren{}}
computes the real solutions to precision $epsilon$ of a system of
equations $eq_i$ involving rational functions.
The complex solutions are either expressed
as rational numbers or floats depending on the type of $epsilon$.
\bigitem$\mbox*radicalSolve*\opLeftPren{$eq\optinner{, x}
\opRightPren{}} finds solutions expressed in terms of
radicals of the equation
$eq$ involving rational functions.
Solutions will be found with respect to a \spadtype{Symbol}
given as a second argument to the operation.
This second argument may be omitted when
$eq$ contains a unique symbol.
\bigitem$\mbox*radicalSolve*\opLeftPren{$leq{, lv}\opRightPren{}} 
finds solutions
expressed in terms of radicals of the system
of equations $leq$ involving rational functions.
Solutions are found with respect to a list $lv$ of \spadtype{Symbol}s,
or with respect to all variables appearing in the equations,
if no second argument is given.
\bigitem$\mbox*solve*\opLeftPren{$eq\optinner{, x}\opRightPren{}} 
finds exact symbolic solutions to equation
$eq$ involving either
rational functions or expressions of type \spadtype{Expression(R)}.
Solutions will be found with respect to a \spadtype{Symbol}
given as a second argument to the operation.
The second argument may be omitted when
$eq$ contains a unique symbol.
\bigitem$\mbox*solve*\opLeftPren{$leq{, lv}\opRightPren{}} 
finds exact solutions
to a system of equations $leq$ involving rational functions 
or expressions
of type $\mbox*Expression*\opLeftPren{$R\opRightPren{}}.
Solutions are found with respect to a list of $lv$ of 
\spadtype{Symbol}s,
or with respect to all variables appearing in the equations
if no second argument is given.
\bigitem$\mbox*solve*\opLeftPren{$eq, {} 
epsilon\opRightPren{}} finds all the real solutions
to precision $epsilon$
of the univariate equation $eq$ of rational functions with
respect to the unique variable appearing in $eq$.
The real solutions are either expressed
as rational numbers or floats depending on the type of $epsilon$.
\bigitem$\mbox*solve*\opLeftPren{$[ eq_1... eq_n], 
epsilon\opRightPren{}}
computes the real solutions to precision $epsilon$ of a system of
equations $eq_i$ involving rational functions.
The real solutions are either expressed
as rational numbers or floats depending on the type of $epsilon$.
\bigitem$\mbox*solve*\opLeftPren{$M, 
{} v\opRightPren{}}, where $M$ is a matrix and
$v$ is a \spadtype{Vector} of coefficients, finds a particular
solution of the system $Mx=v$ and a basis of the associated 
homogeneous system
$MX=0$.
\bigitem$\mbox*solve*\opLeftPren{$eq, {} y, 
{} x=a, {} [ y_0... y_m]\opRightPren{}} returns either
the solution of the initial value problem $eq$,
$y(a) = y_0$, \smath{y'(a)=a_1}, \smath{...} or
\mbox="failed"= if no solution can be found.
Note: an error occurs if the equation $eq$ is not a linear
ordinary equation or of the form $dy/dx = f(x, y)$.
\bigitem$\mbox*solve*\opLeftPren{$eq, {} y, 
{} x\opRightPren{}} returns either a solution of the
ordinary diffential equation $eq$ or \mbox="failed"= if no
non-trivial solution can be found. If $eq$ is a linear ordinary
differential equation, a solution is of the form
$[ h, [ b_1, ..., ]]$ where \smath{h}
is a particular solution and $[ b_1, ..., b_m]$ are
linearly independent solutions of the associated homogeneous equation
$f(x, y) = 0$. The value returned is a basis for the solution
of the homogeneous equation which are found (note: this is not
always a full basis).
\bigitem See also
\spadfun{dioSolve},
\spadfun{contractSolve},
\spadfun{polSolve},
\spadfun{seriesSolve},
\spadfun{linSolve}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{solveLinearlyOverQ}}\opLeftPren{}
/vector/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(Vector(R), R)->Union(Vector(Fraction(Integer)), "failed")}
{IntegerLinearDependence}
{$\mbox*solveLinearlyOverQ*\opLeftPren{$[v_1, 
{} ..., v_n], u\opRightPren{}} 
returns $[c_1, ..., c_n]$ such that
$c_1v_1 + \cdots + c_n v_n = u$, or \mbox="failed"= if no such
rational numbers $c_i$ exist.
The elements of the $v_i$ and \smath{u} can
be from any extension ring with an explicit linear
dependence test, for example,
expressions, complex values, polynomials, rational functions, or exact numbers.
See \spadtype{LinearExplicitRingOver}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{solveLinearPolynomialEquation}}\opLeftPren{}
/listOfPolys/, {}/poly/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(List(SparseUnivariatePolynomial(\$)), 
SparseUnivariatePolynomial(\$))->Union(List(SparseUnivariatePolynomial(\$)),
 "failed")}
{PolynomialFactorizationExplicit}
{$\mbox*solveLinearPolynomialEquation*\opLeftPren{$
[f_1, {} ..., f_n], g\opRightPren{}},
where $g$ is a polynomial and the \smath{f_i} 
are polynomials relatively prime to
one another,
returns a list of polynomials $a_i$ such that 
$g/{\prod_i{f_i$} = \sum_i{ai/fi}},
or \mbox="failed"= if no such list of $a_i$'s exists.
}



% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{sort}}\opLeftPren{}{\it
\optinit{predicate, }aggregate}\opRightPren{}%
 \opand \mbox{\axiomFun{sort!}}\opLeftPren{}{\it 
\optinit{predicate, }aggregate}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{((S, S)->Boolean, \$)->\$}{FiniteLinearAggregate}
{$\mbox*sort*\opLeftPren{$\optfirst{p, }a\opRightPren{}} 
returns a copy of
$a$ sorted using total ordering predicate \smath{p}.
\newitem
$\mbox*sort!*\opLeftPren{$\optfirst{p, }u\opRightPren{}} 
returns $u$ destructively changed with its
elements ordered by comparison function $p$.
\newitem
By default, $p$ is the operation \smath{\leq}.
Thus both $\mbox*sort*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} and 
$\mbox*sort!*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} returns \smath{u} with
its elements in ascending order.
\newitem
Also: $\mbox*sort*\opLeftPren{$lp\opRightPren{}} 
sorts a list of permutations /lp/
according to cycle structure, first according to the length of cycles,
second, if $S$ has \spadtype{Finite} or \smath{S} has 
\spadtype{OrderedSet},
according to lexicographical order of entries in cycles of equal length.
}

}%
}%
{1}{(Point(R))->Point(R)}{CoordinateSystems}

transforms point $pt$ from spherical coordinates to
Cartesian coordinates, mapping $(r, \theta, \phi)$ to
$x = r \sin(\phi) \cos(\theta)$, \smath{y = r \sin(\phi)
\sin(\theta)}, $z = r \cos(\phi)$.
}

/binarySearchTree/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, Integer)->\$}{UnaryRecursiveAggregate}
{$\mbox*split*\opLeftPren{$x, {} t\opRightPren{}} 
splits binary search tree $t$ into two components, returning a
record of two components:
$less$, a binary search tree whose components are all

$greater$, a binary search tree with all the rest of the

}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{split!}}\opLeftPren{}/aggregate/,
{}/integer/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(\$, Integer)->\$}{UnaryRecursiveAggregate}
{$\mbox*split!*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} n\opRightPren{}} splits $u$ into two aggregates:
the first consisting of $v$, the first \smath{n}
elements of $u$, and \smath{w} consisting of all the rest.
The value of $w$ is returned.
Thus $v = *first*(u, n)$ and \smath{w := *rest*(u, n)}.
Note: afterwards $\mbox*rest*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} n\opRightPren{}} returns 
$\mbox*empty*\opLeftPren{$\opRightPren{}}.
}

/listOfFractions/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(A)->Record(num:A, den:R)}{CommonDenominator}

where $u$ is a list of fractions
$[q_1, ..., q_n]$, returns \smath{[[p_1, ..., p_n], d]} such that
$q_i = p_i/d$ and \smath{d} is a common denominator 
for the $q_i$'s.
Similarly, the function is defined for a matrix (respectively, a polynomial)
$u$ in which case the \smath{q_i} are the elements of 
(respectively, the coefficients of)
$u$.
}

{2}{(\$, \$)->\$}{SetAggregate}
{$\mbox*symmetricDifference*\opLeftPren{$u, 
{} v\opRightPren{}} returns the set aggregate of
elements $x$ which are members of set aggregate \smath{u} or
set aggregate $v$ but not both.
If $u$ and \smath{v} have no elements in common,
$\mbox*symmetricDifference*\opLeftPren{$u,

/integers/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(List(Integer))->PermutationGroup(Integer)}{PermutationGroupExamples}
{$\mbox*symmetricGroup*\opLeftPren{$n\opRightPren{}} 
constructs the symmetric group $S_n$ acting on the
integers 1, ..., $n$.
The generators are the $n$-cycle \smath{(1, ..., n)} 
and the 2-cycle $(1, 2)$.
\newitem
$\mbox*symmetricGroup*\opLeftPren{$li\opRightPren{}}, 
where $li$ is a list of integers,
constructs the symmetric group acting on the
integers in the list $li$.
The generators are the cycle given by $li$ and
the 2-cycle $(li(1), li(2))$.
Duplicates in the list will be removed.
}

}

{RepresentationPackage1}

{} n\opRightPren{}}, where $la$ is a list
$[a_1, ..., a_k]$ of \smath{m}-by-\smath{m} square
matrices, applies to each matrix $a_i$, the irreducible,

corresponding to the partition $(n, 0, ..., 0)$ of
$n$.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{taylor}}\opLeftPren{}/various/,
{}/../\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->UTS}{UnivariateLaurentSeriesConstructorCategory}
{$\mbox*taylor*\opLeftPren{$u\opRightPren{}} 
converts the Laurent series $u(x)$ to a Taylor series  if possible,
and if not, calls \spadfun{error}.
\newitem
$\mbox*taylor*\opLeftPren{$f\opRightPren{}} 
converts the expression $f$ into a
Taylor expansion of the expression $f$.
Note: $f$ must have only one variable.
\newitem
$\mbox*taylor*\opLeftPren{$sy\opRightPren{}}, 
where $sy$ is a symbol, returns \smath{sy} as a Taylor series.
\newitem
$\mbox*taylor*\opLeftPren{$n +-> a(n), 
{} x = a\opRightPren{}} returns $\sum_{n = 0 ...$
a(n)(x-a)^n)}.
\newitem
$\mbox*taylor*\opLeftPren{$f, 
{} x = a\optinner{, n}\opRightPren{}} 
expands the expression $f$ as a
series in powers of $(x - a)$ with \smath{n} terms.
If $n$ is missing, the number of terms is governed by
the value set by the system command \spadsyscom{)set streams calculate}.
\newitem
$\mbox*taylor*\opLeftPren{$i +-> a(i), 
{} x = a, {} m..\optinner{n, k}\opRightPren{}} creates the
Taylor series
$\sum\nolimits_{i = m..n {\ \tt by\ $ k}{a(i) (x-a)^i}}.
Here $m$, \smath{n} and \smath{k} are integers.
Upper-limit $n$ and stepsize \smath{k} are optional 
and have default values
$n = \infty$ and \smath{k = 1}.
\newitem
$\mbox*taylor*\opLeftPren{$a(i), {} i, 
{} x=a, {} m..\optinner{n, k}\opRightPren{}} returns
$\sum\nolimits_{i = m..n *by* k${a(n) (x - a)^n}}.
}

{$\mbox*taylorIfCan*\opLeftPren{$f(x)\opRightPren{}}

$f(x)$ to a Taylor series if possible, and returns
\mbox="failed"= if this is not possible.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{tensorProduct}}\opLeftPren{}
{\it listOfMatrices\opt{, listOfMatrices}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{2}{(List(Matrix(R)), List(Matrix(R)))->List(Matrix(R))}
{RepresentationPackage1}
{$\mbox*tensorProduct*\opLeftPren{$[a_1, 
{} ..., a_k]\optinner{, [b_1, ..., b_k]}\opRightPren{}}
calculates the list of Kronecker products of the matrices
$a_i$ and \smath{b_i} for
$1 \leq i \leq k$.
If a second argument is missing, the $b_i$ is defined as the 
corresponding $a_i$.
Also, $\mbox*tensorProduct*\opLeftPren{$m\opRightPren{}}, 
where $m$ is a matrix,
is defined as $\mbox*tensorProduct*\opLeftPren{$[m], 
{} [m]\opRightPren{}}.
Note: If each list of matrices corresponds to a group representation
(representation of generators) of one group, then
these matrices correspond to the tensor product of the two representations.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{terms}}\opLeftPren{}/various/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->List(Record(gen:S, exp:E))}{FreeAbelianMonoidCategory}
{$\mbox*terms*\opLeftPren{$s\opRightPren{}} 
returns a stream of the non-zero terms
of series $s$.
Each term is returned as a record with selectors
$k$ and \smath{c}, which correspond to the
exponent and coefficient, respectively.
The terms are ordered by increasing order of exponents.
$\mbox*terms*\opLeftPren{$m\opRightPren{}},
where $m$ is a free abelian monoid of the form
$e_1 a_1 + \cdots + e_n a_n$,
returns $[[a_1, e_1], ..., [a_n, e_n]]$.
See \spadtype{FreeAbelianMonoidCategory}.
}

#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{trace}}\opLeftPren{}
/various/, {}/../\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->R}{SquareMatrixCategory}
{$\mbox*trace*\opLeftPren{$m\opRightPren{}} 
returns the trace of the matrix $m$, that is, the
sum of its diagonal elements.
\newitem$\mbox*trace*\opLeftPren{$a\opRightPren{}} 
returns the trace of the regular
representation of $a$,
an element of an algebra of finite rank.
See \spadtype{FiniteRankAlgebra}.
\newitem$\mbox*trace*\opLeftPren{$a\optinner{, d}\opRightPren{}},
where $a$ is an element of a finite algebraic extension field,
computes the trace of $a$ with respect to the field of
extension degree $d$
over the ground field of size $q$.
This operation calls \spadfun{error} if
$d$ does not divide the extension degree of \smath{a}.
The default value of $d$ is 1.
Note: 
$\mbox*trace*\opLeftPren{$a, d) = \sum_{i=0}^{n/d} a^{q^{d i}}}.
}

matrix
whose $i$, \smath{j} element is  \smath{Tr(v_i  v_j)}.
If no argument is given, the $v_i$ are assumed to be elements
of the fixed basis.
}

{\it matrix\opt{, options}}\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{1}{(\$)->\$}{MatrixCategory}
{$\mbox*transpose*\opLeftPren{$m\opRightPren{}} 
returns the transpose of the matrix $m$.
\newitem
$\mbox*transpose*\opLeftPren{$t\optinner{, i, j}\opRightPren{}} 
exchanges the \eth{$i$}
and \eth{$j$} indices of \smath{t}.
For example, if $r = *transpose*(t, 2, 3)$ for a rank four
tensor $t$, then \smath{r} is the rank four tensor given by

creates an element of \spadtype{Tree} with

in left-to-right order.
\newitem
$\mbox*tree*\opLeftPren{$x\opRightPren{}} is equivalent to

where

}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{trapezoidal}}\opLeftPren{}/floatFunction/,
{}/fourFloats/, {}/threeIntegers/
\opRightPren{}%
\optand \mbox{\axiomFun{trapezoidalClosed}}\opLeftPren{}/floatFunction/, 
{}/fourFloats/, {}/twoIntegers/\opRightPren{}%
\opand \mbox{\axiomFun{trapezoidalOpen}}\opLeftPren{}/floatFunction/, 
{}/fourFloats/, {}/twoIntegers/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{}{}{}
{$\mbox*trapezoidal*\opLeftPren{$fn, {} a, 
{} b, {} epsrel, {} epsabs, 
{} nmin, 
{} nmax, {} nint\opRightPren{}}
uses the adaptive trapezoidal method to numerically integrate
function $fn$ over the closed interval from \smath{a} to
$b$, with relative accuracy \smath{epsrel} and absolute
accuracy $epsabs$, where the refinement levels for the
checking of convergence vary from $nmin$ to \smath{nmax}.
The method is called ``adaptive'' since it requires an additional
parameter $nint$ giving the number of subintervals over
which the integrator independently applies the convergence
criteria using $nmin$ and \smath{nmax}; this is useful when
a large number of points are needed only in a small fraction of
the entire interval.
Parameter $fn$ is a function of type \spadsig{Float}{Float};
$a$, \smath{b}, \smath{epsrel}, and \smath{epsabs} are
floats; $nmin$, \smath{nmax}, and \smath{nint} are integers.
The operation returns a record containing: =value=, an
estimate of the integral; =error=, an estimate of the error in
the computation; =totalpts=, the total integral number of
function evaluations, and =success=, a boolean value that is
$true$ if the integral was computed within the user
specified error criterion.
See \spadtype{NumericalQuadrature} for details.
\bigitem\smath{trapezoidalClosed(fn, a, b, epsrel, epsabs, nmin,
nmax)} similarly uses the trapezoidal method to numerically
#+INDEX: trapezoidal method
integrate function $fn$ over the closed interval \smath{a}
to $b$, but is not adaptive.
\bigitem\smath{trapezoidalOpen(fn, a, b, epsrel, epsabs, nmin,
nmax)} is similar to \spadfun{trapezoidalClosed}, except that
it integrates function $fn$ over the open interval from
$a$ to \smath{b}.
}

defined by

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{unrankImproperPartitions0}}\opLeftPren{}
/integer/, {}/integer/, {}
/integer/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{3}{(Integer, Integer, Integer)->List(Integer)}
{SymmetricGroupCombinatoricFunctions}
{$\mbox*unrankImproperPartitions0*\opLeftPren{$n, {} m, 
{} k\opRightPren{}} computes the
\eth{$k$} improper partition of nonnegative \smath{n} in
$m$ nonnegative parts in reverse lexicographical order.
Example: \smath{ [0, 0, 3] < [0, 1, 2] < [0, 2, 1] < [0, 3, 0] < [1, 0, 2] <
[1, 1, 1] < [1, 2, 0] < [2, 0, 1] < [2, 1, 0] < [3, 0, 0]}.
The operation calls \spadfun{error} if $k$ is negative or
too big.
Note: counting of subtrees is done by
\spadfunFrom{numberOfImproperPartitions}{SymmetricGroupCombinatoricFunctions}.
}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#+LATEX: \opdata{{\mbox{\axiomFun{unrankImproperPartitions1}}\opLeftPren{}
/integer/, {}/integer/, {}
/integer/\opRightPren{}%
}%
}%
{3}{(Integer, Integer, Integer)->List(Integer)}
{SymmetricGroupCombinatoricFunctions}
{$\mbox*unrankImproperPartitions1*\opLeftPren{$n, {} m,
{} k\opRightPren{}} computes the
\eth{$k$} improper partition of nonnegative \smath{n} in at most
$m$ nonnegative parts ordered as follows: first, in reverse
lexicographical order according to their non-zero parts, then
according to their positions (i.e.
lexicographical order using $subSet$: \smath{[3, 0, 0] < [0, 3, 0]
< [0, 0, 3] < [2, 1, 0] < [2, 0, 1] < [0, 2, 1] < [1, 2, 0] < [1, 0, 2] <
[0, 1, 2] < [1, 1, 1]}).
Note: counting of subtrees is done by
\spadfun{numberOfImproperPartitionsInternal}.
}

differential polynomial in the differential indeterminate $s$ alone.
\newitem
$\mbox*weight*\opLeftPren{$op, 
{} n\opRightPren{}} attaches the weight $n$ to \smath{op}.
}

* Programs for Axiom Images
# label: ugAppGraphics

%
This appendix contains the Axiom programs used to generate
the images in the gallery color insert of this book.
All these input files are included
with the Axiom system.
To produce the images
on page 6 of the gallery insert, for example, issue the command:
#+begin_example
)read images6
#+end_example

These images were produced on an IBM RS/6000 model 530 with a
standard color graphics adapter.  The smooth shaded images
were made from X Window System screen dumps.
The remaining images were produced with Axiom-generated
PostScript output.  The images were reproduced from slides made on an Agfa
ChromaScript PostScript interpreter with a Matrix Instruments QCR camera.

** images2.input
# label: ugFimagesTwo

These images illustrate how Newton's method converges when computing the
#+INDEX: Newton iteration
complex cube roots of 2.   Each point in the $(x,y)$-plane represents the
complex number $x + iy,$ which is given as a starting point for Newton's
method.  The poles in these images represent bad starting values.
The flat areas are the regions of convergence to the three roots.

#+begin_example
)read newton                               Read the programs from
)read vectors                              Chapter 10
f := newtonStep(x**3 - 2)                  Create a Newton's iteration
                                            function for $x^3 = 2$
#+end_example

The function $f^n$ computes $n$ steps of Newton's method.

#+begin_example
clipValue := 4                              Clip values with magnitude > 4
drawComplexVectorField(f**3, -3..3, -3..3)  The vector field for $f^3$
drawComplex(f**3, -3..3, -3..3)             The surface for $f^3$
drawComplex(f**4, -3..3, -3..3)             The surface for $f^4$
#+end_example

** images5.input
# label: ugFimagesFive


The parameterization of the Etruscan Venus is due to George Frances.
#+INDEX: Etruscan Venus

#+begin_example
venus(a,r,steps) ==
  surf := (u:DFLOAT, v:DFLOAT): Point DFLOAT +->
    cv := cos(v)
    sv := sin(v)
    cu := cos(u)
    su := sin(u)
    x := r * cos(2*u) * cv + sv * cu
    y := r * sin(2*u) * cv - sv * su
    z := a * cv
    point [x,y,z]
  draw(surf, 0..\%pi, -\%pi..\%pi, var1Steps==steps,
       var2Steps==steps, title == "Etruscan Venus")

venus(5/2, 13/10, 50)                                  The Etruscan Venus
#+end_example

The Figure-8 Klein Bottle
#+INDEX: Klein bottle
parameterization is from
``Differential Geometry and Computer Graphics'' by Thomas Banchoff,
in /Perspectives in Mathematics,/ Anniversary of Oberwolfasch 1984,
Birkh\"{a}user-Verlag, Basel, pp. 43-60.

#+begin_example
klein(x,y) ==
  cx := cos(x)
  cy := cos(y)
  sx := sin(x)
  sy := sin(y)
  sx2 := sin(x/2)
  cx2 := cos(x/2)
  sq2 := sqrt(2.0@DFLOAT)
  point [cx * (cx2 * (sq2 + cy) + (sx2 * sy * cy)), _
         sx * (cx2 * (sq2 + cy) + (sx2 * sy * cy)), _
         -sx2 * (sq2 + cy) + cx2 * sy * cy]

draw(klein, 0..4*\%pi, 0..2*\%pi, var1Steps==50,       Figure-8 Klein bottle
     var2Steps==50,title=="Figure Eight Klein Bottle")
#+end_example

The next two images are examples of generalized tubes.

#+begin_example
)read ntube
rotateBy(p, theta) ==                            Rotate a point $p$ by
  c := cos(theta)                                $\theta$ around the origin
  s := sin(theta)
  point [p.1*c - p.2*s, p.1*s + p.2*c]

bcircle t ==                                     A circle in three-space
  point [3*cos t, 3*sin t, 0]

twist(u, t) ==                                   An ellipse that twists
  theta := 4*t                                   around four times as
  p := point [sin u, cos(u)/2]                   $t$ revolves once
  rotateBy(p, theta)

ntubeDrawOpt(bcircle, twist, 0..2*\%pi, 0..2*\%pi,    Twisted Torus
             var1Steps == 70, var2Steps == 250)

twist2(u, t) ==                                 Create a twisting circle
  theta := t
  p := point [sin u, cos(u)]
  rotateBy(p, theta)

cf(u,v) == sin(21*u)                    Color function with $21$ stripes

ntubeDrawOpt(bcircle, twist2, 0..2*\%pi, 0..2*\%pi,        Striped Torus
  colorFunction == cf, var1Steps == 168,
  var2Steps == 126)
#+end_example
